2026-09-16-bceao-communique-homologation.summary: The BCEAO certified the business APIs of a first group of participants on the regional instant payment platform on 16 September 2026, letting firms send and receive payments, submit bulk settlements and track transactions across the monetary union whatever the other party's provider.

2026-09-16-bceao-liste-api-business-pi-s.summary: The BCEAO's list of September 2026 names 23 participants whose business APIs are certified on the regional instant payment platform: nine in Senegal, seven in Côte d'Ivoire, two in Niger and one each in Benin, Burkina Faso, Guinea-Bissau, Mali and Togo.

2026-09-16-ben-lanation-economie-la-cryp.summary: La Nation explains that no law in Benin bars individuals from holding cryptocurrency, but it is not legal tender in the West African monetary union and no merchant must accept it. Taxes cannot be paid in it directly, and the union's own framework for crypto-assets is still being built.

2026-09-16-ben-lanation-recensements-gen.summary: ECOWAS member states began validating a practical guide for population and housing censuses in Cotonou on 15 September 2026, meant to make West African census data more reliable and comparable across countries.

2026-09-16-bfa-libreinfo-fasosign-lancem.summary: Burkina Faso launched FasoSign, a national electronic signature platform for the public administration, on 15 September 2026. It is already built into the mission-order, mail and cadastre systems, and the government says its keys and certificates are held under state responsibility.

2026-09-16-biometricupdate-international.summary: International Identity Day 2026 turned the emphasis from population coverage to trust, with ID4Africa's executive chairman arguing that identity systems should be judged on whether they are useful, secure and under people's control throughout their lives.

2026-09-16-broadcastmediaafrica-crasa-46.summary: Southern African communications regulators meeting in Mangochi, Malawi, for the 46th executive committee of their association, CRASA, called for more agile and collaborative regulation as AI, satellite services and cross-border platforms reshape the sector. Host regulator MACRA's director-general urged more knowledge sharing and harmonised approaches.

2026-09-16-civ-aip-pnd-2026-2030-sept-pi.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's digital minister presented seven pillars and 40 projects for the digital part of the 2026-2030 development plan, from universal connectivity and interoperable administration to AI, cybersecurity and skills. The target is to raise the digital economy from an estimated 6 to 8% of GDP to 15% by 2030.

2026-09-16-cod-7sur7-rdc-pass-formation-.summary: DR Congo began training the first 50 enrolment agents for its RDC-Pass digital identity platform on 15 September 2026, three months after its launch. The digital economy minister said RDC-Pass is an authentication tool, not a national identity card, and does not replace civil registration.

2026-09-16-connectingafrica-vodacom-keny.summary: Vodacom and Kenya's Treasury both said on 16 September 2026 that they will appeal the High Court ruling that voided the sale of a 15% government stake in Safaricom. The court found the deal lacked meaningful public participation and hid material information, and ordered the stake returned to the state.

2026-09-16-cpv-expressodasilhas-ministro.summary: Cabo Verde's health minister said on 16 September 2026 that sharing clinical records and test results across health facilities would stop patients repeating examinations as they move between islands. He set digitalisation beside new financing sources as Global Fund support declines.

2026-09-16-dgi-mauritanie-teleservices.summary: Mauritania's tax directorate runs an online filing and payment system for businesses and a set of teleservices for all registered taxpayers, covering online returns, the taxpayer's file, payment schedules and a secure channel to the administration.

2026-09-16-dji-adi-ministre-telecommunic.summary: Djibouti's telecoms minister received a Huawei vice-president to discuss cooperation on new-generation infrastructure and services, calling the company a leading partner in the country's ambition to be a regional connectivity hub. No agreement was announced.

2026-09-16-dji-lanation-previsions-meteo.summary: Djibouti's meteorological agency and its disaster risk secretariat held regional workshops in Ali-Sabieh and Tadjourah under the WISER programme, working with local officials, farmers and herders on turning forecasts into early action.

2026-09-16-dpi-map-mali-country-profile.summary: The DPI Map profile for Mali records the NINA identity number but no identity or civil registry act, no regulation for digital ID, no biometric use and no digital authentication function, while noting a national data protection law is in place.

2026-09-16-egy-ahram-mcit-intel-mou-ai-t.summary: Egypt's communications ministry signed a three-year memorandum with Intel on 16 September 2026 to train one million citizens a year in AI online and certify 500 trainers a year, in support of the national AI strategy for 2025-2030.

2026-09-16-egy-youm7-civil-registry-digi.summary: A Youm7 feature describes Egypt's interior ministry moving civil-registry services onto self-service machines that issue civil status documents at any hour, placed beyond registry offices in busy public locations. The piece gives no count of machines or transactions.

2026-09-16-gab-gabonreview-data-center-i.summary: A Chinese government delegation inspected La Poste and Gabon Telecom sites in Libreville on 15 September 2026 as a possible home for an AI data centre serving the public administration. The postal site can host more than 300 servers; the project depends on the Gabon-China partnership being finalised.

2026-09-16-gha-myjoyonline-bog-digital-a.summary: The Bank of Ghana told a digital assets summit on 16 September 2026 that firms should build compliance, transparency and customer asset protection into their operations from the start. The organiser named the virtual assets law passed in December 2025 as the main change since the previous edition.

2026-09-16-gha-myjoyonline-customs-reven.summary: Ghana's revenue authority says customs collections have risen from about US$350 million to as much as US$450 million a month since an AI valuation system was installed at the ports in April 2026. It attributes the rise to more accurate valuation and classification rather than new taxes.

2026-09-16-gha-myjoyonline-household-reg.summary: Ghana's National Household Registry now covers 11.24 million people in 2,906,288 households across all 16 regions, 508,870 of them classed extremely poor. It is the targeting base for the LEAP cash grant, whose ceiling has risen to 450,000 households.

2026-09-16-gimtel-missions.summary: GIMTEL, the Mauritanian interbank card group set up under the central bank, groups ten banks and the postal service to develop card payments, including acceptance of international card networks and a domestic interbank network for payments and withdrawals.

2026-09-16-gnq-seneweb-coupure-facebook-.summary: Facebook and TikTok have been unreachable in Equatorial Guinea without a VPN since 2 September 2026, with internet speeds throttled, AFP reports. The restrictions followed a viral video accusing Vice-President Teodoro Nguema Obiang of corruption; its author was arrested.

2026-09-16-ipr-digital-sovereignty-empty.summary: An Internet Policy Review essay argues that digital sovereignty has come to mean so many conflicting things, from rights protection in the EU to content control in China, that it is empty as a concept, though not without limits.

2026-09-16-itweb-africa-kenya-ica-nation.summary: Kenya's ICT Authority tendered two framework agreements, national backbone links and cross-border and metro links, each for three years extendable by two. Treasury puts the public-sector fibre network at 30,454km against a 100,000km target before the 2027 election.

2026-09-16-itweb-africa-nigeria-governme.summary: An assessment presented to Nigeria's IT development agency found only 47% of about 30 government digital platforms met an accessibility threshold, with failures also on banking and payment platforms. The agency said it has written accessibility into revised website guidelines and is considering national standards.

2026-09-16-itweb-hollard-rejects-hacking.summary: An extortion attack on insurance technology provider MIP Holdings, detected on 14 June 2026, exposed personal data linked to customers of about 45 South African insurers. Hollard said a ransomware group's claim against it traced to that incident, not to its own systems.

2026-09-16-itweb-sa-banks-ai-value-micro.summary: PwC's review of South Africa's six largest banks for the first half of 2026 finds them moving from counting AI use cases to measuring returns, judged on fraud prevention, credit decisions, service speed and cost. Combined headline earnings rose 9.3% to R82.3 billion.

2026-09-16-ken-nation-opposition-irreduc.summary: A Kenyan opposition and civil-society coalition led by former Chief Justice David Maraga set five electoral demands for 2027, including an independent international audit of the voter register and biometrics and mandatory biometric voter identification. It also wants the electoral commission's technology policy, source code and procurement specifications published by 30 September 2026.

2026-09-16-ken-standard-ai-outpaces-regu.summary: The 2026 International AI Safety Report, presented at Daystar University in Kenya, warns that general-purpose AI is advancing faster than regulation. It notes at least 700 million weekly users of leading systems, with adoption below 10% across much of Africa, Asia and Latin America.

2026-09-16-ken-techtrendske-icta-kdeap-n.summary: Kenya's backbone tender will be scored 80% on technical factors and 20% on cost, with winning bidders required to disclose beneficial ownership. Public-sector fibre stood at 30,454km in 2026, up from 22,486km in 2022.

2026-09-16-lbr-fpa-cbl-financial-inclusi.summary: Liberia's draft national financial inclusion and education strategy went through a two-day validation and will be revised. Participants said its success depends on the identity registry, business registration and credit reference systems, and parts will need legislation and budget.

2026-09-16-lbr-fpa-prime-credit-sues-cbl.summary: Prime Credit Reference Bureau is suing the Central Bank of Liberia for US$1,180,953, alleging the bank never supplied or ordered lenders to supply the loan data its November 2025 licence depended on. It says the bank later wrote that it lacked clear authority to license private bureaux; the claims are untested.

2026-09-16-lby-libyaherald-customs-autom.summary: Libya's Customs Authority met foreign contractors on 15 September 2026 to revive automated inspection, container scanning and coastal monitoring contracts signed in earlier years but never completed. The meeting reviewed what had been delivered and what had blocked the rest; no contract values or dates were given.

2026-09-16-mar-assabah-rni-poursuites-im.summary: Morocco's National Rally of Independents said on 16 September 2026 that it will take to court anyone who made or spread doctored images and false content about two of its figures, Fatima Khair and Benaissa Al-Jarrari, during the election campaign.

2026-09-16-mar-hespress-ai-campagne-elec.summary: A New Democrats candidate in Tangier-Assilah for Morocco's 23 September 2026 legislative election has put QR codes on his posters linking to a site where an AI system answers voters' questions from the party programme.

2026-09-16-mdg-lexpressmg-etat-civil-20-.summary: About 20% of Madagascar's population remains outside the civil register, L'Express reports from the National Identity Day launch in Antananarivo. Officials named biometric registration in the communes and simpler procedures at communal offices as priorities.

2026-09-16-mdg-midimadagasikara-cooperat.summary: Madagascar's industrialisation ministry handed biometric cards to the first 124 registered cooperatives in Analamanga on 15 September 2026, under a UNDP-funded census building a verified national database of cooperatives. The census has also begun in Atsinanana and Analanjirofo.

2026-09-16-mdg-midimadagasikara-etat-civ.summary: Madagascar opened a second phase of its Izaho Tokana 2.0 birth-registration drive on National Identity Day, 15 September 2026, with support from the Francophonie organisation's civil status project. The 2025 multiple indicator survey found close to 20% of children under five without a birth certificate, 21% in rural areas against about 12% in towns.

2026-09-16-mesrs-etablissements-enseigne.summary: Mauritania's higher education ministry lists 17 public and 10 private higher education institutions on its site, with 33,049 students and 500 teaching staff.

2026-09-16-moz-mznews-regulamento-segura.summary: Mozambique's Council of Ministers approved a Postal Security Regulation on 15 September 2026, setting controls against theft, fraud and cyber threats to the postal network as e-commerce parcels increase.

2026-09-16-mrt-ami-conseil-ministres-pro.summary: Mauritania's Council of Ministers took a statement on 16 September 2026 proposing a national framework on minors' use of social media, with an access threshold at 16. It would switch off recommendation algorithms, infinite scroll and autoplay for minors by default, ban advertising aimed at them and add a reporting route for children harmed online; no draft text has been published.

2026-09-16-mrt-instant-payment-system-in.summary: Mauritania sought providers for an instant payment system to make financial services interoperable, under the World Bank-financed regional digital integration programme. The call closed on 3 June 2025.

2026-09-16-mrt-internet-society-pulse-co.summary: The Internet Society rates Mauritania's internet resilience at 43%, with 3% of the 1,000 most-visited websites served from local servers or caches against a 50% target. About 46% of the population uses the internet.

2026-09-16-mwi-malawi24-drops-expiry-dat.summary: Malawi's homeland security minister ordered on 16 September 2026 that national identity cards be issued without expiry dates from that day. He gave the order at the launch of the Nzika digital ID wallet, which lets citizens show government credentials on a phone by QR code.

2026-09-16-nam-namibiansun-itransfer-tea.summary: iTransfer, a self-funded Namibian platform launched in January 2026, matches public servants who want to swap postings and has registered 970 teachers across the 14 regions. It does not approve transfers and charges N$200 for three months.

2026-09-16-ner-actuniger-lancement-passe.summary: Niger opened mass enrolment for the Sahel confederation's biometric passport in Niamey on 15 September 2026, with enrolment kits to go to every region and the diaspora. An ordinary passport costs 45,000 FCFA and runs five years, with online pre-enrolment through mobile money services.

2026-09-16-nga-authorityngr-au-pre-elect.summary: An African Union pre-election mission, in Nigeria from 13 to 19 September 2026, asked the electoral commission for details of its readiness for the 2027 elections on voter registration, technology, logistics and funding. The mission described its role as supportive, not supervisory.

2026-09-16-nga-thisday-fg-december-deadl.summary: Nigeria's government set December 2026 as the deadline for 95% national identity number coverage, announced on National Identity Day. Officials put the database at close to 140 million and said physical e-ID cards will be issued before the end of the year.

2026-09-16-nga-thisday-nhrc-accountabili.summary: Nigeria's human rights commission and AccountabilityLab called for coordinated mechanisms so victims of digital rights violations can get justice quickly, at a meeting of agencies, regulators, lawyers, media and technology firms in Abuja.

2026-09-16-nga-thisday-sanusi-telcos-ent.summary: Former central bank governor Sanusi Lamido Sanusi said at the launch of Nigeria's 2026 Access to Financial Services survey that he was wrong to delay telecoms operators' entry into financial services during his tenure. He said concern for depositors after the banking crisis drove the decision and that it slowed financial inclusion.

2026-09-16-sen-seneweb-identite-synapsys.summary: Senegal marked International Identity Day with a first Senegal ID Day in Dakar on 16 September 2026, organised by Synapsys Conseils, the deposit fund's digital subsidiary, where partners presented biometric and digital trust products.

2026-09-16-swz-eswatinipositivenews-come.summary: A COMESA official told the regional AI validation meeting in Eswatini that AI could improve public services, agriculture, health and education across the region if member states invest in the skills, infrastructure and data it needs.

2026-09-16-swz-eswatinipositivenews-nati.summary: Eswatini has hired a consultant to draft a national AI strategy, the ICT minister's representative said at a COMESA regional validation meeting in Ezulwini on 16 September 2026.

2026-09-16-swz-eswatinipositivenews-sadc.summary: Public accounts committees across SADC adopted 32 resolutions in Eswatini on 16 September 2026, committing each to map major digital transformation projects and review at least one digital system for value for money within 12 months. Oversight is to extend to e-government, digital identity, e-procurement and e-payment systems.

2026-09-16-swz-network-blackout-home-aff.summary: A network outage on 16 September 2026 halted all identity card and passport processing at Eswatini's Home Affairs headquarters in Mbabane and at postal counters, with no restoration time given. Pupils needing original ID cards to sit examinations that week were among those turned away.

2026-09-16-swz-times-comesa-regional-ai-.summary: Eswatini is hosting a three-day COMESA meeting, opened on 16 September 2026, to validate a draft study on AI and emerging technologies. It precedes work on a regional AI strategy, model policy guidelines and a model regulatory framework under the World Bank-funded IDEA programme.

2026-09-16-techafricanews-egypt-intel-ai.summary: Under Egypt's agreement with Intel, the training covers basic AI concepts and safe, responsible use, alongside a digital trust programme.

2026-09-16-techafricanews-kenya-digital-.summary: Kenya began the second phase of its Digital Literacy Programme, putting teacher laptops and interactive smartboards into 10,382 public junior schools. In Nairobi all 98 targeted schools had devices and 91 had completed installation and acceptance.

2026-09-16-techafricanews-kenya-icta-fib.summary: Kenya's ICT Authority opened an international tender to extend the national fibre backbone and cross-border and metro links under the World Bank-backed digital economy project, which TechAfricaNews says is financed by US$390 million in World Bank credits.

2026-09-16-techafricanews-kitsoft-smart-.summary: Smart Africa's secretariat signed a memorandum with Kitsoft, a GovTech firm of Ukrainian origin, on digital public infrastructure, e-government and AI, including building public services on low-code tools. No budget or country deployment is named.

2026-09-16-techafricanews-nitda-digital-.summary: Nigeria's IT development agency said it will work with the Centre for Inclusive Development on digital accessibility after the group presented research on barriers facing people with disabilities. The agency tied the work to its target of 70% digital literacy by 2027.

2026-09-16-techafricanews-senegal-cybast.summary: US cybersecurity company Cybastion committed to mobilise about US$300 million for digital projects in Senegal, presented to President Bassirou Diomaye Faye in Washington on 14 September 2026. The money is named for cybersecurity, data centres, technology transfer and capacity building; no instrument or timetable was given.

2026-09-16-techcabal-22-on-sloane-kumii-.summary: Cape Town's 22 On Sloane launched KUMii, an AI platform matching startups and small firms to funders, tenders and mentors, with more than 4,000 already registered. Its lending arm, Sloane Capital, is raising R1 billion, about US$63 million, to finance them.

2026-09-16-techcabal-amodei-pace-the-fro.summary: A TechCabal commentary sets Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei's call to slow the pace of frontier AI against Africa's position, arguing that the continent's AI debate starts from access, compute and skills rather than from racing ahead.

2026-09-16-techcabal-botswana-mukuru-com.summary: TechCabal looks at Mukuru's Visa Companion Card in Botswana, which lets wallet holders pay at merchants without a bank account, in a country where mobile money is widespread but bank accounts reach 58% of adults.

2026-09-16-techcabal-bujeti-ai-agents-fi.summary: Nigerian fintech Bujeti launched four AI agents that process documents, chase unpaid invoices, watch transactions and answer staff finance questions for businesses in Nigeria and Kenya. They go on general release on 30 September 2026; the company says more than 1,000 teams use its platform.

2026-09-16-techcabal-pula-s2e-fsd-africa.summary: FSD Africa, a UK aid-funded agency, is paying the consultancy S2E Africa to find corporate buyers for African startups and help them through deals, with insurtech Pula among the first clients. FSD Africa takes no stake in the acquisitions.

2026-09-16-techtrends-spectrum-allocatio.summary: A TechTrends analysis argues that spectrum allocation is industrial policy in all but name, contrasting Nigeria's 2026 push for more predictable assignment with South Africa's auction delayed for close to a decade by disputes over its rules.

2026-09-16-telecompaper-macra-crasa-sadc.summary: Malawi's regulator head, chairing the Southern African regulators' association CRASA, urged members at its 46th executive committee to replace outdated frameworks with rules that keep pace with technology.

2026-09-16-tgo-siham-farmers-agricultura.summary: Togo handed its SIHAM agricultural information system and five regional kiosks to the national farmers' organisation and regional managers on 15 September 2026. Financed by the World Bank, it sends weather forecasts, prices and input availability to farmers free by SMS in local languages.

2026-09-16-tza-mwananchi-kamera-za-barab.summary: Zanzibar's automated road cameras, which catch speeding, phone use and red-light running, drew criticism in the House of Representatives over the 50 km/h limit, the Sh230,000 fine and the absence of action against government drivers. The deputy works minister said raising the limit would be examined.

2026-09-16-tza-mwananchi-nida-yaondoa-ki.summary: Tanzania's Prime Minister ordered the identity authority on 16 September 2026 to drop the age bar and start registering young children. The authority plans to bring birth certificates, health insurance and the passport onto the national ID, and the home affairs minister put registrations at 27,527,835 with 2,027,103 finished cards uncollected.

2026-09-16-uga-newvision-transitioning-f.summary: Uganda's revenue authority said the taxpayer identification number will be phased out for individuals in favour of the national identification number, with companies using their registration number instead. It said the old system reached only just over 5 million taxpayers and that the change will remove duplicate and ghost records.

2026-09-16-uga-nilepost-digital-hubs-mus.summary: MTN Foundation Uganda and the ICT ministry handed over a second innovation hub at Busitema University, part of a Shs4 billion three-year programme for four university hubs and a refurbished national hub in Kampala. The programme expects to reach more than 20,000 students and community members.

2026-09-16-uga-nilepost-uganda-stronger-.summary: Speakers at the 15th East Africa Information Security Conference in Uganda urged investment in people, information sharing and resilience rather than tools alone. A Uganda Communications Commission director said mobile money, government platforms and health services now depend on secure infrastructure.

2026-09-16-universite-sahel-faculte-info.summary: The Université du Sahel in Mali runs a computing faculty offering professional bachelor's degrees in system and network administration and in database systems built on PostgreSQL.

2026-09-16-wearetech-benin-ruddy-gbaguid.summary: A WeAreTech profile of Beninese engineer Ruddy Gbaguidi, who founded Foniva in 2009, a cloud platform for running call centres that routes calls to available agents and reports performance in real time.

2026-09-16-wearetech-cameroun-zuo-bruno-.summary: A WeAreTech profile of Cameroonian entrepreneur Zuo Bruno, whose firm Zuoix, founded in 2013, offers preventive cybersecurity services to companies and public bodies, from penetration testing to incident management.

2026-09-16-wearetech-kenya-1000-diplomes.summary: Kenya's Public Service Commission opened applications on 15 September 2026 for 1,000 ICT graduates to spend 12 months in schools and sub-county education offices supporting the Digital Literacy Programme. Applications close on 5 October 2026.

2026-09-16-wto-tfa-mauritania-article-7-.summary: Mauritania's commitment under the WTO trade facilitation agreement to allow electronic payment of border duties was due by 31 December 2024; it has asked for 31 December 2027, saying it still needs a partner to help, and the request is not yet approved. The work includes linking the customs system, the Treasury and banks.

2026-09-16-xaf-afdb-kaist-letter-of-inte.summary: The African Development Bank and Korea's KAIST signed a three-year letter of intent in Seoul on 9 September 2026 covering joint research on AI policy and datasets, advice on digital transformation and training for African officials and researchers. No funding figure is attached.

2026-09-16-xaf-afdb-kexim-five-year-cofi.summary: The African Development Bank and the Export-Import Bank of Korea signed a five-year co-financing memorandum in Seoul on 9 September 2026, replacing a 2005 framework. It targets projects in AI, digital infrastructure, critical minerals, energy and transport; no amount is given.

2026-09-16-xaf-afdb-koafec-joint-declara.summary: Korea, 45 African countries and the African Development Bank adopted a joint declaration and a 2027-2028 action plan in Seoul on 9 September 2026 centred on AI, digital infrastructure and skills. The plan names thirteen initiatives, among them a regional data embassy in Sierra Leone and compute credits for African AI start-ups; no sums are attached.

2026-09-16-xaf-afdb-korea-nia-letter-of-.summary: The African Development Bank and Korea's National Information Society Agency signed a three-year letter of intent in Seoul on 9 September 2026 on data governance, AI-ready datasets and digital public infrastructure. The agency provides expertise and the bank identifies priorities and financing.

2026-09-16-xaf-chinadaily-africa-seeks-a.summary: African health officials told China Daily that AI and connected health systems could detect outbreaks earlier and speed emergency response. An Africa CDC adviser described digital transformation as health security infrastructure rather than an IT agenda.

2026-09-16-xaf-cnbcafrica-gates-africa-n.summary: Bill Gates said the Gates Foundation is working with AI companies to collect and publish data for African languages spoken by at least a million people. He tied the foundation's commitment of more than US$1 billion to AI projects to governments first improving health, agriculture and education data.

2026-09-16-xea-thestar-rects-multi-vendo.summary: Importers, exporters and logistics firms welcomed the Kenya Revenue Authority's decision to open the regional electronic cargo tracking system to private seal vendors. The Shippers Council of Eastern Africa expects competition to end seal shortages that have delayed transit cargo at Mombasa.

2026-09-16-zaf-timeslive-absa-collaborat.summary: Absa's compliance and governance heads urged South African banks, fintechs and telecoms operators to share fraud and mule-account intelligence, saying criminals now operate like organised businesses using AI. Absa's IT costs rose 7% to R8.78 billion in the six months to June 2026.

2026-09-16-zmb-efficacynews-liquid-zambi.summary: Liquid Intelligent Technologies Zambia cut its entry home fibre package to K300 a month for up to 6 Mbps and raised speeds on its other plans at unchanged prices. The company puts Zambian internet penetration at 33% without giving a source.

2026-09-17-aacb-cbe-egypt-ai-central-ban.summary: A high-level conference on artificial intelligence in central banking ran on the sidelines of the Association of African Central Banks' 48th annual meetings in Nairobi, covering AI in monetary policy and financial stability, in supervision and financial integrity, and in governance and risk management, with national readiness and regional cooperation on frameworks for responsible use.

2026-09-17-afdb-korea-ai-hub-letter-of-i.summary: The African Development Bank and the Republic of Korea signed a letter of intent in Seoul to establish a joint hub for artificial intelligence, to support responsible development, adoption and financing of AI across the continent. It was signed on the sidelines of the eighth Korea-Africa ministerial conference; no capitalisation, host or start date is published.

2026-09-17-bfa-lefaso-lefaso-digital-202.summary: Burkina Faso's national digital event returns for a second edition from 17 to 24 October, wholly online and with Rwanda as guest of honour. Its innovation competition had taken 95 entries by 16 September.

2026-09-17-bfa-sidwaya-ia-usage-responsa.summary: A state daily's editorial reads the US-China contest over semiconductors, models and digital infrastructure as a geopolitical rather than purely technological rivalry, and argues for verifying what AI systems produce, building an AI culture and protecting data.

2026-09-17-civ-abidjannet-qualite-donnee.summary: Consultative meetings on the quality of Cote d'Ivoire's credit bureau data carried a dated diagnostic from the meeting's own terms of reference: 67.88 per cent of contracts not updated against a union average of 46.20 per cent on data as at 10 June 2026, at 77.64 per cent in banking, 56.59 among decentralised financial systems and 28.77 for financial institutions. The country holds 40.96 per cent of the union's active contracts and accounts for 60.17 per cent of its non-updated ones.

2026-09-17-civ-fratmat-bic-qualite-donne.summary: Cote d'Ivoire's finance ministry opened consultative meetings on the quality and completeness of the credit bureau's data, naming late transmission by banks, decentralised financial systems and large billers as the defect degrading credit reports. The ministry put non-updated contracts at 67.88 per cent against a union average of 46.20; the bureau's own operator gave about 45 per cent against a regional 30, undated and spoken.

2026-09-17-civ-ivoirematin-data-center-i.summary: A data centre has been installed at the Institut national polytechnique Felix Houphouet-Boigny in Yamoussoukro to support Cote d'Ivoire's electronic administration. It is presented as strengthening national capacity to store, process and secure the public administration's data.

2026-09-17-cmr-techafricanews-trb-operat.summary: Cameroon's telecommunications regulator gave operators until 30 September 2026 to file identification forms for a public directory that is to separate licensed and compliant providers from unlicensed ones. Nothing is yet published and no publication date for the directory itself is stated.

2026-09-17-cod-actualitecd-seguce-guice-.summary: The concessionaire running DR Congo's integrated foreign-trade single window took it to Mbuji-Mayi in Kasai Oriental, presenting its services to provincial authorities, the administrations concerned and local traders and hearing their concerns. Its director general framed provincial establishment as territorial equity, the window being a national instrument.

2026-09-17-cod-forumdesas-kinshasa-quali.summary: Internet subscribers in Kinshasa report slow speeds, frequent interruptions and difficulty reaching online services across all four mobile operators, against the packages they pay for. The regulator is being called on to act.

2026-09-17-com-alwatwan-comores-russie-c.summary: A Russian embassy delegation visiting the Comoros took up with the telecommunications minister the information-security memorandum the two governments had already initialled, covering professional training, skills-building and action against cybercrime. The Comorian side proposed a further document on training Comorian trainers; the same visit prepared the opening of a Russian embassy in Moroni.

2026-09-17-cpv-expressodasilhas-justica-.summary: A second evaluation of Cabo Verde's justice information system reports 46,000 criminal case files handled digitally across all 17 comarcas and an estimated 2.3 million sheets of paper saved over the 2025/2026 judicial year. It records 95.5 per cent of respondents using the system daily or several times a week, 401 professionals holding qualified digital signatures and 110 judges, prosecutors and court officers trained in artificial intelligence, with civil-process pilots awaiting authorisation.

2026-09-17-dji-adi-telecom-ai-training-e.summary: Djibouti's state operator certified 35 of its engineers in artificial intelligence at a ceremony presided over by the communications minister, who cited the national AI readiness assessment run on UNESCO's methodology: it credits engaged digital transformation, strategic infrastructure and a nascent academic base while finding room to improve on skills, governance and research. He called for closer ties between the operator, the university and research centres.

2026-09-17-dji-lanation-ai-ethics-forum-.summary: Djibouti's minister delegate for the digital economy and innovation took part in UNESCO's fourth global forum on the ethics of artificial intelligence in Riyadh, its first Arab edition, arguing for ethical and responsible AI.

2026-09-17-ecowas-ai-election-framework-.summary: The communique of a youth democracy conference in Dakar urged ECOWAS to finalise and operationalise a regional framework for the use of artificial intelligence by election management bodies, citing deepfakes and disinformation as risks to electoral integrity. It also asks member states to invest in digital civic education and the bloc to use diplomatic channels against internet and social-media restrictions during elections, and endorses a youth election-observers network anchored to ECOWAS.

2026-09-17-ecowas-enbic-biometric-card-r.summary: Officials said at a Lagos workshop that seven ECOWAS member states — Senegal, Guinea-Bissau, Ghana, Benin, The Gambia, Sierra Leone and Nigeria — have deployed the regional biometric identity card, which is intended to replace the handwritten regional travel certificate. The chip carries the issuing authority's digital signature over the stored identity data, so any alteration breaks the trust chain at border authentication; member states committed in April to work towards mutual acceptance at borders by December.

2026-09-17-egy-techafricanews-nti-jupite.summary: Egypt's national telecommunication institute, the communications ministry's capacity-building body, signed a protocol with a private firm to design and deliver training jointly for work in enterprise resource management systems, IT systems management and technical infrastructure, combining instruction with applied projects and workshops. No cohort size, duration or cost is published.

2026-09-17-egy-youm7-child-protection-so.summary: Egypt's media council and telecom regulator issued a joint decision obliging platforms to protect children under 15: no independent accounts for under-13s, an automatic and undisableable safe mode for those aged 13 to under 15, and age verification that resists circumvention while minimising the data collected for it. Platforms must review existing accounts that appear to belong to under-15s, offer a route to correct an age, and comply within three months.

2026-09-17-eu-commission-kids-act-propos.summary: The European Commission proposed a KIDS Act introducing age-based access to social media across the European Union, barring under-13s from social media services while leaving child-friendly video-sharing available. It would apply to online services used by minors, including video-sharing platforms, online games and artificial-intelligence companions and chatbots.

2026-09-17-gab-gabonreview-snedai-digita.summary: Gabon's housing and cadastre ministry signed a protocol of agreement with an Ivorian group on digitalising land and cadastral procedures, and the group presented its offer to the vice-presidents of the Republic and of the government two days later. The group frames the work as better mapping and parcel identification feeding a more structured land database, fewer disputes and a wider tax base; no contract, sum or delivery date is published.

2026-09-17-gha-myjoyonline-nca-5g-spectr.summary: Ghana's regulator awarded the second operator all three of the 2.3 GHz lots it applied for, of five made available, a week after the dominant operator took both 700 MHz lots. No licence fee or assignment date is reported.

2026-09-17-issafrica-papss-cemac-aml-con.summary: An analysis sets the pan-African settlement rail against Central Africa's exchange and anti-money-laundering rules: the rail settles in seconds where the rules expect documentary checks before a transfer, and fewer than 13 per cent of adults in the zone hold an account. The supervisory model and the instrument are not on the same clock.

2026-09-17-itu-building-trust-next-gener.summary: The ITU and the World Bank set out the trust problem created by artificial-intelligence agents acting for people in public services: a registry, licensing authority or lender needs to know whether an agent is genuinely authorised by the applicant. They argue identity and authorisation infrastructure has to be built for agents, not only for people.

2026-09-17-itweb-africa-cameroon-telecom.summary: Cameroon's Telecommunications Regulatory Board is compiling a public directory of licensed operators and has told every operator to complete an identification form on its website. The board says the directory will let consumers verify which companies are licensed, expose fraudulent operators and help agencies identify legitimate players.

2026-09-17-itweb-africa-intelogix-ai-hub.summary: InteLogix opened an artificial-intelligence delivery hub in Cairo, inaugurated by Egypt's Information Technology Industry Development Agency. The company says it plans to grow the site from about 135 employees to 1,365 over three years.

2026-09-17-itweb-africa-momo-fnb-zambia-.summary: MTN MoMo and FNB launched a service in Zambia letting mobile-money customers withdraw from their wallets at the bank's ATMs without a card or an account at that bank. It extends a partnership that already carried transfers between wallets and bank accounts and wallet payments at the bank's terminals.

2026-09-17-itweb-africa-sierra-leone-ai-.summary: Sierra Leone launched a national artificial-intelligence and deepfake awareness campaign in Freetown, planned in two phases across all 16 districts. It is led by the Directorate of Science, Technology and Innovation with the communications and information ministries, and funded through the World Bank's digital transformation project.

2026-09-17-itweb-co-za-fpb-online-conten.summary: South Africa's Film and Publication Board imposed R16.175 million in fines on distributors found non-compliant with the Films and Publications Act, most of the content distributed online. The board says its enforcement reaches distributors based abroad.

2026-09-17-itweb-co-za-inforeg-ai-regula.summary: South Africa's Information Regulator says artificial intelligence, automated decision-making and biometric systems have produced compliance questions its founding laws did not anticipate, naming consent, retention, transparency and the absence of a national artificial-intelligence policy. Its chairperson said the regulator is not convinced privacy by default or personal information impact assessments are being practised.

2026-09-17-itweb-co-za-third-party-breac.summary: Four South African financial and telecommunications names disclosed customer-data exposure that began at third-party suppliers rather than in their own systems, and a separate supplier breach is said to have compromised information held for about 45 insurers. One financial services group suspended data sharing with its screening supplier and reinstated the service only after forensic sign-off and credential replacement.

2026-09-17-ken-kbc-kiarie-parliamentary-.summary: The chairman of Kenya's parliamentary communications, information and innovation committee called for stronger parliamentary oversight as the country accelerates artificial-intelligence adoption, arguing innovation must come with accountability, human-rights protection and safeguards for citizens.

2026-09-17-ken-standard-nyakera-parallel.summary: A party official called for a parallel tallying system at the 2027 general election to check results transmitted through the official electoral system, saying interference during transmission is to be expected.

2026-09-17-ken-tech-ish-papss-growth-pes.summary: Payments across the pan-African settlement network are reported to have grown about tenfold over the year while the average payment fell to about a fifth of its level a year earlier — many small transfers in place of a few large ones. Kenya's national switch is the first of its kind piloted for termination on the network.

2026-09-17-lso-publiceye-census-lgbtiq-n.summary: Lesotho's 2026 census asked questions recognising gender identity and sexuality for the first time, after the statistics bureau brought an advocacy organisation into the first consultation. The round had a reference night of 11 April, employed more than 8,000 temporary field staff and has finished enumeration with mop-up still running in Maseru; advocates welcomed the inclusion while warning that the answers need explicit privacy and confidentiality safeguards.

2026-09-17-mar-al3omk-beni-mellal-coupur.summary: Residents of thirteen douars in the Ben Cherro area of Morocco's Beni Mellal province say phone service cuts out nightly from about 8pm until morning, with internet throughput degraded over the same hours. They describe the consequences as sharpest in emergencies.

2026-09-17-mdg-lexpressmg-cybercriminali.summary: Madagascar's cybercrime bill was left off the agenda of the extraordinary session that opened on 17 September, which lists seventeen bills over twelve days; the companion bill on electronic communications and digital infrastructure is absent too. Both had their votes deferred to a later session in the closing hours of the previous extraordinary session, and an extraordinary session's agenda is set by presidential decree.

2026-09-17-mdg-midimadagasikara-etat-civ.summary: Madagascar's National Identity Day, institutionalised by a 2024 decree, carried a high-level conference of more than 150 people preparing the 2027-2036 civil-registration decade. Phase II of the biometric enrolment operation was launched on the second day under the World Bank's digital connectivity project, with no target or coverage figure given for it.

2026-09-17-mediaguinee-armp-base-donnees.summary: Guinea's procurement regulator opened an operation to build and clean up a database of the officials who run public procurement and public-private partnerships, reaching contract officers, procurement-unit assistants, control-directorate controllers, PPP experts and section heads across ministries, public establishments, state companies, local authorities and donor-financed programmes. It is framed as part of the dematerialisation of public purchasing.

2026-09-17-moz-clubofmozambique-tmcel-mo.summary: Documentation prepared for the strategic partner the Mozambican government intends to bring into the state operator puts it at 1.79 million active mobile customers at the end of 2025, up 62.1 per cent on the year, on 1,303 sites and about 6,500 km of backbone with 4,500 km of access fibre. Fixed lines fell 20 per cent to 15,537; the figures are the seller's rather than a regulator's.

2026-09-17-moz-integritymagazine-ai-educ.summary: Mozambique's education ministry says its law regulating the use of artificial intelligence in education is almost ready and will reach the Council of Ministers before the end of 2026, covering every institution from primary schooling to higher education with all of them consulted. The text is still being drafted and is not published.

2026-09-17-mwi-digital-gap-nzika-id-roll.summary: Malawi's ICT minister put smartphone ownership at 33 per cent and basic internet skills at 12.5 per cent, saying the gaps could hinder adoption of the digital identity wallet launched the same week in Lilongwe. He called for collaboration between the private sector, civil society and academia to close them.

2026-09-17-mwi-heslgb-biometric-verifica.summary: Malawi's higher education loans and grants board has moved loan-contract bonding onto a paperless process in which students present the national identity card and scan fingerprints on a device linked to the registration bureau's database, which matches the details before bonding completes. The board's stated reason is cost; the 2026/2027 exercise began on 7 September and has so far covered campuses of three universities.

2026-09-17-nam-universities-local-techno.summary: An academic argues that Namibian universities, researchers and agencies should build local expertise in satellite data, crop monitoring and digital mapping to reduce long-term dependence on foreign providers, and that procurement should be judged on skills, ownership, data access and dependence rather than on cost and performance alone.

2026-09-17-nga-broadband-electoral-proce.summary: At a Lagos e-government summit on election management, speakers pressed for stronger broadband and connectivity before the 2027 general elections, naming the absence of last-mile broadband at polling units as the constraint rather than the technology itself. The data-protection commission's representative spoke to securing the electoral commission's voter data.

2026-09-17-nga-ncc-active-internet-subsc.summary: Nigeria recorded 157,706,496 active data subscriptions and 1,662,021.45 terabytes of data usage in July 2026 on the regulator's own series — twelve consecutive months of growth from 140,328,196 subscriptions and 1,152,347.24 TB in August 2025, with a dip in June before recovery. The operators' association attributed the growth to stable regulatory policy and to a federal zero-rated educational access programme.

2026-09-17-reuters-us-china-experts-nucl.summary: American and Chinese security experts have proposed nuclear-style safeguards against artificial-intelligence risks, including red lines around nuclear command systems, keeping military decisions in human hands, and an incident hotline between the two governments. The recommendations precede planned bilateral talks on artificial intelligence.

2026-09-17-rwa-china-ai-model-template-r.summary: At the launch of a Chinese enterprises' corporate responsibility report and a workshop's first AI class in Kigali, a Huawei architect set out a three-tier model of sovereign AI for Rwanda, arguing that a country must build a base model locally, on its own data and by its own engineers, before industry models and citizen-facing applications follow. The Chinese ambassador said Chinese enterprises are expected to comply with the laws of both states.

2026-09-17-rwa-gsma-digital-reforms-one-.summary: A GSMA report projects that more than a million additional people in Rwanda could be using mobile internet by 2031 if smartphones are made more affordable and digital services more relevant to everyday life. It names lower-income and rural households as the group the reforms would reach.

2026-09-17-rwa-newtimes-decentralisation.summary: A civil-society organisation called for stronger powers at cell level and more decentralised services, putting 44 per cent of 522 public services as decentralised. The local government ministry is stated to be digitalising local government services and reviewing the capacity of the cell, the lowest administrative level.

2026-09-17-sen-pressafrik-cdp-daf-intero.summary: Senegal's data protection commission and the state file-automation directorate have finished work on interoperability between the civil registry and public-service identification systems. Two strategic options are now before the authorities for a decision.

2026-09-17-ssd-techafricanews-nca-ngso-d.summary: South Sudan's National Communication Authority took part in the third African preparatory meeting for the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference, held in Tunisia. Non-geostationary satellite systems and direct-to-device connectivity were among the items African regulators worked on for common regional positions.

2026-09-17-swz-eswatinipositivenews-edpa.summary: Eswatini's Data Protection Authority is setting up information desks in major towns to give the public and businesses guidance on data-protection rights, responsibilities and registration. It began the outreach after finding that about eight in ten visitors to its trade fair stand had limited knowledge of the Data Protection Act.

2026-09-17-techafricanews-chad-nigeria-d.summary: Chad and Nigeria agreed to strengthen cooperation in telecommunications, digital transformation and artificial intelligence after ministerial talks in N'Djamena on 16 September. Regional fibre-optic connectivity through the BRIDGE project, government service digitalisation and research were named as the areas of collaboration.

2026-09-17-techafricanews-gabon-electron.summary: Gabon launched an electronic document management platform at the General Secretariat of the Government on 16 September, developed with the national digital infrastructure and frequencies agency. It lets administrations register, classify, search, share and preserve documents, reducing reliance on paper.

2026-09-17-techcabal-nigeria-payment-dat.summary: Nigeria's 1 January 2027 deadline for payment data localisation is pushing banks and fintechs to rethink how they store and secure customer and transaction data. The central bank frames the objective as local oversight of core financial records rather than separation from global providers, and the risks raised include offshore backups and several institutions concentrating on the same domestic facility.

2026-09-17-techtrends-africa-green-data-.summary: African data centres face grids that fail outright rather than merely cost too much, and operators are increasingly building solar-powered server farms from the start instead of retrofitting diesel-dependent ones. The continent holds under 1 per cent of global data-centre capacity, with an industry association putting the shortfall at 1,000MW across some 700 further facilities.

2026-09-17-tgo-ahouevinfo-ipdcp-33-admin.summary: Togo's data-protection authority briefed the heads of 33 ministries and public institutions on their obligations in processing, securing and protecting citizens' personal data, as part of making the 2019 data-protection law known across the administration. Focal points and certified data-protection correspondents are to be named.

2026-09-17-tgo-togofirst-otr-e-tpu-platf.summary: Togo's revenue office opened online filing and payment of the single business tax, the first time the declaration and payment steps have been available without a visit to a tax office. The six-step procedure runs from the taxpayer's identification number to a QR-coded receipt, is designed for a basic handset and connection, accepts three mobile money services, and targets artisans, traders and microenterprises on the flat-rate regime.

2026-09-17-tgo-togopresse-otr-etpu-platf.summary: Togo's revenue office launched its single business tax platform in Lome, automating declaration and assessment, tracking deadlines, securing payment and generating tax documents, available at any hour from a phone, tablet or computer. The finance minister directed the office to run a change-management plan so taxpayers who struggle with the technology are not cut out.

2026-09-17-tun-assabah-conseil-statistiq.summary: Tunisia's National Statistics Council reviewed the statistics institute's development strategy and its 2027 work programme at its second plenary of the year, alongside its own annual statistical programme and the progress of the general agricultural census. Neither the strategy nor the work programme is published with the communique.

2026-09-17-tun-cyberera-african-delegati.summary: African governments and regulators opened four days of talks in Tunis to build common positions on the radio frequencies used by mobile, satellite and other wireless services, ahead of the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference. Broadband capacity, rural connectivity and future communications technologies are the focus.

2026-09-17-tza-citizen-ai-glasses-visual.summary: Tanzanian innovators have built a second prototype of AI glasses for visually impaired users, with a target price of US$200 to US$300 and market entry set for March 2027. The price and the date are the developers' own; no funding or manufacturing route is published.

2026-09-17-tza-citizen-content-creators-.summary: Tanzania's journalists accreditation board said content creators doing journalistic work fall under the Media Services Act, so that none may report news or conduct interviews without accreditation, which requires at least a diploma. The board also said a creator doing journalism must register their platform with the communications regulator as a media outlet.

2026-09-17-tza-citizen-nida-number-digit.summary: Tanzania is piloting registration of children from birth in three districts, and 2,027,103 finished identity cards remain uncollected.

2026-09-17-tza-dailynews-unclaimed-ids-l.summary: Tanzania's Prime Minister told the registration authority to put a legally backed reminder-and-penalty mechanism into law for processed identity cards left uncollected, saying the state cannot keep absorbing the cost of printing cards that are then abandoned. He also directed deeper integration with employment, social-service and economic institutions, and put more than 132bn/- to the authority's development projects for 2026/27, including 31 registration offices.

2026-09-17-tza-mwananchi-zmbf-mixx-yas-d.summary: A foundation, a mobile money service and a business operator signed a partnership to pay Zanzibar's seaweed farmers — most of them women — digitally and to extend savings, contribution and group-lending services to them. The operator supplies connectivity and the registration, reporting and monitoring systems for the foundation's wider programmes.

2026-09-17-uga-newvision-nitau-ughub-ugp.summary: Uganda's IT authority is building a digital signature and document-authentication service on the national authentication platform, binding a signature cryptographically to the holder's national identification number so land sale agreements, transfer forms and consent letters can be signed digitally. The integration platform is to carry real-time verification to the registration authority, so a lands office checks the register rather than a photocopied card; forged signatures in land transactions are the stated first target.

2026-09-17-uga-nilepost-uganda-law-socie.summary: Uganda's law society opened its second digital transformation festival on access to justice, innovation and ethical governance, with lawyers, judges and technologists calling for responsible adoption of digital tools, stronger cybersecurity and wider access to digital justice. The attorney general asked the society to send the festival's recommendations to the justice ministry.

2026-09-17-wearetech-djibouti-huawei-inf.summary: Djibouti discussed the development of its digital infrastructure with Huawei, against its position on the telecommunications routes linking Africa, Asia and the Middle East and its stated ambition to become a regional digital hub. No agreement or project has been published.

2026-09-17-wearetech-mozambique-bresil-n.summary: Mozambique and Brazil signed a memorandum in Maputo on 14 September to accelerate the digitalisation of public services, between Mozambique's finance ministry and Brazil's ministry of management and innovation in public services. Digital sovereignty, cybersecurity and solutions modelled on Brazilian practice are named among its strands.

2026-09-17-wearetech-nic-klopper-alpha-t.summary: A South African entrepreneur has launched Alpha Ticker, a vehicle combining capital deployment, an artificial-intelligence product for portfolio analysis, and a Compute Africa arm targeting data-centre, energy and connectivity infrastructure in sub-Saharan Africa. No fund size or investment has been published.

2026-09-17-wearetech-niger-hamani-kargne.summary: Niger's president appointed e-government specialist Hamani Kargne as minister of communication and new information technologies in a technical reshuffle on 15 September. He replaces Adji Ali Salatou, in post for more than a year.

2026-09-17-wearetech-rdc-pass-identifica.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's RDC-Pass digital identity project entered its first implementation phase three months after launch, with training for 50 registration agents opening in Kinshasa on 15 September. The identifier is intended to work across several administrations and reduce the number of separate identification systems.

2026-09-17-wearetech-vula-william-mapham.summary: South Africa's Vula platform connects frontline clinicians to specialists, centralising received case files and reporting referral volume and origin back to facilities. It runs through a mobile application and a website for registered professionals at low data consumption.

2026-09-17-xaf-afdb-korea-ai-partnership.summary: At a press conference alongside the African Development Bank's president in Seoul, South Korea's deputy prime minister said Korea would deepen its partnership with Africa by expanding cooperation in artificial intelligence and digital technologies. The bank put AI's potential at up to US$1 trillion of African GDP by 2035.

2026-09-17-xaf-leadership-africa-cdc-bii.summary: The continental health agency, with member states and technical partners, has validated a framework, a strategy, a digital and data architecture and a roadmap for harmonising behavioural intelligence and infodemic management, at a five-day workshop in Mombasa. None of the four documents is published.

2026-09-17-xaf-spaceinafrica-rcmrd-digit.summary: A regional mapping centre is training 55 officials from its 20 member states on planning and managing digital land record systems, over five days in Nairobi. The course covers bringing surveying, registration, valuation and mapping into one system, connecting it to national platforms so information is not re-entered, data accuracy and access control, and where state data should be hosted.

2026-09-17-xca-iss-papss-instant-payment.summary: A think-tank analysis sets Central Africa's instant-payment rail against the zone's exchange and anti-money-laundering rules: settlement takes seconds where the rules expect documentary checks before a transfer, and fewer than 13 per cent of adults hold an account.

2026-09-17-xea-eabc-ceo-investment-forum.summary: The East African science and technology commission and the German state of Hessen launched a cooperation through the regional AI alliance at an investment forum in Nairobi, for skills development, innovation and business; no sum, instrument or duration was stated. The forum also launched a regional trade and investment climate report and an investment projects catalogue, and ran a digital economy, telecommunications and fintech track.

2026-09-17-xgl-pbs-us-china-ai-safety-st.summary: An agency report reads the prospects for a global approach to AI safety as dependent on US-China cooperation, with each treating the other's strategy as the problem, ahead of a Washington meeting at which AI governance is expected on the agenda.

2026-09-17-xgl-pewresearch-trust-ai-regu.summary: A survey across twelve countries between February and May 2026 finds a median 43 per cent trusting China to regulate artificial intelligence, against 35 per cent for the United States and 34 for the European Union. In Ghana, as in Peru and Colombia, trust in the United States and China runs at about the same level.

2026-09-17-xwa-tribuneonlineng-ecowas-en.summary: At a Lagos workshop on the regional biometric identity card, Nigeria's immigration service said the card serves the same purpose as the regional passport within the subregion, is renewable every five years, costs N35,500 and is applied for online with a single physical visit for biometric capture. The ECOWAS Commission framed it as harmonising identification and addressing cross-border crime and irregular migration.

2026-09-17-zaf-ewn-dfc-wiocc-investment.summary: The United States development finance corporation approved an equity investment in a Johannesburg-headquartered operator of undersea cables, fibre networks and data centres in more than 30 African countries, naming two investment partners. Its board published no amount; a news organisation puts the investment at around R2.5 billion, up to US$155 million, as a ceiling rather than a committed sum.

2026-09-17-zaf-itweb-ekurhuleni-cameras-.summary: Gauteng's e-government department offered its camera networks to the police investigation into nine women's bodies found in Ekurhuleni since July, for detection, investigation and intelligence gathering. The department had access to 7,271 privately operated cameras in 2025/26 and a cumulative 960 of its own, and is reported to have spent R124 million on closed-circuit television.

2026-09-17-zaf-techcentral-cape-town-dat.summary: Cape Town is drafting new development guidelines for large data-centre applications, its first public acknowledgement that the approvals process needs changing, and confirms that the hyperscale precinct rezoning it granted in July is suspended pending appeal. The operator named throughout the project says the site is a long-term land bank on which it has submitted no planning application.

2026-09-17-zaf-techcentral-offshore-wind.summary: South Africa's electricity and energy department published a strategic framework for offshore wind, identifying about 95GW of technical potential along the coastline and naming energy-hungry coastal users, data centres among them, as the customers who could justify building it. The laws and regulations the build would need do not yet exist and the costs are large.

2026-09-17-zaf-wits-crasa-linkcentre-mou.summary: The Southern African communications regulators' association and a university research centre signed a memorandum on regulatory capacity building, applied research and policy development, covering professional development programmes, short courses, masterclasses, policy dialogues and research across the ICT, postal, audio-visual, digital media and digitally enabled sectors. Activities are expressly subject to institutional processes, funding and separate project agreements.

2026-09-17-zwe-thisisafrica-passport-dat.summary: A commentary follows a passport scan at Harare's airport into the systems behind it, asking what the e-passport chip discloses, where the data is held, who secures it and who built the infrastructure. It traces the build-own-operate-transfer arrangement behind the passport, the earlier supplier, the national data centre opened in 2021 and the regulator's role.

2026-09-18-aacb-annual-meetings-nairobi-.summary: The Association of African Central Banks held its 48th annual meetings in Nairobi from 13 to 18 September, hosted by the Central Bank of Kenya alongside its sixtieth-anniversary events and an AI conference. The published programme names the technical committee, bureau and assembly sittings and the member banks attending each.

2026-09-18-aacb-cbe-egypt-ai-conference-.summary: Governors of more than forty African central banks met in Nairobi for a conference on artificial intelligence in central banking, covering its use in monetary policy and financial stability, in supervision and financial integrity, and in governance and risk management.

2026-09-18-africhange-secures-ghana-imto.summary: A digital remittance company received an international money transfer operator licence from the Bank of Ghana, letting it operate directly rather than through intermediary partners.

2026-09-18-au-maroc-deyaa-wahbi-lance-un.summary: A profile of a Moroccan start-up founded in 2024 whose AI tool is meant to support emergency medical staff. No deployment or evaluation figures are given.

2026-09-18-ben-banouto-anip-eservices-ex.summary: Benin's identification agency added a feature to its e-services portal showing how many residents share a given name, first name or date of birth, drawn from the population register.

2026-09-18-ben-beninwebtv-cnib-renouvell.summary: Benin's identification agency opened online renewal of the biometric identity card to all holders on International Identity Day, through its e-services platform. The procedure is started online but not fully automatic.

2026-09-18-ben-beninwebtv-dgi-eservices-.summary: Benin's tax directorate is opening its online declaration and payment platform to the small-business tax centres of Parakou from 21 September, Comè from 28 September and Lokossa from 5 October.

2026-09-18-ben-chicinfos-univservices-bj.summary: Benin launched UnivServices.bj, a national portal for students at four public universities, with transport as its first live service and catering, housing and health to follow.

2026-09-18-bog-pushes-investor-protectio.summary: Ghana's central bank governor said wider financial inclusion and capital-market participation must come with stronger investor protection. The remarks announce no new rule.

2026-09-18-civ-techafricanews-signature-.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's civil service ministry enrolled the mayor and secretary-general of Marcory in the administration's electronic signature system on 15 September, extending it to local government. No count of enrolled officials is published.

2026-09-18-cmr-businessincameroon-camtel.summary: Cameroon's state operator plans 245 new mobile sites, taking its declared network from 473 to 718, with decongestion of 122 existing sites and a new billing system; a second shipment of equipment from China arrived on 17 September. No cost or completion date is stated.

2026-09-18-dcdt-upbeat-after-entities-sh.summary: South Africa's communications department reported clean audits for three of its entities and an unqualified opinion for the Post Office, its first in six years. The department presents it as a governance recovery.

2026-09-18-drc-using-anonymized-mobile-o.summary: Anonymised call, text and internet records from a mobile operator are being used with a Swedish nonprofit to map population movements in the DR Congo's Ebola outbreak, flagging Kisangani and Kinshasa as relatively high risk. The outbreak had reached 7,200 confirmed cases and 3,475 deaths by 12 September; the same method was used during COVID-19.

2026-09-18-egy-elmydan-biometric-verific.summary: Egypt's communications and interior ministries launched a platform for remote biometric identity verification and electronic signature, which licensed telecom operators can offer inside their own smartphone applications so users need not visit a branch. It was built by the telecom regulator with the IT industry development agency, a local developer and licensed signature providers; no user count or list of relying services is given.

2026-09-18-eri-martinplaut-new-cash-rest.summary: An Eritrean human-rights group reports that a central bank legal notice of 9 September caps the cash an individual may keep beyond 15 days at 25,000 nakfa, with higher limits for businesses, following a June order to deposit cash holdings. It notes that the country has no generally available cash machines or cards and thin branch access outside the main towns.

2026-09-18-eth-fana-knowledge-digital-se.summary: Ethiopia told an Africa-Europe gathering that services trade, digital services and local capacity should be at the centre of new partnerships. The statement sets positions, not agreements.

2026-09-18-eth-fana-mesob-citizen-center.summary: Ethiopia's MESOB one-stop public service presented its digital government model at a Chinese technology vendor's conference in Shanghai. The account is promotional and gives no new usage figures.

2026-09-18-eu-urges-businesses-to-turn-t.summary: At the launch of Eswatini's new trade and investment dashboards, the European Union urged businesses and investors to use them for better-informed decisions.

2026-09-18-fg-sets-up-technical-committe.summary: Nigeria set up a technical sub-committee to review the 2025 tax laws within six weeks, tasked with a Finance Bill 2027, revised withholding tax regulations and an amended significant economic presence order, the rule that reaches foreign digital businesses. The drafts themselves are not yet published.

2026-09-18-ghana-must-turn-research-into.summary: Ghana's chief of staff called for closer collaboration between universities, research institutions, industry and policymakers so that research becomes practical solutions. The speech carries no programme or funding.

2026-09-18-ghanaian-times-volta-chiefs-c.summary: A delegation of Ghana's Volta Regional House of Chiefs signed three memoranda with Chinese companies during a business visit to China, the first with a technology firm on digital transformation and technology transfer in the region. The others cover construction and investment; no values or project list are stated.

2026-09-18-gmb-alkambatimes-moherst-sdai.summary: The Gambia's higher education minister secured Saudi backing, at UNESCO's AI ethics forum in Riyadh, for putting artificial intelligence into universities, technical colleges and madrassa reform. He set out plans to teach AI ethics, data protection and algorithmic accountability in tertiary programmes; no agreement text or funding is stated.

2026-09-18-gmb-voicegambia-gra-wataf-tax.summary: The Gambia's revenue commissioner called at a West African tax forum in Ghana for closer regional cooperation among tax administrations to protect tax bases, including as economic activity moves online.

2026-09-18-gov-t-is-committed-to-moving-.summary: A Ghanaian minister of state told a digital assets summit that the government means to move from digital policy to jobs and investment. The keynote announced no instrument.

2026-09-18-government-plans-unified-syst.summary: Kenya's head of public service convened the public service commission, the examinations council and the education ministry to build a single mechanism linking academic credential databases to hiring agencies, to cut verification delays and fake certificates. No design or date is set.

2026-09-18-govt-eyes-e3bn-in-new-loans.summary: Eswatini's finance minister said the government will table a World Bank loan package for ICT, including support for the state posts and telecommunications corporation and lower data costs, within a wider borrowing programme. He gave no amount or date for the ICT package.

2026-09-18-heads-must-roll-there-is-noth.summary: Ghana's acting rent control commissioner called for an investigation into a digitisation programme on which US$1.7 million was reportedly spent under the previous government, saying he found only four computers at the facility. No audit finding is yet on record.

2026-09-18-hollard-data-hits-dark-web-af.summary: Data allegedly stolen from a South African insurer appeared on the dark web, a researcher confirming it is public, after the June attack on its software supplier. The criminal group had demanded a ransom from the insurer to keep it private.

2026-09-18-ifc-complete-farmer-to-transf.summary: The World Bank's private-sector arm partnered with a Ghanaian agricultural technology company to extend data, farm technology and financing to smallholders. No amount or farmer target is stated in this account.

2026-09-18-inside-the-fake-aarto-fine-sc.summary: South Africa's road traffic infringement agency is considering an investigation into whether the national vehicle database was accessed, after fake traffic-fine messages began quoting motorists' correct number plates. The fines platform being impersonated says its own system was not breached.

2026-09-18-internet-society-pulse-sao-to.summary: The Internet Society's resilience index scores São Tomé and Príncipe at 33 out of 100, below the Middle Africa average of 38 and the Africa average of 44, across infrastructure, market readiness, performance and security.

2026-09-18-kenya-mobile-money-accounts-h.summary: Kenya's regulator put mobile money subscriptions at 54,005,800 at the end of June 2026, up 1.2 per cent in the quarter and 13.2 per cent on the year, while more than 34,000 registered agents left the market in the same three months. Subscriptions count accounts, not people.

2026-09-18-kenya-plans-to-expand-bpo-and.summary: Kenya's ICT principal secretary set out plans to extend outsourcing and global business services jobs beyond Nairobi and Mombasa for young people, noting that one international operator runs more than 2,500 seats in the two cities.

2026-09-18-kenya-takes-ai-and-technology.summary: Kenya's technology envoy said the country will press AI governance, digital resilience, investment and technology capacity at the 81st UN General Assembly. The briefing set out positions, not commitments.

2026-09-18-kenya-to-spread-bpo-jobs-beyo.summary: Kenya's ICT principal secretary said the government wants business process outsourcing and global services jobs to spread beyond Nairobi and Mombasa to smaller towns, after touring a French outsourcing firm's Nairobi operation. No incentive or site plan is named.

2026-09-18-kenyan-fintech-payd-to-resume.summary: A Kenyan cross-border payments startup serving about 30,000 freelancers and businesses paused payouts around May after foreign-exchange losses left it short of customer balances, and says it will resume after overhauling its treasury system. The case shows how currency exposure can strand customer funds at small payment firms.

2026-09-18-l-algerien-nacer-abdelli-lie-.summary: A profile of an Algerian entrepreneur whose platform, founded in 2020, combines vocational training courses and tests with recruitment, so employers can choose and train future staff in one tool. No user figures are given.

2026-09-18-lby-libyaupdate-cbl-governor-.summary: Libya's central bank governor presented the bank's payments modernisation, including instant transfers and a salary-payment project, to Arab and international banks in London. The meeting discussed widening correspondent banking; no agreements are reported.

2026-09-18-malawi-drops-id-card-expiry-d.summary: Malawi launched the Nzika digital ID wallet on International Identity Day, holding national ID, birth, marriage and death credentials on a phone as an optional complement to the physical card. The homeland security minister also ended expiry dates on the biometric ID card with immediate effect.

2026-09-18-mar-assahafa-idarati-portail-.summary: Morocco's digital transition ministry launched a new version of the Idarati portal, giving access to 874 online services organised around user journeys and 2,533 published administrative acts, with a feedback function, an accessibility redesign and a marketplace of AI solutions. The ministry presents it as groundwork for Idarati X.0.

2026-09-18-mar-mmsp-inauguration-btechno.summary: A French telecom group's Moroccan engineering subsidiary opened in Rabat with more than 1,000 staff, close to 850 of them engineers, working on fibre, 5G, AI, cybersecurity and network supervision. The digital transition minister placed it under the Digital Morocco 2030 strategy and its talent and digital-export aims.

2026-09-18-mar-mtnra-communique-idarati-.summary: The Moroccan digital transition ministry's own communiqué on the relaunched Idarati portal presents it as a proactive, user-centred single access point to administrations' digital services.

2026-09-18-mar-telquel-paiement-digital-.summary: A Moroccan analysis finds that cash in circulation has doubled since 2019 despite payment accounts, cards, wallets and instant transfers, and that less than fourteen of every hundred dirhams passing through a bank card are spent as payments. It notes that direct social aid lands in payment accounts and is withdrawn within hours.

2026-09-18-moz-360mozambique-incm-intern.summary: Mozambique's telecoms regulator says a tariff management system due in November 2026 will compare operators' packages, identify the effective price including validity, and stop data bundles running out before their stated expiry, after consumer complaints. It is also restructuring packages.

2026-09-18-mwi-malawi24-macra-warns-misu.summary: Malawi's communications regulator warned publicly that using AI or other digital tools to create or spread false or manipulated information could bring civil and criminal liability, citing the Penal Code's section on false statements likely to cause fear and alarm. It says it and other authorities are acting to identify and trace those responsible.

2026-09-18-mwi-techreviewafrica-giz-data.summary: GIZ ran a three-day training-of-trainers programme for Malawi's data protection authority in Lilongwe, to build capacity to implement the country's data protection framework.

2026-09-18-nam-neweralive-cyber-threats-.summary: Namibia's communications regulator reports cyber threat events up 57 per cent and vulnerabilities up 40 per cent in the April-June quarter, alongside 2 per cent growth in mobile subscriptions to about 2.79 million and about N$243m invested in networks.

2026-09-18-new-trade-dashboards-open-glo.summary: Eswatini launched two public dashboards, one on investment attractiveness and one on export-market intelligence, built by the trade ministry and the investment promotion authority with the International Trade Centre under EU support. No data licence or update schedule is stated.

2026-09-18-nga-arusha-mandate-ai-examina.summary: The registrar of Nigeria's National Examinations Council was elected vice-president of the Association for Educational Assessment in Africa at its 42nd conference in Arusha, and Abuja will host the 2027 meeting. The piece argues that this puts Nigeria in a position to shape how African examinations are run as AI enters assessment.

2026-09-18-nga-blueprint-digital-id-akum.summary: The Secretary to the Government of the Federation told the National Day of Identity that Nigeria's digital identity infrastructure is now a trusted foundation for banking, telecommunications, social protection and cross-border trade. He credited the National Identity Management Commission Act 2026 with giving it a stronger legal footing and making the commission the country's root certification authority for identity, citing no enrolment figure.
