2026-09-18-nga-ecowas-biometric-card-enb.summary: At a Lagos media workshop the migration organisation, Nigeria's immigration service and the ECOWAS Commission set out the case for the regional biometric identity card, presenting it as the instrument of the free movement protocol and as conferring the right to live and trade in any member state. The card is put at N35,000 to acquire, a figure another account of the same workshop gives as N35,500.

2026-09-18-nga-ndifs-digital-invoices-fi.summary: Nigeria inaugurated the steering committee of a National Digital Invoicing and Financial Optimisation Strategy, meant to let businesses raise working capital against verified digital invoices. The trade minister framed it as moving e-invoicing beyond tax compliance into a national receivables-finance corridor; no rules or launch date are set.

2026-09-18-nga-thisday-smedan-koica-undp.summary: Nigeria's small-business agency broke ground in Abuja on a US$12 million entrepreneurship centre funded by Korea through KOICA and developed with UNDP. It is to support 500 young entrepreneurs and 400 start-ups in fintech, edtech, healthtech and agritech; no completion date is stated.

2026-09-18-nga-tinubu-digital-free-zones.summary: The president declared Nigeria's Digital Free Zones initiative moved to its implementation stage, with one zone licensed. The stated aim is that Nigerian technology and service companies raise global capital and serve international markets without incorporating or holding intellectual property abroad; the declaration came through an adviser's release and carries no zone count, investment figure or timetable.

2026-09-18-nigcomsat-picks-hughes-for-ne.summary: Nigeria's satellite operator says part of the ground equipment for its two next communications satellites, due to launch in 2028 and 2029, will be assembled locally with engineering support from the US firm supplying the ground system. The satellites themselves are being built by European and Israeli manufacturers.

2026-09-18-niger-begins-operational-roll.summary: Niger opened public enrolment for the Alliance of Sahel States biometric passport in Niamey on 15 September, with regional and diaspora centres and online pre-enrolment through mobile money to follow. An ordinary passport costs FCFA 45,000; Niger is the last of the three states to issue it.

2026-09-18-nigeria-warns-pos-agents-agai.summary: Nigeria's anti-corruption agency warned point-of-sale agents against facilitating money laundering, terrorist financing, ransom payments and fraud, saying investigations show such funds are often routed through their machines. It asked the agents' association to keep full records of operators and transactions.

2026-09-18-rdc-transco-et-firstbank-s-al.summary: Kinshasa's public transport company signed a partnership with a commercial bank on 17 September to digitise several of its systems, starting with revenue management, and to prepare a prepaid fare card. No timetable or cost is stated.

2026-09-18-rgph-2-le-gouvernement-impliq.summary: The DR Congo's planning minister met telecom operators to enlist them in spreading information about the second general population and housing census. The meeting concerned publicity for the census rather than any use of operator data.

2026-09-18-sakaja-gives-nairobi-traders-.summary: Nairobi's governor told traders to apply for county permits directly through official online channels rather than intermediaries, and announced ways to verify county enforcement officers against impersonators. No figures on permits or fraud cases are given.

2026-09-18-sle-sierraloaded-stats-sl-cen.summary: Statistics Sierra Leone completed nationwide mapping for the December 2026 census, the country's first digital census, and the census technical committee received the mapping completion report on 15 September. The committee also reviewed an August mock census; Census Night is set for 1 December.

2026-09-18-som-wardheernews-digital-iron.summary: Somali journalists and political figures had Facebook accounts suspended, removed, or falsely marked as belonging to the dead, including the pages of two regional presidents and a journalist with more than a million followers. The account disruptions are documented; responsibility for them is not, and the piece states plainly that no evidence establishes who ordered or carried them out, calling for an independent investigation.

2026-09-18-south-africa-sme-funding-gap-.summary: An African Bank executive argues that South Africa's estimated R350 billion small-business financing gap persists despite funders doubling since 2018 because lenders lack usable data on small firms. It is a commentary, and the remedies it proposes are a lender's view rather than policy.

2026-09-18-tcd-lendjampost-digitalisatio.summary: A Chadian analysis finds the state's push to go paperless and cashless under the 2026 finance law, with 3,000 payment terminals in revenue offices and compulsory electronic invoicing, held back by power cuts, thin connectivity in the provinces and some officials' limited digital skills. It also names the integrated public-finance system and a June 2026 awareness campaign; no transaction figures are given.

2026-09-18-techcabal-mafab-5g-spectrum-n.summary: A Nigerian licensee is seeking to transfer its 2x20 MHz at 2.1 GHz and its 100 MHz block at 3.5 GHz to the largest operator, subject to regulatory approval. It paid US$273.6 million for the 3.5 GHz lot at the December 2021 auction against a US$197.4 million reserve, took a unified access licence in July 2022 and never reached commercial service; a wider review of underused spectrum is attributed to people familiar with the matter rather than to the regulator.

2026-09-18-terra-industries-leads-1m-rou.summary: Aeon, a Nigerian cybersecurity startup built inside a cloud infrastructure platform, raised US$1 million in a pre-seed round led by a defence-technology firm, with several African venture funds participating. It sells risk detection, vulnerability management and in-network monitoring to banks, energy and mobility operators.

2026-09-18-tgo-togofirst-sme-financing-p.summary: Togo's credit information bureau presented a portal on which small businesses will submit financing requests that banks and microfinance institutions review directly, guiding applicants through the documents a complete loan file needs. It is to launch by the end of 2026 with development-finance support, and Togo was chosen as the pilot country because of existing public programmes to strengthen small-business financing.

2026-09-18-transformation-numerique-les-.summary: The Comoros' digital development agency and UNDP signed a memorandum on 16 September to run a national digital readiness assessment covering skills, connectivity, public services, regulation and the digital economy across the three islands. It is presented as a way to target the next investments under the Comores Numérique 2028 strategy; no timetable is given.

2026-09-18-tun-directinfo-ministere-agri.summary: Tunisia's agriculture ministry says it is integrating the E-Houwiya digital identity into its online services to unify access and secure transactions, setting 15 November 2026 as the deadline for the bodies under it.

2026-09-18-tun-leconomistemaghrebin-paie.summary: A Tunisian central bank and GIZ mission studied Brazil's PIX instant payment system, its architecture, governance, regulation and economic model. The outlet stresses that nothing indicates Tunisia is building its own version: no adoption or launch calendar has been announced.

2026-09-18-tun-tunisietribune-ministere-.summary: Tunisia's agriculture ministry issued a circular requiring every body under it to integrate the E-Houwiya digital identity into its platforms by 15 November 2026. It makes the E-Houwiya identifier the sole reference for any new digital service and requires strong multi-factor authentication where extra checks apply.

2026-09-18-uga-ceoeastafrica-centenary-b.summary: Uganda's Centenary Bank launched GonzaPay, a wallet running as an app and over USSD for customers without smartphones, and says it will add savings, lending, insurance and investment with AI-based credit assessment. The account is the bank's own, given in an interview, with no user figures.

2026-09-18-uga-kampalareport-parish-deve.summary: An inter-ministerial meeting put Uganda's Parish Development Model at 3,571,108 beneficiaries against UGX 4.317 trillion capitalised through 10,589 parish SACCOs, lending up to UGX 1 million at 6 per cent a year. It says 183,430 of 222,389 enterprise groups are profiled on the programme's information system; the figures are the government's own.

2026-09-18-vodafone-warns-network-shutdo.summary: A Vodafone report argues that deliberate network shutdowns are growing in frequency, length and cost while often failing to achieve their stated aims, citing at least 313 shutdowns across 52 countries in 2025, the worst year on record, and an economic cost approaching US$20 billion. It is an operator's own study drawing on civil-society counts, not a regulatory finding.

2026-09-18-zaf-citizen-opinion-social-me.summary: An opinion piece argues South Africa should consider an under-16 social-media age restriction rather than a ban, with the obligation resting on platforms as it does in Australia, and as part of a wider child-development and online-safety strategy rather than as a solution on its own.

2026-09-18-zaf-citizen-sassa-digital-gra.summary: South Africa's social security agency set out a modernisation programme taking grant services online: applications and payment-detail changes, electronic life certification, messaging support, self-service kiosks and free Wi-Fi at its offices. Its systems are being integrated with other government institutions, which the agency says will help detect fraud and speed processing; no uptake figure is published for any of it.

2026-09-18-zaf-ewn-black-sash-social-gra.summary: A South African rights group reports a spike in calls from grant beneficiaries facing the social security agency's review, citing transport costs, queues, poor network coverage and offices that are offline. It urges beneficiaries to respond to review notices despite the system problems.

2026-09-18-zaf-mip-breach-hackers-extort.summary: The group behind the June breach at an insurance software supplier is now extorting South African insurers directly, after the supplier paid a ransom for an undertaking to destroy the data. Material on a leak site includes policyholders' names, their children's names, identity numbers and email addresses; about 45 insurers' customers were exposed.

2026-09-18-zambia-turns-to-ai-to-hit-tou.summary: Zambia's tourism ministry says it will use artificial intelligence and other technologies toward its target of doubling international arrivals to 5 million a year, opening with a first Tourism and Technology Symposium in Lusaka on responsible AI and smart tourism. No specific system, budget or timetable is named.

2026-09-18-zmb-efficacynews-70-schools-s.summary: Zambia launched a three-year programme to connect an initial 70 public schools by satellite, with solar power for schools off the grid, run by the presidential delivery unit with private partners. No cost or school list is stated.

2026-09-18-zwe-businesstimes-mavetera-te.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT and postal minister told the first annual postal and courier conference that the sector must reinvent itself as an engine of e-commerce and trade. The speech sets out an expectation, not a programme or funding.

2026-09-18-zwe-herald-30-new-vehicles-bo.summary: Zimbabwe's home affairs minister commissioned 30 vehicles for the civil registry department to improve mobility and service delivery nationwide.

2026-09-19-egy-egypttoday-sisi-5g-data-c.summary: The presidency directed the expansion of fifth-generation mobile networks, hyperscale data centres and a unified government services card. The instruction is tied to a target of eight billion dollars in digital exports by 2028.

2026-09-19-expense-ai-day-1-1000.summary: A Lagos expense-tracking startup abandoned open banking after the account-data calls it depended on came to about 200 naira each, and rebuilt the product around reading receipts instead. It now reports 10,000 users across 100 countries.

2026-09-19-mtn-foundation-ict-business-s.summary: The eighth phase of an operator foundation's skills programme narrowed its intake to young women running micro businesses in six states. Its grant pool is 100 million naira for 100 participants, against 300 million for 600 in the previous phase.

2026-09-19-nga-thenicheng-katsina-ncc-mt.summary: The governor of Katsina State constituted a four-member joint implementation committee with the communications regulator and the dominant mobile operator, to turn a courtesy visit into a costed connectivity plan.

2026-09-19-techtrends-african-developers.summary: A survey of open-source work across Africa counts 9.3 million developer accounts in the first quarter of 2026 and committers up 18 per cent over 2025. It notes that some governments now build public infrastructure on open code, citing a Rwandan payment service running on an open-source switch.

2026-09-19-tunisie-cni-hosting-services-.summary: Tunisia's national computing centre describes the state data centre that carries the government's major applications: about fifty servers serving some 4,500 workstations across ministries, regional offices, public bodies and municipalities, with a replicated backup site.

2026-09-19-xaf-timeslive-afcfta-mene-dat.summary: The head of the continental free trade area told a conference that Africa should aim for more than 700 data centres within ten years to carry a digital economy he put at 700 billion dollars. About 260 are counted now, and he named South Africa, Nigeria and Kenya as the builds to replicate.

2026-09-20-aacb-48th-meetings-bureau-dai.summary: The Association of African Central Banks approved a second edition of the African Financial Stability Report and constituted the board of the African Monetary Institute, closing its 48th annual meetings in Nairobi with the governors of 34 of its 41 member central banks present. Egypt joined the Bureau of Governors as deputy chair for North Africa and chairs the taskforce preparing the report, which is to be published through the stability committee's portal.

2026-09-20-businessdaily-eac-insurance-r.summary: Insurance regulators from six East African states adopted a harmonised assessment template built on about 25 insurance core principles, and agreed to run assessments against it and compare them in December. The same meeting approved regional guidelines on complaints handling and on comparable market data, and progressed a shared supervisory software for information exchange between the regulators.

2026-09-20-cemac-data-governance-roadmap.summary: A five-day African Development Bank, CEMAC and UNFPA workshop closed at Libreville with a 2026-2029 calendar for migrating the six member states to SDMX and version 2.0 of the Open Data Platform. The stated aim is not to make the national statistical systems uniform but to define common structures that let them interoperate; 14 recommendations were addressed to the institutes, the Commission, the Bank and the World Bank.

2026-09-20-egy-youm7-madbouly-infrastruc.summary: Egypt's communications minister told a cabinet meeting on digital projects that the ministry is drawing up an integrated national data-centre strategy with other ministries, to expand capacity inside the country. He set out the incumbent's programme to replace copper with fibre nationally, including in the villages of the rural development initiative, and the finance minister said state spending is being steered towards digital infrastructure and artificial intelligence. No text, timetable or cost was given.

2026-09-20-ken-standard-iebc-voter-regis.summary: Kenyan political parties and election observers are to be given access to the source code and audit logs of the electoral commission's continuous voter registration system, following a court directive. The account is a free lede behind a paywall and names neither the court, the case nor the date of the directive.

2026-09-20-nam-namibian-ransomhouse-ndf-.summary: A ransomware group listed the Namibian Defence Force among its victims and published an evidence pack it says shows access to the force's systems, with a message accusing its IT department of concealing the incident. No confirmation or response from the force is on record, and the defence minister said he had not heard of it.

2026-09-20-papss-im-bank-kenya-go-live-t.summary: The Pan-African Payment and Settlement System went live for customers of I&M Bank Kenya, the second Kenyan bank on the network. Customers can send to participating African markets in Kenyan shillings through the bank's branches rather than converting into an international currency; no volume, fee or corridor detail was published.

2026-09-20-papss-meeza-card-integration-.summary: Afreximbank is connecting the continental card scheme to Egypt's Meeza national card network so cards issued on either side work across more African markets. The first phase joins the two infrastructures and establishes a settlement layer; payment would be in the currency of the country being visited, and no availability date was given.

2026-09-20-som-hiiraan-national-id-1-5-m.summary: Somalia's identity authority has registered more than 1.5 million citizens since 2023, against a target of 15 million citizens and residents by 2029. The interior minister said issuance would extend to embassies abroad, with priority for persons with disabilities and displaced communities.

2026-09-20-tcd-lendjampost-house-of-afri.summary: A campaign on digital citizenship and the risks of internet use was launched at Abeche by a non-governmental organisation with Chad's national youth council, backed by an external democracy initiative. No participant target, duration or further location was given.

2026-09-20-techtrends-digital-skills-gap.summary: An account of the cybersecurity staffing gap in African governments, putting 63 per cent of sub-Saharan organisations short of cyber staff and Nigeria's shortfall at 90.6 per cent against 25,760 people in post. It runs through recent attacks on the core of the state, among them three on Senegalese public institutions in under six months.

2026-09-20-the-next-wave-the-expensive-l.summary: An account of the Kenyan business-to-business commerce company Twiga Foods, which raised about US$185.4 million over twelve years without reaching profitability. It traces the premise that software could displace the brokers between smallholder farmers and neighbourhood kiosks, and what the company's farming arm, its Tatu City lease and a creditor's petition have cost that premise.

2026-09-20-uga-nilepost-mtn-internet-bus.summary: 305 people graduated in Kampala from the sixth phase of a mobile-classroom digital and financial literacy programme run by the largest mobile operator's foundation, taking the number trained to more than 6,700. The training covers safe internet use, digital productivity and the use of digital financial services.

2026-09-20-xgl-reuters-bessent-he-ai-tra.summary: The US Treasury Secretary and China's Vice Premier were to meet to prepare possible agreements on artificial intelligence, tariffs and critical minerals ahead of a Washington summit, with the trade truce between the two set to expire on 10 November. The report is held only as far as its paywall.

2026-09-20-zwe-newzimbabwe-mnangagwa-ai-.summary: Zimbabwe's president named the digital divide, online safety and fair artificial intelligence as the country's priorities for the UN General Assembly, saying the world must rebuild trust to manage a transformation moving faster than ever. The statement was made in a post on his own account on arriving in New York.

2026-09-21-ago-angop-abanc-campanha-cont.summary: The Angolan Bankers Association launched a 60-day public campaign against banking fraud in Luanda on 21 September 2026, working with the interbank processor EMIS. Its president linked the campaign to the risks of banking by phone and to customers' low financial literacy. The campaign will appear in traditional and digital media, on billboards and ATMs, and through banks' own channels.

2026-09-21-ago-expansao-kwik-carteiras-d.summary: Transfers between digital wallets were only 0.6% (Kz 3.1 billion) of the Kz 557.4 billion that passed through Angola's Kwik instant-payment system in the first half of 2026, according to EMIS data. Wallets sent about 38% of the value, nearly all of it to bank accounts, while banks sent about 62%, and only Kz 2.8 billion of that went to non-bank providers. Only the free opening of the article is held.

2026-09-21-bfa-burkina24-orange-max-it-n.summary: Orange Burkina Faso relaunched its Max It app on 18 September 2026 with a promotional caravan through four cities. The new version adds messaging and TV to mobile money, calls and SMS, and is open to customers of other networks. It links to almost all the country's banks for transfers to wallets, and takes water and electricity bills and public charges such as the vehicle tax.

2026-09-21-bwa-weekendpost-absa-google-p.summary: Absa Bank Botswana has made Google Pay available on Android for its Visa debit, credit and multi-currency virtual cards, with no extra fees. The launch date was not given. The service only works where merchants have NFC terminals, and the report says these are patchy outside Gaborone and Francistown.

2026-09-21-civ-aip-pagds-realisations-di.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's World Bank-funded PAGDS project, approved in April 2019, reported its digitalisation results on 21 September 2026, and its coordinator said a second phase has started. The results include digital allocation and tracking of pupils in private schools, patient tracking under universal health coverage, electronic payment of state transfers and online company registration. World Bank figures cited put average growth in non-oil tax revenue at 12.4% against a 5% target, and customs revenue at 19.2% against 6%.

2026-09-21-cod-7sur7-igf-afd-transformat.summary: DR Congo's Inspection Générale des Finances asked the French development agency AFD, at its Paris headquarters on 18 September 2026, to support its digital transformation. The plan centres on a national store of state financial data for auditing. The head of the DRC's digital transformation project said AFD could help through that project, but the talks were exploratory and no amount was named.

2026-09-21-cod-actualitecd-bcc-adhesion-.summary: DR Congo joined the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System on 18 September 2026, when the central bank governor, André Wameso, signed the accession agreement in Nairobi. The same day he signed the East African Community central banks' memorandum on currency convertibility and repatriation, which Burundi, Uganda, Tanzania, Kenya and South Sudan had already joined.

2026-09-21-cog-adiac-sicom-bilan-23-reso.summary: Congo's first information, communication and media fair closed at Kintélé on 19 September 2026 with 23 resolutions from participants. They call for rewriting the three core media laws to take account of digital broadcasting, online platforms and AI, and cover digital content, advertising and tax. These are recommendations from the profession, not government decisions.

2026-09-21-dza-interfil-conseil-ministre.summary: Algeria's Council of Ministers, meeting under President Tebboune on 20 September 2026, called for a presidential decree setting up a secure plan for data exchange between state bodies, overseen by the High Commissioner for Digitalisation. The president asked for the plan to reach the wilayas too, with strong protection of citizens' data. He also ordered that payments to farmers at the state cereals office be digitised immediately.

2026-09-21-egy-mubadala-paymob-35m-pre-s.summary: Egyptian payments company Paymob raised $35 million in a pre-Series C round co-led by Abu Dhabi's Mubadala and the EBRD, with BII, Global Ventures and DPI Ventures also taking part (21 September 2026). The money will fund expansion across the Middle East and North Africa. Paymob says revenue from the Gulf grew sevenfold in 18 months and now makes up close to half the total.

2026-09-21-egy-newkerala-india-egypt-ict.summary: India's ambassador to Egypt, Suresh Reddy, met communications minister Raafat Hindy to discuss closer cooperation on ICT. According to the Indian embassy, the talks covered India's digital public infrastructure and how it could be used elsewhere, cooperation between institutions, and links between the two countries' tech companies. No outcome was announced.

2026-09-21-egy-zawya-orange-egypt-marake.summary: Orange Egypt will design, install and operate telecoms networks at four Marakez developments: Ramla, District 5, Aeon Towers and Mall of Arabia. The deal covers fibre to the home, bundled broadband, TV and voice, public Wi-Fi and a smart CCTV system for the mall's first phase. No value was disclosed.

2026-09-21-gamtel-company-profile-ace-25.summary: The Gambian state operator's undated company profile. It says Gamtel has four international gateways on the ACE submarine cable giving 25 Gbps, and a 28 Gbps backup link through Senegal's Free that traffic switches to if ACE fails.

2026-09-21-gmb-gnnliberia-lra-gra-revenu.summary: The Liberia Revenue Authority signed a memorandum of engagement to help the Gambia Revenue Authority build a dashboard that tracks revenue collection; it was announced from Accra on 20 September 2026 and signed during meetings of the West African Tax Administration Forum. The help covers a review of GRA's data sources, choice of indicators, design, a prototype, integration and staff training. The LRA will send the developer of its own dashboard to Banjul for an initial three weeks.

2026-09-21-gmb-thepoint-gra-lra-digital-.summary: The Gambian account of the Liberia–Gambia revenue dashboard agreement, summarised under the GNN Liberia report. It adds that the LRA pays the expert's airfare while the GRA covers lodging and local transport.

2026-09-21-gsma-pdaa-advancing-digital-c.summary: The report behind the GSMA and PDAA roadmap, summarised under the launch. It counts 550 million internet users in Africa in 2025 (36% of the population) and projects about 700 million by 2030 on current trends. Halving the coverage and usage gaps could add some 514 million people and take the total past 1 billion.

2026-09-21-gsma-pdaa-roadmap-1-billion-c.summary: The GSMA and the Partnership for Digital Access in Africa launched a roadmap in New York on 21 September 2026 on how to reach 1 billion connected Africans by 2030. Based on 11 markets, it finds about 906 million people living within mobile broadband coverage but not using the mobile internet, against 122 million with no coverage at all. Its three priorities are moving over 600 million 2G and 3G connections to 4G or 5G, investing in energy and connectivity together, and reaching rural areas more cheaply.

2026-09-21-itweb-africa-kenya-hoover-ins.summary: Kenya's foreign ministry signed a five-year memorandum of understanding with the Emerging Markets Working Group at Stanford's Hoover Institution during the UN General Assembly in New York. The signing date was not given. The first project is an El Niño monitoring and response system that brings climate, geospatial, water, farming and infrastructure data together by county. Later work is to include a digital trade readiness index and a tracker for public-private partnerships.

2026-09-21-itweb-africa-malawi-india-tec.summary: India's High Commission and the mHub innovation hub held a workshop in Lilongwe on AI, digital skills and technology investment, attended by more than 70 companies. India's high commissioner pointed to openings in agriculture, digital public infrastructure and financial inclusion. No agreement or commitment came out of it.

2026-09-21-itweb-fpb-ai-oversight-stream.summary: South Africa's Film and Publication Board has approved a strategy on digitisation and AI and plans to try generative AI for monitoring, classifying content and managing cases over the next three to five years. None of it is yet in use. Its enforcement committee fined 21 content distributors a total of R16.175 million in September 2026.

2026-09-21-ken-cbk-draft-nps-policy-and-.summary: Kenya's National Treasury and central bank published a draft National Payment System Policy and a draft National Payment System Bill, 2026 for public comment on 21 September 2026. The bill would replace the current Act and license payment providers and system operators by category, with minimum capital of Ksh5 million to Ksh250 million. It also requires interoperability, allows open-finance data sharing with consent and brings virtual asset providers that offer payments under the law, while the policy commits the government to a national instant payment switch.

2026-09-21-ken-kenyans-ardhisasa-outage-.summary: Kenya's ArdhiSasa land platform announced an outage on 21 September 2026 affecting searches, transfers, title and lease registration, and stamp duty and land-rent payments, with no time given for restoring service. The Law Society of Kenya had already complained that the platform was unavailable from 1 September.

2026-09-21-ken-treasury-draft-national-p.summary: Kenya's draft National Payment System Policy, dated August 2026, which identifies ten gaps in the current system. It commits to a national instant payment switch, requires open APIs and gives non-banks access to settlement. The consultation is summarised under the Treasury and central bank's joint release.

2026-09-21-ken-treasury-national-payment.summary: The full draft text of Kenya's National Payment System Bill, 2026, which runs to 79 clauses. It sets licence capital of Ksh5 million to Ksh250 million, requires interoperability, provides for open finance, brings virtual asset providers into scope and sets fines of up to Ksh20 million. The consultation is summarised under the Treasury and central bank's joint release.

2026-09-21-lbr-frontpageafrica-cybercrim.summary: A second account of the Wrotto arrest, summarised under the New Dawn report. It adds a justice ministry prosecutor's view that the state, not the vice-president, decides whether a prosecution goes ahead, and notes that the Act does not mention AI or deepfakes.

2026-09-21-lbr-newdawn-koung-seeks-relea.summary: Liberia's vice-president Jeremiah Koung asked for the release of Jerry Nyantee Wrotto, whom police detained under the Cybercrime Act over AI-made images and videos of Koung, and said he would not press charges. It is one of the first high-profile uses of the Act, signed on 19 August 2026 with the Data Protection Act. The head of the Executive Protection Service defended the arrest, while critics including former finance minister Samuel Tweah said the Act's cyberbullying clauses cover protected speech.

2026-09-21-lby-alwasat-cbl-unified-datab.summary: Libya's central bank governor, Naji Issa, put forward an electronic system and a single national database for recording and following up international grants, projects and support. He made the proposal on 21 September 2026 at the second meeting of the committee set up under prime-ministerial decision 422 of 2026. The idea is still under discussion and has not been adopted.

2026-09-21-mdg-newsmada-gasy-money-bgfib.summary: BGFIBank Madagascar launched Gasy Money, a mobile banking app open to people without an account at the bank, including those with no bank account at all, on any mobile network. The launch date was not given. It handles deposits and withdrawals through agents, branches and ATMs, merchant and bill payments, top-ups of prepaid Visa cards, and transfers to bank accounts and Airtel Money.

2026-09-21-mli-burkina24-centre-ia-robot.summary: Transition president Assimi Goïta opened Mali's artificial intelligence and robotics centre, CIAR-Mali, at Kati on 21 September 2026. He had laid its foundation stone on 7 June 2023. The 50-hectare site has six buildings, including teaching space, dormitories and a workshop for building intelligent systems, and cost FCFA 3.3 billion, all from the national budget.

2026-09-21-moz-aim-transformacao-digital.summary: Mozambique is drafting a three-year operational plan to speed up the digitisation of public services to 2029. At a meeting of the technical commission on digital transformation in Maputo on 21 September 2026, the head of the digital transformation agency said the Citizen Portal already offered about 26 services and had over 3,000 users before its official launch. An interoperability portal, a payments platform for state services, a government cloud and a government data centre are to follow. The commission expects to harmonise and cost the plan within two to three months, with funding spread across many donor projects.

2026-09-21-moz-diarioeconomico-soberania.summary: A second account of the Mozambique digital transformation meeting, summarised under the AIM report. It leads on the state administration minister, Inocêncio Impissa, saying that data produced by public bodies must belong to the state. The plan has not yet been costed.

2026-09-21-mrt-rfi-restriction-reseaux-s.summary: Reactions in Nouakchott to the government's plan, presented to cabinet on 16 September 2026, to bar under-16s from social media without parental consent. A blogger supports protecting children but fears the measure could be used to restrict free expression, and a cybersecurity expert argues for education rather than bans.

2026-09-21-mtnima-etablissements-sous-tu.summary: Mauritania's digital ministry lists the bodies under its supervision: a distance-learning centre, the postal operator, and the state company that owns the national fibre backbone, created by decree in 2014, alongside the regional connectivity projects it runs. The page states each body's mandate but gives no budget, staffing or performance figures.

2026-09-21-nam-newera-fintech-jobs-namfi.summary: The head of Namibia's financial regulator, Kenneth Matomola, said fintech could help with jobs and financial inclusion now that the Financial Institutions and Markets Act and a new Namfisa Act are in force. Both took effect on 1 May 2026. He cited youth unemployment of 44.4% in the 2023 labour force survey.

2026-09-21-nga-boi-idice-tor-kpo-it-enab.summary: The terms of reference, dated 21 September 2026, for the iDICE consultancy to build a knowledge-process outsourcing industry under the Outsource to Nigeria Initiative. They set five workstreams and a target of paid placement for 80% of trainees within six months. The procurement is summarised under the Premium Times notice.

2026-09-21-nga-businessday-national-broa.summary: Nigeria's National Broadband Plan 2020–2025 ended short of its main target: broadband penetration was 51.97% in December 2025 against 70%, according to NCC figures. 4G made up 52.95% of mobile subscriptions at the end of 2025, also short of its 70% target. The analysis traces penetration through the plan period, when it fell as low as 40.88% in 2021.

2026-09-21-nga-idice-reoi-kpo-it-enabled.summary: Nigeria's Bank of Industry, which runs the iDICE programme, is seeking consultants for a 16-month assignment to build a knowledge-process outsourcing industry under the Outsource to Nigeria Initiative. The brief includes an academy for 1,000 graduates, 200 paid residency places a year, a target of 80% placement within six months of certification, and a framework of rules and tax incentives for delivery centres. iDICE is co-financed by the AfDB, AFD and IsDB; expressions of interest close on 5 October 2026.

2026-09-21-nga-naltf-kankia-rural-digita.summary: A research summary from the National Assembly Library Trust Fund arguing that Nigeria's rural digital divide comes from weak funding, coordination and oversight, not from a lack of policy. It reviews the digital economy strategy, the 2020–2025 broadband plan, the Universal Service Provision Fund and the Digital Nigeria programme.

2026-09-21-rwa-taarifa-ingabire-cross-bo.summary: Speaking in New York ahead of the UN General Assembly, Rwanda's ICT minister Paula Ingabire said African countries need digital systems that work across borders if they are to benefit from technology and AI. She argued that separate national systems limit how far data, services and businesses can move across the continent.

2026-09-21-sdn-dabanga-cbos-strategy-dig.summary: An analysis of the Central Bank of Sudan's 2026–2030 strategic plan, published in December 2025, which includes speeding up digital transformation in the banking system. Banker Omar Sid Ahmed argues that with about 98% of the money supply outside the banks and branches lost to the war, the plan needs a 12-month emergency programme with budgets and measurable targets. He adds that digital projects depend on infrastructure that is not yet in place.

2026-09-21-sle-calabash-ai-strategy-auth.summary: An opinion column by Gleb Tsipursky arguing that Sierra Leone's first national AI strategy, which the communications ministry is drafting with the World Bank, should limit what AI agents are allowed to do. He proposes minimum access rights, identities for machines, human approval before consequential actions, and testing before deployment.

2026-09-21-som-sonna-id-control-training.summary: Officers from Somalia's identity authority, immigration agency and criminal investigation department are taking part in a joint course with Kenyan immigration in Nairobi from 21 to 25 September 2026. It is the third such course and covers document examination, identity checks and facial comparison. Norway's migration partnership supports it.

2026-09-21-subtelforum-ace-cable-ciena-3.summary: The consortium behind the 17,000 km Africa Coast to Europe submarine cable has chosen Ciena's WaveLogic 6 Extreme optics to raise its total capacity above 30 Tb/s, Ciena said on 21 September 2026. The upgrade keeps the existing equipment at ACE's 18 landing stations, which serve more than 20 countries, and adds new transmission gear. No completion date was given.

2026-09-21-swz-independent-eptc-loan-tax.summary: Eswatini's House of Assembly took the second reading of three bills on 21 September 2026 financing the US$65 million World Bank Digital Eswatini Project. MPs focused on the US$26 million (about E455 million) loan to the state telecoms company EPTC, which the government would guarantee. The finance minister said that loan pays for EPTC's financial stabilisation and a change in its pension scheme, repayable from 2034 to 2051; the other two facilities fund broadband to Tinkhundla centres, schools and clinics, online government services, digital ID, payments and skills training. The bills now go to committee.

2026-09-21-swz-observer-eswatini-payment.summary: The Central Bank of Eswatini says the fast-payments service of the Eswatini Payment Switch now links banks and mobile-money providers in real time at any hour, with QR-code payments to merchants being built next. Speaking at Tourism Nkwe 2026 in Mbabane, a deputy director said open banking and a domestic card switch will follow. Links to other countries come at a later stage.

2026-09-21-swz-positivenews-mps-back-dig.summary: Eswatini MPs spoke in support of the three World Bank facilities, together worth US$65 million (about E1.14 billion), that fund the Digital Eswatini Project, at the bills' second reading. The debate is summarised under the Eswatini Independent's report.

2026-09-21-techafricanews-egypt-nti-4dt.summary: Egypt's National Telecommunications Institute agreed with digital-twin and automation firm 4DT.io, in Cairo on 19 September 2026, to train young people in digital transformation and automation. The programmes will mix classroom teaching, hands-on training and project work. No intake, length, cost or certification was stated.

2026-09-21-techafricanews-sa-online-shop.summary: The Online Retail in South Africa 2026 report finds 79.1% of adults online but only 34.2% shopping online in 2025, down from 36.6% in 2024, while online retail turnover rose to about R130 billion. The gap is widest among lower-income consumers and women. Delivery costs, weak last-mile service outside the cities and worries about payment security are named as barriers.

2026-09-21-techcabal-local-stablecoins-u.summary: An analysis arguing that stablecoins tied to African currencies have a weak case for retail use, because mobile money and bank transfers already work at home. It sees more promise in wholesale use and currency exchange on the blockchain. It gives supply as of 21 September 2026: about R74.6 million of ZARP in circulation and more than ₦3.75 billion of cNGN.

2026-09-21-techcabal-nigeria-device-mana.summary: A feature on how the NCC's Device Management System, which requires every SIM-enabled phone to be registered by IMEI before sale or connection, could raise phone prices. Importers, traders and repair shops fear the validation fee and compliance costs will be passed to buyers. The NCC says the registry records device data but gives it no access to the contents of phones.

2026-09-21-telecomreview-ericsson-vodafo.summary: Vodafone Egypt has started commercial rollout of Ericsson's AI-capable RAN Processor 6672, making Egypt one of the first markets after Japan. The unit runs AI at each radio site rather than centrally, and Ericsson claims it gives up to four times the processing capacity for less than half the energy. No number of sites, contract value or timetable was given.

2026-09-21-wearetech-sonar-orange-money-.summary: Insurer SONAR Assurance and Orange Money Burkina Faso signed a partnership in Ouagadougou on 18 September 2026 so clients can take out policies, pay premiums and check their contracts by phone. Orange Money says it has about 100,000 points of sale in the country. The exact terms of access have not yet been set.

2026-09-21-xgl-fortune-un-dialogue-safe-.summary: An opinion piece by the two co-leads on safe and secure AI at the first UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance, held in Geneva in July. They ask the UN to take steps with no downside now: a formal link between its scientific panel on AI and the negotiations before next May, and a common safety baseline built on existing frameworks such as the OECD principles and the Hiroshima code.

2026-09-21-zaf-africatechsummit-vea-capi.summary: VEA Capital Partners, the investment arm of VEA Group, has bought a stake of undisclosed size in Bonisa Applied Insights. Bonisa is a South African data science and AI firm that combines credit bureau data with other data sources for credit scoring, fraud modelling and lending decisions. The stated plan is to sell decisioning as a service and take it into new markets.

2026-09-21-zaf-businessday-sita-boss-reb.summary: An interview with Magatho Mello, managing director of South Africa's State Information Technology Agency since April and its first permanent head since late 2023. He wants to retire old systems, build shared platforms that serve several departments, and simplify tendering for start-ups. A ministerial report in July had set out governance and procurement failures at the agency over 2020–25.

2026-09-21-zaf-govza-malatsi-national-di.summary: Opening GovTech 2026 in Durban on 21 September 2026, South Africa's communications minister Solly Malatsi said government digital systems are still fragmented and that the first phase of the Digital Transformation Roadmap ends in February 2027. He presented digital sovereignty as a matter of development rather than security. He also said he had discussed with Operation Vulindlela and the Digital Council making the country a hub for submarine cables and digital infrastructure.

2026-09-21-zaf-itweb-mission-mobile-r500.summary: Johannesburg start-up Mission Mobile, which finances smartphones and connectivity through operators' stores, says it has secured R500 million from DN Invest, drawn from DNI's own funds and dedicated debt facilities. The date of the commitment was not given. Its Beam platform uses data on how people earn and spend to offer phones to prepaid customers, who account for over 80% of South African mobile connections.

2026-09-22-bujeti-financial-management-t.summary: Nigerian finance-software company Bujeti launched more than 15 integrations with banking, payment and accounting tools, among them Stripe, Paystack and QuickBooks, to automate invoicing, collections and bookkeeping.

2026-09-22-egypt-nti-al-riyada-universit.summary: Egypt's National Telecommunication Institute signed a protocol with Al-Riyada University for Science and Technology to train its students and graduates in NTI's technology programmes and to cooperate on research.

2026-09-22-egypt-nvidia-ai-cooperation-s.summary: Egypt's communications minister Raafat Hendy met an NVIDIA delegation to discuss cooperation on AI, data science, training-of-trainers programmes and support for start-ups. No agreement was announced.

2026-09-22-egyptian-gazette-ict-minister.summary: Egypt's communications minister Raafat Hendy said a national data centre strategy will be launched by the end of 2026, opening the FDC Summit in Cairo. He also set a target of 400 services on the Digital Egypt platform by 2030, through wider digital identity, e-signature and digital mail.

2026-09-22-geopol-usembassy-australia-on.summary: The US government's submission to Australia's consultation on its Digital Duty of Care online-safety bill argues against rules that would restrict protected speech, mandate product design or widen litigation risk for American platforms. It is a direct statement of the US position on how far other states may regulate US technology companies.

2026-09-22-gha-gna-ai-regulation-without.summary: Ghana's communications minister Samuel Nartey George said the government will regulate the risks and harms of AI rather than experimentation, separating low-risk student use from high-risk systems such as credit decisions. He spoke at the Pan African AI and Innovation Summit in Accra.

2026-09-22-itweb-africa-kenya-targets-ai.summary: Kenya's Principal Secretary for Broadcasting and Telecommunications, Steven Isaboke, said at a forum held with the World Bank that the government's focus is shifting from AI policy to measurable gains in jobs, productivity and public services.

2026-09-22-itweb-africa-us-backs-african.summary: The US International Development Finance Corporation said it intends to invest US$155 million in WIOCC Group, joining Africa Finance Corporation and Vision Invest as investors. The announcement followed an AFC roundtable in New York during the UN General Assembly; WIOCC operates in more than 30 African countries.

2026-09-22-kenya-ca-finalise-commercial-.summary: Kenya's Communications Authority invited stakeholders to validate its draft guidelines for commercial internet telephony services, after reviewing responses to an earlier consultation. The guidelines set the technical and operational terms for rolling out such services.

2026-09-22-kenya-ict-authority-digital-l.summary: The ICT Authority's account of the same Nyeri rollout adds that more than 62,000 teachers nationally have already been trained under the Digital Literacy Programme.

2026-09-22-kenya-intel-ai-literacy-publi.summary: Kenya's State Department of ICT signed a partnership with Intel at the UN General Assembly to teach AI literacy through public libraries. It will run through the Kenya National Library Service and the Mandela AI Hub Foundation under Intel's AI for Citizens programme.

2026-09-22-kenya-smart-boards-178-junior.summary: Kenya began delivering smart boards and teacher laptops to 178 public junior schools in Nyeri County on 21 September, under phase II of the Digital Literacy Programme. The programme is funded through the World Bank-supported Kenya Digital Economy Acceleration Project and is to reach all 377 junior schools in the county.

2026-09-22-kredete-acquires-gravv-nigeri.summary: Nigerian financial platform Kredete acquired Gravv, bringing in stablecoin-based technology that connects banks and local payment systems. Kredete says the aim is cheaper and faster international transfers; no price was given.

2026-09-22-lbr-newdawn-gongloe-national-.summary: Liberian lawyer and politician Tiawan Gongloe urged the legislature to scrutinise the proposed concession for the National Identification System before ratifying it. He asked whether Austria's OeSD would provide only technical support or take over state functions, and raised jobs, revenue and the protection of biometric data.

2026-09-22-nga-ngcert-ransomware-phobos-.summary: Nigeria's national CERT warned of rising Phobos ransomware attacks on cloud service providers whose clients include government agencies, banks and telecoms operators. It rates the damage critical and the probability high, and sets out mitigations.

2026-09-22-rwanda-mou-chipmango-semicond.summary: Rwanda's Ministry of ICT and Innovation signed a memorandum of understanding with ChipMango to build local semiconductor design skills. It followed talks between Minister of State Yves Iradukunda and the company on a national chip-design talent pipeline.

2026-09-22-sita-recovery-mode-comms-mini.summary: Communications minister Solly Malatsi told GovTech 2026 in Durban that the State IT Agency is recovering under stable leadership and must now deliver on digitising government services and ending fragmented systems. The conference ran under the theme of South African digital sovereignty.

2026-09-22-south-africa-zaru-stablecoin-.summary: A second report of the ZARU launch on Arc adds how trades settle: the ZARU/USDC pair clears through StableFX's request-for-quote engine, with both legs settling together or not at all, which is meant to remove counterparty risk from rand foreign exchange.

2026-09-22-standard-bank-stellenbosch-re.summary: Standard Bank and Stellenbosch University's School for Data Science and Computational Thinking are developing a framework for responsible AI use in business, announced at a panel in Cape Town.

2026-09-22-techafricanews-mastercard-wal.summary: Mastercard launched Wallet Pay, a set of services letting digital wallets accept contactless, QR and online payments across its network. MTN and AXIAN are among the launch partners, alongside Alipay+ and others.

2026-09-22-techcabal-safaricom-hits-1-mi.summary: Safaricom became the first Kenyan provider to pass one million fixed broadband subscribers, with 1,024,950 at the end of June 2026 according to the Communications Authority, a 36.1% market share. The report argues that the volume-led growth is straining margins.

2026-09-22-techcabal-south-africas-bank-.summary: App-only Bank Zero recorded its first break-even month in August 2026, five years after opening, with 275,000 direct customers and about 500,000 more through partner platforms. Its CEO put the cost of building its own platform at under R300 million, against an estimated R3 billion to buy one.

2026-09-22-techcabal-tanzania-regulator-.summary: Tanzania's Fair Competition Commission put KCB Group's stake in Kenyan payments firm Pesapal at 22.23%, the first public figure for a deal KCB announced in 2025 without terms. The stake gives KCB indirect control of Pesapal Tanzania and is under the commission's review; its value is undisclosed.

2026-09-22-unitel-revenue-rises-17-perce.summary: Angolan operator UNITEL reported first-half 2026 revenue of 274 billion kwanzas, up 17%, with EBITDA of 91 billion kwanzas and net income of 66.3 billion. Subscribers passed 21.2 million, data use rose 43% and the network reached 12,302 base stations.

2026-09-22-verto-visa-multi-currency-cor.summary: Payments platform Verto and Visa launched the Verto Card, a corporate card for African businesses that funds and settles in 11 currencies with no FX markup on eligible ones and indirect access to 160 more. It runs on Visa's commercial rails rather than prepaid rails, which Verto blames for declined cross-border payments.

2026-09-22-zambia-mytochondria-ai-satell.summary: Zambian start-up Mytochondria, co-founded in 2023 by data scientist Thomas Fred Lungu, uses satellite imagery and AI to assess soil quality, moisture and temperature for farmers. The profile presents it as a response to climate shocks hitting harvests in southern Africa.

2026-09-22-zaru-goes-live-circle-arc-blo.summary: ZAR Universal (ZARU), a rand stablecoin issued by BlockTower under a Financial Sector Conduct Authority licence, went live on Circle's Arc blockchain and opened as a founding currency pair on Circle StableFX. Each token is backed by one rand held in South Africa, with reserves managed by Sanlam Specialised Asset Management; Luno, EasyEquities and Lesaka are partners in its development.

2026-09-22-zwe-technomag-africa-data-pro.summary: Zimbabwe's regulator POTRAZ, which acts as the country's data protection authority, marked the first Africa Data Protection Day on 21 September. The day commemorates the 2016 founding of the Network of African Data Protection Authorities, which now has 34 members and in which POTRAZ is second vice-president.

2026-09-23-ago-forum-lusophone-gouvernan.summary: Angola's information-society institute is hosting the Lusophone Internet Governance Forum in Luanda on 23 and 24 September, bringing together experts from Portuguese-speaking countries on digital transformation, online safety and the digital divide.

2026-09-23-ben-rwa-explorent-cooperation.summary: Benin's digital minister Mahuna Akplogan and Rwanda's ICT minister Paula Ingabire discussed AI cooperation in agriculture, health and education on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, including infrastructure, data access, skills and joint research. No agreement or specific project was announced.

2026-09-23-bfa-lefaso-arcep-aes-conventi.summary: The telecoms regulators of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger are to sign a cooperation agreement in Ouagadougou on 25 September creating a Sahel Regulators' Council. It covers roaming within the Alliance of Sahel States, consumer protection, cybersecurity, spectrum, mutual recognition of type-approved equipment and joint positions in international bodies.

2026-09-23-bfa-lefaso-ecole-langue-ia-so.summary: In an opinion piece timed to the SIST 2026 science symposium in Ouagadougou, sociolinguist Mamadou Lamine Sanogo of Burkina Faso's CNRST argues that schooling and AI must be built on African languages, data and indigenous knowledge. He presents this as the condition for scientific and digital sovereignty.

2026-09-23-botswana-bofinet-internationa.summary: Botswana Fibre Networks signed a long-term international capacity lease with an unnamed South African partner, raising capacity through the Ramatlabama and Pioneer Gate border crossings from 300 Gbit/s to 1 Tbit/s.

2026-09-23-cedeao-aip-adapt-data-protect.summary: At the same Dakar conference, digital-governance expert Janet Gbam said the 2010 ECOWAS Supplementary Act on personal data no longer covers AI, algorithmic decision-making or the right to erasure. She named Senegal, Ghana, Nigeria and Cabo Verde as ahead on legislation and regulators, with other member states constrained by capacity.

2026-09-23-cedeao-court-justice-digital-.summary: At a Dakar conference, law lecturer Jake Okechukwu Effoduh argued that the ECOWAS Court already has the legal basis to hear digital-rights cases, from internet shutdowns to biometric surveillance, without a new treaty. A Bissau law professor noted that Guinea-Bissau still has no data-protection law or authority, though a bill would create one.

2026-09-23-cod-claude-assistant-ia-anthr.summary: DR Congo's Ministry of Digital Economy announced on 22 September that Anthropic's Claude is now officially available in the country, both the consumer service and commercial API access. Users had previously reached it through VPNs; the communiqué gave no terms.

2026-09-23-eac-igad-eardip-regional-digi.summary: The EAC, IGAD and the World Bank are holding a three-day workshop in Nairobi (22 to 24 September) with Djibouti, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia and South Sudan to align national projects under the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project. It covers cross-border broadband, digital public infrastructure, cybersecurity cooperation and digital trade; Kenya takes part through its own World Bank-funded KDEAP.

2026-09-23-egy-ahramonline-kemet-data-ce.summary: Egypt's communications minister met INTRO Investment Holding to review the Kemet data centre in the Suez Canal Economic Zone's Sokhna industrial zone, planned as the zone's first Tier III facility at 80 MW. The project is put at USD 1.2 billion, with USD 270 million for phase one; no timeline was disclosed.

2026-09-23-egy-youm7-smart-courts-justic.summary: Youm7 surveys Egypt's Ministry of Justice programme to move courts off paper: digitised case files and archives, remote litigation in some circuits, automated queueing, and systems that transcribe audio recordings of hearings into written minutes. It also points to training for judges and staff through the National Center for Judicial Studies and to legislation on electronic procedure and personal-data protection.

2026-09-23-enterpriseam-instapay-papss-e.summary: Afreximbank plans to connect the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) to Egypt's InstaPay, and six unnamed Egyptian banks have applied to the Central Bank of Egypt for integration approval, PAPSS's chief executive said. InstaPay does not yet handle cross-border payments, so a gateway has still to be built; no launch date was given.

2026-09-23-gha-gna-data-protection-boss-.summary: Ghana Data Protection Commission head Arnold Kavaarpuo called for African privacy and competition regulators to act together against big-tech concentration, and presented NADPA's draft model policy on cross-border data transfers, which sets six lawful transfer routes. He said 44 of 55 AU member states have data-protection laws, 38 with operational regulators.

2026-09-23-gha-myjoyonline-dvlaverify-ap.summary: Ghana's Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority released its DVLAverify biometric identity-verification app on Apple's App Store and opened a web version usable from any computer with a webcam. Vehicle-registration applicants can now complete identity checks remotely.

2026-09-23-gha-myjoyonline-gra-itas-digi.summary: The Ghana Revenue Authority said its Integrated Tax Administration System is to be linked to customs (ICUMS), the companies registrar, SSNIT, the Bank of Ghana, Ghana.gov, the Lands Commission and the National Identification Authority. Some capabilities are live, with return pre-population and further automation to follow in stages.

2026-09-23-gha-tvet-unesco-kpmg-microsof.summary: Ghana's TVET Service signed a memorandum with UNESCO, KPMG and Microsoft under the AI EmpowerED initiative to train at least 100,000 technical and vocational instructors in AI and digital skills. No cost or timeline was given.

2026-09-23-gmb-thepoint-land-lease-digit.summary: The Gambia's Lands Minister told the National Assembly that lease documents will be issued within three days once the ministry's World Bank-supported digital system is fully running, with contracts already awarded. The ministry is clearing about 50 lease files a week from a backlog in which some had waited three to five years.

2026-09-23-gnb-ang-transformacao-digital.summary: Bissau's municipal council launched CMB+, its integrated modernisation and digital transformation project, on 22 September, including a municipal portal for access to council services. The territorial administration minister spoke at the launch.

2026-09-23-internetsociety-au-ai-governa.summary: The African Union Commission is holding an open online consultation on 23 and 24 September on its draft Guidelines on AI Governance and Regulation, which implement the 2024 Continental AI Strategy. Day two covers regulation, security and standards, including the AU Model AI Law; written submissions are accepted until 30 September.

2026-09-23-ken-standard-kenya-anthropic-.summary: Kenya signed a Joint Declaration with Anthropic in New York during UNGA 81, covering AI applications in education and health, research, capacity building, and AI safety and evaluation. The next step is to develop specific pilots and institutional partnerships with government agencies.

2026-09-23-lbr-cybastion-women-digital-b.summary: Liberia's gender ministry signed an agreement with Cybastion, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, for women's technology and business hubs with childcare: a Monrovia campus and regional sites in Voinjama, Gbarnga, Kakata and Buchanan. Training is to run through Cisco's Networking Academy; no cost or timetable was given.

2026-09-23-lbr-fpa-cdc-cybercrime-law-su.summary: Liberia's opposition CDC says it will ask the Supreme Court to rule on the constitutionality of the Cybercrime Act of 2025. The move follows the court-ordered release on 22 September of commentator Jerry Nyantee Wrato, whom police intended to prosecute under the Act over AI-generated images of the Vice President.

2026-09-23-lby-libyaherald-unified-trade.summary: The Libya Trade Network met international shipping agents and the Libyan Ports Company to review the mandatory Unified Trade System (PTS) for vessel arrival notices and cargo manifests. Priorities are finishing testing of XML shipment-data transmission and completing roll-out at Tripoli and Al-Khoms ports.

2026-09-23-moz-incm-consultants-modernis.summary: Mozambique's regulator INCM has called for expressions of interest (ref. INCM/SC/95/2026) for a six-month study of the postal market and a transformation strategy and roadmap, with particular attention to the designated operator CORREIOS. The scope includes digital transformation, postal financial services and e-commerce.

2026-09-23-moz-partenariat-public-prive-.summary: Mozambique's ICT institute INTIC signed a memorandum with Kamaleon, a rural mobile-multimedia provider, on 21 September to run digital-literacy, cybersecurity and data-protection campaigns in rural communities. Content is to be produced in Portuguese and, where possible, Mozambican languages, alongside joint studies of digital-literacy levels.

2026-09-23-nga-mtn-gates-foundation-mate.summary: MTN Group Foundation and the Gates Foundation launched the Nigeria Maternal Health Multiplier, combining AI-enabled phone-based decision support for health workers and mothers with subsidised smartphones and data and better clinic connectivity. By 2030 it aims to reach 500,000 women, 5,000 frontline workers and 500 facilities.

2026-09-23-nga-nitda-seeks-global-partne.summary: NITDA's director-general joined a Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy meeting at Purdue with US State and Commerce Department officials, the DFC and firms including Google, Visa and Africell. NITDA presented Nigeria as a destination for technology investment and called for partnerships with measurable outcomes; no agreements were announced.

2026-09-23-nga-thisdaylive-nimc-identity.summary: Nigeria's National Identity Management Commission denied claims in a social-media video that NIN and other personal data had been breached and put up for sale. Its director-general ordered an investigation into whether any tokenisation verification agents breached their licences; no findings or timeline were given.

2026-09-23-nga-vanguard-edoicta-internet.summary: Edo State ICT Agency head Eghosa Urhoghide said the state has replaced a foreign-owned e-governance platform, on which it paid licence fees, with its own, and has brought all 128 ministries, departments and agencies onto it. Certificate of Occupancy applications are now made and signed online, and joint inspections are being used to cut fibre right-of-way charges.

2026-09-23-nga-vanguard-nitda-unga81-inc.summary: At a UNGA 81 high-level dialogue, NITDA director-general Kashifu Inuwa called for AI that reflects local languages and contexts and gives citizens agency rather than only access. He set out four pillars of Nigeria's AI strategy (Connect, Skill, Compute and Create), including sovereign cloud and AI capability.

2026-09-23-nigeria-truecaller-court-ruli.summary: A Lagos High Court ruled on 14 September that Truecaller cannot rely on one user's consent to process the phone numbers of contacts who never used the app, in a case brought by the Data Privacy Lawyers Association under the Nigeria Data Protection Act. It nevertheless denied damages to those affected for want of proof of concrete harm.

2026-09-23-nilepost-uganda-cyber-fraud-i.summary: The Uganda Bankers' Association counted 6,533 cyber and fraud incidents in the financial sector from January to August 2026, with UGX 24 billion lost and a further UGX 68 billion estimated at risk. At the same forum the Deputy Chief Justice said the judiciary is open to specialised handling of cyber and financial crime.

2026-09-23-rwa-newtimes-eac-payment-syst.summary: The East African Legislative Assembly's Accounts Committee began a five-day oversight visit in Uganda (21 to 25 September) on integration of the EAC's payment and settlement systems. Members will examine interoperability, transaction costs and processing times, and report to EAC organs and Partner States.

2026-09-23-sen-seneweb-mobile-money-paie.summary: Seneweb argues Senegal's digital-payments market is no longer an Orange Money-Wave duopoly: under the BCEAO's January 2024 payment-services instruction, licensed payment institutions can now run payment services without being banks or e-money issuers. Of 31 such institutions licensed in the WAEMU by end-February 2026, 11 were in Senegal.

2026-09-23-sen-validates-national-bluepr.summary: Senegal's digital ministry validated a draft national Blueprint on Data Valorisation at a workshop on 21 and 22 September, run with Smart Africa's Data Governance in Africa programme and GIZ. Senegal is a pilot alongside Kenya and Lesotho; the workshop refined the roadmap's implementation and monitoring framework, with no finalisation date given.

2026-09-23-sonna-somalia-eastern-africa-.summary: Somalia's state news agency reports its part in the EAC-IGAD-World Bank regional digital integration workshop in Nairobi (see the EAC entry under this heading), noting the National Communications Authority's cybersecurity law and incident-response centre and Mogadishu University's new degree in cybersecurity and AI.

2026-09-23-swz-independentnews-govt-syst.summary: Eswatini's ICT ministry acknowledged outages across government online services, including elderly grants, e-Visa, road permits, scholarships, deeds registration and the IFMIS, without giving a cause. It did not confirm a reported breach at the Royal Science and Technology Park, home of the National Data Centre, or a reported EUR 1 million ransom demand.

2026-09-23-tcd-ndjampost-etat-civil-anat.summary: N'Djamena's town hall and Chad's secure-documents agency ANATS signed a memorandum on 23 September to digitise and secure civil registration, with support from the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie. The work covers digitising registers, staff training and a secure link between the town hall's systems and ANATS's integrated population register.

2026-09-23-zaf-sovereignty-govt-digital-.summary: At GovTech 2026 in Durban, SITA board chair Stella Bvuma framed digital sovereignty as control over where public data sits, who can reach it and how services survive a supplier or network failure. She reported that SITA spent R183 million with SMEs in the first four months of 2026/27, 49% of available procurement spend against a 45% target.

2026-09-23-zaf-uct-r101m-ai-microscopy-a.summary: The University of Cape Town launched openScopes AIDDiA, a four-year, Wellcome Trust-funded programme worth GBP 4.4 million (about R101 million) pairing open-source microscopy with machine-learning image analysis for research on TB, malaria and other infectious diseases. Partners are KEMRI, Uganda's Mbarara University, Côte d'Ivoire's CSRS and Imperial College London.

2026-09-24-africa-ai-disability-data-hai.summary: A Hub for AI and Disability Inclusion (HAIDI), hosted by KNUST's Responsible AI Lab, and an African Disability Data Network were launched at the Global Data Festival in Nairobi with backing from IDRC, the UK FCDO and AI4D. They plan to map disability-related datasets, build three new datasets, assess how national AI strategies treat disability and fund three startups with grants of up to KES 5 million.

2026-09-24-civ-emerging-technologies-dig.summary: Launching Ivoire Tech Forum 2026, to be held in Abidjan on 11-13 November, digital minister Djibril Ouattara announced a startup labelling platform that will give labelled startups access to the country's fiscal incentives. He also named connectivity, administrative digitalisation and digital skills as priorities.

2026-09-24-cpv-ugpe-review-meeting-digit.summary: A World Bank mission reviewed the Digital Cabo Verde project between 22 and 26 September, reporting about 80% disbursement of the original US$20 million financing (2020-2025) and about 40% of the US$20 million additional financing (2025-2028). School connectivity was named the priority for the additional financing, with stronger coordination across ministries and a clearer role for the DGTED.

2026-09-24-egy-moneyhash-geidea-payment-.summary: Payment orchestration platform MoneyHash partnered with payments provider Geidea, giving businesses already integrated with MoneyHash access to Geidea's online gateway and payment methods in Egypt, the UAE and Saudi Arabia without a separate connection.

2026-09-24-eth-ena-unga81-digital-financ.summary: Ethiopia and UNCDF held a side event at UNGA81 presenting digital payments, the Fayda national ID and digital public infrastructure as tools for financial inclusion and the SDGs. Planning minister Fitsum Assefa cited Digital Ethiopia 2030, the National Financial Inclusion Strategy, interoperable payments and BRIDGE 2030.

2026-09-24-eth-her-cybertracks-women-cyb.summary: Nearly 50 women cybersecurity professionals from across Africa met in Addis Ababa for the Her CyberTracks Regional Training Africa 2026. The programme is funded by Germany, the European Commission and Italy and delivered by the ITU and GIZ with UNODC's Global Programme on Cybercrime.

2026-09-24-gha-gmb-nca-pura-benchmarking.summary: Ghana's National Communications Authority is hosting a delegation from The Gambia's Public Utilities Regulatory Authority for a benchmarking visit from 22 to 25 September, PURA's second this year. The visit covers regulatory governance, consumer protection, dispute resolution, quality-of-service indicators and broadcasting.

2026-09-24-gha-myjoyonline-intel-ai-for-.summary: Ghana signed an agreement with Intel on the sidelines of UNGA81 to expand the AI for Youth programme into K-12 schools, with Coral Reef and the Ministry of Education as partners. The gender minister signed on behalf of the First Lady; no value or timeline was given.

2026-09-24-ifc-airtel-money-2026-90m-sta.summary: Airtel Money, Airtel Africa's mobile money arm in 13 markets, filed for a London Stock Exchange listing in which existing shareholders sell shares, aiming to raise about US$800 million at a valuation of US$8-9 billion. The IFC agreed to buy up to GBP 67.2 million (about US$90 million) of shares at the offer price.

2026-09-24-ken-biznakenya-coop-bank-uncd.summary: Co-operative Bank of Kenya and UNCDF launched a US$900,000 loan portfolio guarantee under the DigiKen programme, backing up to US$1.8 million of lending to fintechs, digital credit providers, e-commerce and digitally enabled small firms, and innovation hubs. UNCDF covers 50% of outstanding principal, rising to 70% for borrowers in the Arid and Semi-Arid Lands.

2026-09-24-ken-childrens-rights-ai-roadm.summary: President Ruto co-hosted the launch of a 2026-2027 Roadmap for Children's Rights and Protection in the Age of AI at the UN General Assembly, alongside the leaders of France, Spain and Australia. Kenya's technology envoy Philip Thigo said Kenya would take the work forward at home, across Africa and globally.

2026-09-24-ken-cross-border-digital-publ.summary: ICT Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo proposed that willing African Union member states jointly pilot one cross-border public service and report back by February 2027. He made the proposal at an AUC-Google ministerial roundtable in New York, pointing to eCitizen's more than 22,500 services and Kenya's Government Interoperability Framework.

2026-09-24-ken-mcaai-dholuo-speech-data-.summary: The Maseno Centre for Applied Artificial Intelligence ran a preparatory visit to Suba ahead of collecting Dholuo speech data to improve the language's representation in AI systems, onboarding participants to its SmartVoice app. The work involves the ACTS-AI4D team.

2026-09-24-ken-pulse-co-ke-anthropic-ai-.summary: Kenya and Anthropic signed a Joint Declaration in New York on 22 September covering AI skills, research, responsible public-sector use, AI safety and evaluation, and applications in education and health. Pilots, research and training with Kenyan institutions are to follow, governed by Kenyan law including on data protection and cybersecurity.

2026-09-24-kenya-kenswitch-domestic-card.summary: Kenswitch, Kenya's largest independent payments switch, launched a domestic card scheme on 22 September that lets banks and other institutions issue physical and virtual cards on its network of more than 2,200 ATMs, 50,000 point-of-sale terminals and 80,000 agent outlets. It named no issuers, launch dates or pricing against Visa and Mastercard.

2026-09-24-lbr-thenewdawn-justice-minist.summary: Nimba County Senator Nya Twayen asked Liberia's Justice Ministry to publish enforcement guidelines for the Cybercrime Act of 2025, including clear charging thresholds, to protect free expression and due process. His call follows the arrest and four charges under the Act against Jerry Nyantee Wrato over allegedly manipulated content about the Vice President; Wrato was later freed after court intervention.

2026-09-24-nga-data-protection-digital-i.summary: At UNGA81, Nigeria Data Protection Commission head Vincent Olatunji said personal data used in social protection programmes and social registers must follow the safeguards of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, and called for African datasets built with proper rights protections. Communications minister Bosun Tijani cited the BRIDGE broadband project, which he said is expected to reach more than 20 million Nigerians.

2026-09-24-nga-ngcert-whatsapp-vulnerabi.summary: Nigeria's national CERT issued a critical advisory on two WhatsApp flaws (CVE-2026-23866 and CVE-2026-23863) on iOS, Android and Windows that allow malicious links to run from crafted Instagram Reels messages and attachments to be spoofed. It advised updating the app, including forced updates through mobile device management.

2026-09-24-nga-nuran-wireless-starlink-b.summary: NuRAN Wireless will pilot Starlink low-Earth-orbit satellite backhaul at a rural site in Nigeria with its partner Infratel, its first LEO integration, to test capacity, 4G migration and site costs. The satellite service is bought through third-party providers; NuRAN has no direct contract with Starlink or SpaceX.

2026-09-24-nga-von-ndpc-olatunji-africa-.summary: In a keynote at a Vivacity Development event on the sidelines of UNGA81, Nigeria Data Protection Commission head Vincent Olatunji named regulatory alignment, data sovereignty and trust as the three foundations of Africa's digital economy. He argued for compatible data-protection rules across African jurisdictions and described data governance as economic infrastructure.

2026-09-24-nigeria-ufarmx-agri-credit-da.summary: A TechCabal feature profiles UfarmX, founded by Alexander Zanders in Oyo State, which turns farm data into credit ratings used by commercial banks and retailers rather than lending itself. The company says it has facilitated more than US$6.8 million in trade across over 10,000 farmers in Nigeria, Senegal and Liberia.

2026-09-24-sen-beninwebtv-daf-cyberattac.summary: The director of Senegal's file-automation department (DAF), Ibrahima Dieng, confirmed that the February 2026 incident which halted national identity-card production was a cyberattack, but said the identity-card and electoral files were intact and no personal data was compromised. The Interior Ministry had earlier called it only an incident; a group's claim to have taken 139 terabytes of biometric and immigration data remains unverified.

2026-09-24-sen-digital-ministry-sonatel-.summary: After a week-long workshop, Senegal's digital ministry and Sonatel set out a package of initiatives for Sonatel's contribution to the New Deal Technologique, covering infrastructure, e-government, the digital economy and services for citizens and businesses. Minister Samba Diouf asked other operators, banks, fintechs and startups to bring forward contributions of their own, with timelines and monitoring.

2026-09-24-swz-positivenews-change-readi.summary: About 40 change agents from five ministries and parastatals held a change-readiness workshop in Mbabane on 24 September, assessing their own directorates ahead of implementation of the World Bank-financed Digital Eswatini Project (US$65 million, about E1.06 billion). They are to help public servants adjust to the new digital systems.

2026-09-24-tcd-wearetech-ndjamena-civil-.summary: English-language report of the same N'Djamena civil-registry digitisation launch and ANATS memorandum of 23 September. It adds that an earlier OIF-backed project regularised the civil status of 53,000 children in Tandjile and Ennedi Est in 2024 and 2025.

2026-09-24-tchad-ndjamena-numerisation-e.summary: N'Djamena's municipality launched a project on 23 September, backed by the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie, to digitise and secure its civil registers, and signed a memorandum with the secure-documents agency ANATS to link municipal records to the national identification system. ANATS counted more than 623,000 school-age children without a birth certificate in 2023.

2026-09-24-uga-airtel-starlink-satellite.summary: Airtel Uganda launched Starlink satellite-to-mobile service, giving compatible smartphones SMS and light data such as WhatsApp outside terrestrial coverage, free for a 30-day trial and then through data bundles. Uganda is Airtel Africa's second commercial market for the service after the DRC in August.

2026-09-24-undp-africa-ai-crossroads-blo.summary: A UNDP Africa blog argues that AI adoption is a set of development choices about institutions, markets and rights, drawing on 26 AI Landscape Assessments completed between 2024 and 2026. It finds that readiness does not end when implementation starts, and links the work to the African Union's Continental AI Strategy.

2026-09-24-xaf-gmb-cioafrica-africa-plac.summary: At the African AI Governance Summit convened by Lawyers Hub in New York on 22 September, Gambian ambassador Muhammadou Kah urged Africa to co-design its technology and own its data rather than import both. He set out five markers: negotiate as one bloc, finance its own digital rails, co-author global AI rules, write rules with entrepreneurs and turn presence into influence.
