2026-09-24-xgl-mofcom-china-us-first-ai-.summary: China's commerce ministry said the eighth round of China-US trade consultations in New York included the first dialogue on artificial intelligence under the consultation mechanism, between Vice Premier He Lifeng and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. No outcome on AI was stated beyond continued communication.

2026-09-24-zaf-microsoft-digital-soverei.summary: At a GovTech breakfast for senior officials, Microsoft South Africa set out six dimensions of digital sovereignty: data, control, operational, AI, resilience and assurance. It presented sovereignty as a range of controls set by workload and regulatory risk rather than a yes-or-no choice, and pointed to its two Azure regions in South Africa.

2026-09-24-zwe-google-ai-digital-economy.summary: ICT minister Tatenda Mavetera said President Mnangagwa met Google senior vice president James Manyika on the sidelines of UNGA81 to deepen engagement on AI, digital skills, research and home-grown innovation. No agreement, funding or programme was announced.

2026-09-24-zwe-zse-invoicex-invoice-disc.summary: The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange opened InvoiceX, a regulated invoice-discounting market run under the Zimbabwe Entrepreneurship Exchange, for invoices of US$1,000 to US$1.5 million. Once a buyer authenticates an invoice, licensed banks and microfinance lenders bid on the discount rate, with supplier payment targeted within 48 hours and platform fees of 0.65% of the transaction.

2026-09-25-africa-web3-funding-lisk-exit.summary: Lisk, the Swiss Web3 company, is to shut its blockchain on 31 October and move its remaining products and developers to Celo, removing one of the few ecosystems still funding early-stage African Web3 founders, often with grants of about $4,000 in its own token. African blockchain companies raised $90.1 million across 28 deals in 2025, down 26.6% on the year before, according to Crypto Valley VC.

2026-09-25-ago-uae-space-cooperation-loi.summary: Angola's space programme office GGPEN and the UAE Space Agency signed a letter of intent on cooperation in the peaceful uses of outer space, covering space sciences, technologies and applications. It was signed in Abidjan on 25 September at the Africa Space Expo, where Angola is guest country of honour.

2026-09-25-burkina-faso-safa-airport-dig.summary: Burkina Faso's state airports company SAFA signed a memorandum with ACI Africa and Germany's Barthauer Software to pilot the SACOS airport certification and operations platform. The pilot covers runway inspections, certification, document management and safety tracking, before any wider roll-out.

2026-09-25-civ-space-digital-transformat.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's digital minister Djibril Ouattara told the Africa Space Expo in Abidjan on 24 September that satellite infrastructure should complement terrestrial networks to extend coverage, which he put at 95% nationally, towards a 100% target. A radiocommunications forum alongside the expo is addressing the integration of terrestrial and satellite networks.

2026-09-25-egy-ai-council-national-ai-st.summary: Egypt's National Council for AI adopted the first-half 2026 progress report on the National AI Strategy 2025-2030 and reviewed the outline of a National Quantum Computing Strategy 2027-2030. It also discussed guidelines on government AI procurement, generative AI in government and the safe use of AI applications by children.

2026-09-25-gab-gabonreview-archives-parl.summary: Gabon's National Assembly closed a two-day seminar on 24 September on managing, preserving and digitising parliamentary archives, held with the French Parliament under a parliamentary cooperation programme. It trained archive, IT and records staff and aimed to lay the basis of a document policy suited to digital transformation.

2026-09-25-gab-gabonreview-donnees-energ.summary: CEMAC energy ministers met in Libreville on a draft regulation creating a community energy information system (SIE-CEMAC), setting rules for collecting, processing, keeping and sharing energy data. Gabon's energy minister asked the African Energy Commission for technical and financial support and said the sharing of some energy data must be limited because it falls under national sovereignty.

2026-09-25-gab-sonapresse-drones-satelli.summary: At the first Gabon Drone Expo, Drone Hub's director-general Nicolas Adias said Gabon loses about €15 million a year to illegal logging and that near-permanent cloud cover limits optical satellite monitoring of forests and coastal waters. He presented drones, already used by the space observation agency AGEOS, as a way to fly under the clouds and give near real-time information.

2026-09-25-gha-myjoyonline-gcif-ai-phish.summary: The Ghana Cybersecurity Industry Forum, the industry body provided for under the Cybersecurity Act, 2020, warned at an Accra news conference that criminals are using AI to make phishing messages convincing. It named a skills shortage as its main challenge and set out student engagement, a virtual assets workshop and community roadshows for October to December 2026.

2026-09-25-gha-myjoyonline-prempeh-ai-el.summary: Opening the Third Electoral Integrity Summit in Accra, CDD-Ghana's executive director Henry Kwasi Prempeh called on African states to strengthen safeguards against AI-driven disinformation, deepfakes and coordinated manipulation of elections. He said the question is not whether to use these technologies but under what safeguards and who is accountable when they cause harm.

2026-09-25-gmb-information-commission-cs.summary: The Gambia's Information Commission and the UN system opened a three-day workshop on 23 September training civil society organisations on the Access to Information Act and the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, both of which the Commission implements.

2026-09-25-gnq-ahoraeg-inege-anuario-est.summary: Equatorial Guinea's statistics institute INEGE presented the ninth edition of the national Statistical Yearbook in Malabo, covering the last five years. It named stronger administrative registers, digitised processes and interoperable information systems as outstanding challenges, and announced a fifth population and housing census and a first agricultural census, with no dates.

2026-09-25-lbr-fpa-dara-digital-advocacy.summary: Ten Liberian civil society organisations, including CENTAL and the Liberia Equality Network, signed a memorandum establishing the Digital Advocacy and Rights Alliance (DARA). The coalition is to work on digital rights, privacy, online safety and digital freedoms.

2026-09-25-lbr-fpa-dopoh-cybercrime-enfo.summary: Senator Francis Dopoh, who chairs the Senate telecoms committee, defended the Cybercrime Act approved by President Boakai on 3 July 2026 as aimed at fraud, harassment and child exploitation rather than free speech. He called on the executive to designate critical national information infrastructure, set up a national cybersecurity centre and a 24/7 emergency response team, publish the Act's regulations within its six-to-twelve-month timeline and fund its implementation.

2026-09-25-lbr-fpa-wrato-detention-heari.summary: A Monrovia criminal court gave the police a last opportunity to justify holding Jerry Nyantee Wrato, a suspect under the Cybercrime Act, after no officer appeared for the second time. The judge found the state had not shown the case was lawfully before the court and postponed the habeas corpus hearing to 25 September.

2026-09-25-nga-thisdaylive-inec-ai-elect.summary: Nigeria's electoral commission INEC said it has begun using AI tools in its results-management process to flag discrepancies and errors in result records before final validation, with every automated check subject to human audit. Chairman Joash Amupitan said INEC has set up an AI Division and adopted an AI roadmap and governance framework ahead of the January and February 2027 elections.

2026-09-25-nga-thisdaylive-ondo-ai-civil.summary: Ondo State launched Ondo AI, a platform built by SmartApps IT Limited that automates civil-service personnel records, payroll, retirement processing and pension migration. It flags workers nearing retirement and gives staff self-service payslips.

2026-09-25-nga-thisdaylive-stakeholders-.summary: Bank and fintech executives at a Lagos forum on 24 September called on the Central Bank of Nigeria to extend and phase its 1 January 2027 deadline for hosting all payment data in Nigeria, calling it virtually impossible to meet. FCMB's technology chief said bank CIOs had been unable for three months to get clarity from the CBN on which data must be kept on-premise.

2026-09-25-nga-vanguard-ai-deepfakes-cyb.summary: The RACE Centre opened a two-day training in Abuja for the Feminist Digital Watch Collective on responding to technology-facilitated gender-based violence, including AI-generated deepfakes and cyberstalking. Its AI-enabled tracker, launched two months earlier, has documented about 24,000 human-verified cases across five social media platforms.

2026-09-25-nigeria-moniepoint-pos-invest.summary: Moniepoint is selling shares in the Dangote Petroleum Refinery's ₦2.15 trillion IPO through its agent point-of-sale terminals across all 774 local government areas. Buyers are identified by their Bank Verification Number and capped at ₦100,000 each, a test of the agent network as a channel for investment products.

2026-09-25-nigeria-remita-banking-app.summary: Remita launched a mobile app at Nigeria Fintech Week on 23 September that brings several bank accounts into one interface. Users can make payments, invest and send money to other African countries.

2026-09-25-rwa-ktpress-nsengiyumva-ai-go.summary: Prime Minister Justin Nsengiyumva told an AI governance discussion at UNGA81 that Rwanda's National AI Agency could host shared testing of advanced AI systems for the region, so African countries can evaluate frontier models themselves. No timetable, funding or partner countries were stated.

2026-09-25-rwa-newtimes-ai-scaling-healt.summary: Rwanda's ICT ministry hosted a session at UNGA81 on deploying AI at scale in health, agriculture, education and public services, presenting the country as a proof of concept for Africa, with partners including the Gates Foundation, Google, Zipline, Anthropic and UNICEF. The discussion covered the national AI agency, the national data hub and Kinyarwanda-language AI; no new commitment was reported.

2026-09-25-rwanda-jordan-digital-coopera.summary: Rwanda and Jordan signed a memorandum of understanding on ICT cooperation on the sidelines of UNGA81 on 24 September, between Rwanda's ICT minister Paula Ingabire and Jordan's digital economy minister Sami Smeirat. It covers sharing experience in digital public services, digital identity and AI and identifying joint projects.

2026-09-25-sajim-ai-delivery-acceptance-.summary: A systematic review of 42 studies on consumer acceptance of AI-driven delivery systems in sub-Saharan Africa, with implications for South Africa, finds perceived usefulness and ease of use studied together most often, in 57% of studies. Infrastructure access and digital literacy were examined together in a third of them, and institutional and policy support least often.

2026-09-25-sen-lesoleil-kaolack-digital-.summary: The Forum Civil held a two-day regional workshop in Kaolack for civil society and community leaders on digital issues, under an EU-funded project, Recentrer le civisme numérique. It aims to equip young people and community leaders to understand and use digital tools.

2026-09-25-sle-dpg-registry-four-teams.summary: Four Sierra Leonean teams met all nine Digital Public Goods criteria and submitted their products to the global registry, it was announced at a UNICEF event at UNGA81, with three more teams meeting six or seven criteria. The Christex Foundation, which prepared them over six to seven months, used its own AI-assisted assessment tool, Pipeline.

2026-09-25-sle-dpi-country-ownership-ung.summary: Communications minister Salima Monorma Bah told an AU-UNDP ministerial panel at UNGA81 that Sierra Leone's foundational digital identity covers more than 90% of the population, a national payment switch is scaling rapidly and a data exchange layer is being piloted in the financial sector. She presented the ECOWAS Data Embassy Framework as a way to pool digital infrastructure regionally rather than every country building the full stack alone.

2026-09-25-sle-open-source-policy-unveil.summary: Sierra Leone's communications ministry presented a new open source policy at a UNICEF event on the sidelines of UNGA81, as its answer to duplicated government systems, rising proprietary costs, systems that cannot interoperate and vendor lock-in. The policy's text, adoption date and instrument were not given.

2026-09-25-techreviewafrica-smart-africa.summary: Smart Africa's chief executive Lacina Koné told a GSMA and Partnership for Digital Access in Africa summit on the sidelines of UNGA81 that affordability should be treated as an economic and fiscal policy priority, not only a telecoms matter. The roundtable addressed the goal of bringing one billion Africans into meaningful digital participation by 2030.

2026-09-25-tgo-togofirst-togo-mali-data-.summary: Togo's personal data protection authority (IPDCP) and Mali's APDP signed a cooperation agreement on 23 September covering information exchange, joint handling of complaints and compliance checks, and staff training. Their talks also touched on cross-border data transfers, cybersecurity and AI.

2026-09-25-thecitizen-tza-tcra-communica.summary: Tanzania's regulator TCRA reported that mobile-network fraud reports fell 69% between September 2023 and June 2026, from 23,328 to 7,334 cases. Mobile money accounts rose from 32.7 million in March 2021 to 87.0 million in June 2026, and only 15.4% of the country's 17,690 Gbps of international capacity was in use.

2026-09-25-tun-chatel-digital-transforma.summary: A 2026 study of Tunisia's digital transformation and AI sets recent infrastructure gains, including the Medusa submarine cable landing at Bizerte in November 2025, the first national supercomputer entering trials in July 2026 and a national AI strategy for 2026-2030 presented in August, against continuing emigration of engineers. It cites more than 7,000 engineers leaving in 2025 and an expected 8,000 in 2026, and asks how the country can turn that talent into value created at home.

2026-09-25-tun-chourouk-tabelette-inspec.summary: Tunisia's labour-inspection director-general Noureddine Triki said the inspection platform is to exchange data with the national social security fund and the national business register by the end of 2026, and with other ministries' systems from January 2027. Inspectors are to move to tablets that record findings and geolocate establishments, with three regional workshops to train most of them.

2026-09-25-tza-tix-100g-core-upgrade.summary: The Tanzania Internet eXchange in Dar es Salaam upgraded its core switching to 100G, the ISP association TISPA said on 23 September. On the exchange's own statistics its 66 connected networks averaged about 205 Gbps in late September 2026, up from about 110 Gbps a year earlier.

2026-09-25-uemoa-fapbef-ai-forum-dakarac.summary: The federation of UEMOA banking associations (FAPBEF) held a sub-regional forum in Dakar on AI for financial inclusion and banking, with the BCEAO's national director for Senegal present. Its president, Guy Awona, called for a federated and controlled approach to AI across the Union's banks rather than treating it as a purely technological matter.

2026-09-25-uga-mtn-mobile-money-toll-pay.summary: MTN Uganda and the Ministry of Works and Transport launched Mobile Money toll payment on the Kampala-Entebbe Expressway, at the Busega, Kajjansi and Mpala plazas on designated lanes. The motorist gives a phone number to the attendant and approves a PIN prompt; no fee was named.

2026-09-25-zaf-ai-distillation-employee-.summary: An opinion piece asks whether a South African employer that has an employee train an internal AI agent on her work thereby acquires her professional capability. It argues that South African case law, including Automotive Tooling Systems v Wilkens and Nuvest Chemicals v Meyer (January 2026), treats skills and know-how as the employee's own rather than the employer's property.

2026-09-25-zaf-fnb-ai-governance-measura.summary: FNB's AI executive for retail and business banking, Dané Liebenberg, said the bank judges its AI deployments on four measures: sales revenue, process efficiency and cost to serve, fraud losses, and the effect on employees' workload. Its AI tools include the FNB banking app and NAVi, which supports advisers with customer insights.

2026-09-25-zaf-paystack-shopify-onsite-c.summary: Paystack introduced an onsite card checkout for Shopify merchants in South Africa, letting shoppers pay by card without leaving the merchant's checkout. It also added a Shopify integration for its in-store Paystack Terminal.

2026-09-26-afcfta-digital-trade-rules-70.summary: AfCFTA Secretary-General Wamkele Mene said in New York that Africa's digital economy could exceed US$700 billion by 2035 if common rules on payments, data transfers and digital identity remove barriers between national markets. He pointed to the Protocol on Digital Trade and the eight annexes the African Union adopted in February 2025.

2026-09-26-africa-ai-dependency-opinion-.summary: An opinion piece argues that African governments should adopt a pragmatic sovereign stance on artificial intelligence, using it for development while building their own compute, data governance, procurement and research capacity rather than importing foreign technology stacks and regulatory templates wholesale.

2026-09-26-civ-afriksoir-aspex-satellite.summary: At the Africa Space Expo in Abidjan on 25 September 2026, Côte d'Ivoire's telecoms regulator said three operators already sell satellite internet, two on geostationary satellites and one on a low-orbit constellation. It said it regulates them through a sandbox, periodic market analyses and the same consumer rights as terrestrial service.

2026-09-26-dza-jeune-independant-guessou.summary: An Algerian business-federation head welcomed the presidential decree being drafted on a secure digital interoperability plan, arguing that administrations should verify information directly with each other rather than ask citizens and firms to resupply it. The decree was ordered by the Council of Ministers on 20 September 2026 and has not been published.

2026-09-26-egy-afronews-imc-corporate-st.summary: Egypt's Industrial Modernization Center agreed with a local software firm to move small and medium-sized factories onto locally built ERP and other applications on a monthly subscription, with the centre adding incentives and technical support. No price, number of factories or timetable was given.

2026-09-26-gab-agp-itu-pp26-reunion-prep.summary: Gabon's digital economy minister joined an African Union ministerial consultation in New York on ITU governance, preparing a high-level AU meeting in Libreville on 29 and 30 October 2026 on content regulation, satellite internet providers and infrastructure. Gabon is standing for a seat on the ITU Council, to be elected at the Plenipotentiary Conference in Doha from 9 November.

2026-09-26-ken-capitalfm-unga-kdip-diasp.summary: Kenya signed a 2026-2030 country partnership programme with UNIDO at the UN General Assembly, linked to about US$750 million in investment opportunities in industry, technology transfer and manufacturing. President Ruto also discussed an East African refinery and a regional office of the Africa Finance Corporation in Nairobi.

2026-09-26-lumiernews-rdc-national-id-ca.summary: A Congolese civic group asked the government and the identification office on 24 September 2026 to account for the funds spent on the national identity card and to publish a delivery timetable, three years after the first card was handed to President Tshisekedi. It says he remains the only Congolese publicly issued one, and asks why mass enrolment has not reached provinces such as Tshopo.

2026-09-26-mwi-nzika-wallet-laxton-biome.summary: A Malawi24 investigation reports that a Hong Kong-registered company won a US$5.09 million World Bank-financed contract in March 2026 to supply 2,400 biometric registration kits to the National Registration Bureau, with remote software support. The procurement authority says remote access reaches the kits only; the bureau, the communications regulator and the supplier did not say who else can reach the identity system.

2026-09-26-techtrends-africa-startup-eco.summary: A feature argues that African venture capital is spreading beyond Lagos and Nairobi, citing Startup Genome's 2026 ranking of eleven Sub-Saharan ecosystems from Lagos to Dar es Salaam. It puts first-quarter 2026 startup funding at US$705 million across 59 deals in 14 countries, while Egypt, Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa still take the majority.

2026-09-26-thecitizen-tza-finland-startu.summary: A Tanzanian delegation from the ICT Commission, with officials and startups, spent a week studying Finland's innovation system under the EU-funded Digital for Tanzania twinning project. Its leaders said Tanzania needs reliable data on innovation and AI adoption and more domestic investment in startups.

2026-09-27-cpv-anacao-helio-varela-ia-so.summary: In an interview, Cabo Verdean specialist Hélio Varela rejects alarm about losing control of artificial intelligence and argues that the real risk is its concentration in a handful of countries and companies. He proposes a pragmatic technological sovereignty for the islands rather than protectionism.

2026-09-27-egy-sisi-orange-group-ceo-mee.summary: After Orange Group's chief executive met President El-Sisi, the operator announced training grants for about 200,000 people in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity, EUR 25 million for AI and advanced-technology startups, and technology laboratories for Egyptian universities. The President also sought its help with the second phase of the national digital health project.

2026-09-27-forumlibre-cobac-cemac-esg-ai.summary: The Central African banking supervisor met the region's bank and microfinance chiefs in Malabo on 25 September 2026 to set priorities on climate-related risk, stress testing, cybersecurity and the use of artificial intelligence. A single banking law and a green taxonomy for the CEMAC zone were among the reforms discussed.

2026-09-27-gab-gabonreview-ai-national-s.summary: Gabon's digital economy ministry and the UN Development Programme opened consultations toward a national artificial intelligence strategy, held in Libreville from 28 to 30 September 2026. The announcement sets out the themes but gives no budget, adoption date or priority uses.

2026-09-27-gab-gabonreview-oyem-digital-.summary: Gabon's First Lady visited the former governorate building in Oyem, which is being converted into a centre for coding, robotics, fabrication and entrepreneurship for children, young people and adults. It grows out of a local youth coding programme, and no cost or opening date is given.

2026-09-27-lby-alwasat-national-number-f.summary: Libya's public prosecutor announced another case of civil-status records falsified for money, reviving concern over forged national identity numbers, which the last official tally put above 89,000. The report traces the problem to 2022, when forged numbers were found to have drawn salaries and family grants, and asks how the civil registry's gaps can be closed.

2026-09-27-mwi-nzika-digital-id-public-t.summary: An opinion piece asks how Malawi's new Nzika digital identity wallet, launched on 16 September 2026, will protect the biometric data of more than 13.5 million registered people. It notes that reports on a World Bank-financed contract for 2,400 biometric registration kits do not show any data was compromised, and calls for clear rules on access and storage.

2026-09-27-nam-namibian-national-ai-inst.summary: Namibia's ICT minister launched a National Artificial Intelligence Institute in Windhoek, made up of software development, datasets, innovation and research centres. It is to work on skills, local datasets and uses in health, education, food security, energy and public services.

2026-09-27-rwa-newtimes-bk-cips-trader-r.summary: Rwandan importers who buy from China, the country's largest source of imports, expect Bank of Kigali's direct membership of China's yuan payment system to cut the cost of converting francs into dollars and then into yuan. An economist cautions that the gain depends on the bank's rates and fees, and that trade with China will not stop using the dollar.

2026-09-27-sen-seneweb-ia-souverainete-c.summary: A Senegalese professor argues that Africa's future in artificial intelligence depends on turning its young population into producers rather than consumers of technology. He calls for investment in science and mathematics education, research and computing capacity as the basis of what he terms cognitive and algorithmic sovereignty.

2026-09-27-sen-seneweb-pi-spi-gratuite-p.summary: The West African central bank's instant payment platform, live since September 2025, makes transfers between people and payments to merchants free to the customer across banks and wallets. The report looks at how that undercuts mobile money operators' fee income and network advantage as the deadline for institutions to connect approaches.

2026-09-27-techcabal-kenya-payments-revo.summary: A commentary argues that Kenya's success with mobile money has left the rest of its payments system neglected, citing central bank figures of 94.35 million registered accounts and KES 728.7 billion moved in July 2026. It calls for attention to bank rails, cards and cross-border payments beyond the dominant wallet.

2026-09-27-tgo-togofirst-arcep-mobile-qu.summary: Togo's telecoms regulator found neither mobile operator meeting its quality-of-service standards in a national campaign across 86 locations from July to August 2026, with YAS at about 75% compliance and Moov Africa Togo at about 54%. It is drafting rules that would require 95% compliance nationwide, backed by penalties.

2026-09-27-xaf-cipesa-fifafrica26-agenda.summary: The 2026 Forum on Internet Freedom in Africa, hosted in Mauritius by CIPESA with a local partner, has published its agenda: 18 pre-events and 41 sessions across eight themes, chosen from more than 450 proposals. The themes run from data governance and AI to platform accountability and digital security.

2026-09-28-au-achpr-access-to-informatio.summary: The African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights will review its 2013 Model Law on Access to Information next year to add digital-age provisions. It also points to its guidelines for states on monitoring technology companies and for platforms serving the public interest, and to draft guidelines on access to data.

2026-09-28-cioafrica-tcs-sovereign-cloud.summary: Tata Consultancy Services' sovereign cloud went live in Kenya, hosted at iXAfrica's Nairobi campus and delivered with a regional integrator, aimed at government agencies and regulated sectors with data-residency rules. Its capacity, pricing and clients were not disclosed.

2026-09-28-com-alwatwan-3-questions-soil.summary: In an interview, the Comorian engineer explains that AI models draw little on African data because so little of it is digitised.

2026-09-28-com-alwatwan-souverainete-num.summary: A Comorian computer engineer found that an AI search tool's answer on Mayotte drew mostly on French and European sources, and argues that countries must digitise their own data to be heard in AI answers.

2026-09-28-dza-alhirak-hcn-numerisation-.summary: An Algerian engineer argues that the new high council for digital transformation needs real power over technology flows, recommending prior approval of digital imports and concrete support for national industry.

2026-09-28-egy-amwalalghad-itida-giz-ict.summary: Egypt's IT industry development agency and GIZ launched work with 14 ICT companies on a playbook for recruiting and including persons with disabilities, to be produced through 15 workshops and published on the agency's website.

2026-09-28-egy-enterpriseam-ain-sokhna-n.summary: A digital truck yard at Ain Sokhna port, under an EGP 1bn contract for up to 1,100 trucks a day, is already linked live to Nafeza, Egypt's foreign-trade single window, so trucks are admitted only for cargo shown as cleared.

2026-09-28-egy-enterpriseam-tax-app-comp.summary: Egypt's finance ministry is reviewing an extension to the property-tax filing deadline after complaints about its new app, which the deputy finance minister said had about 1.2m users against 10m registrations expected.

2026-09-28-egy-mli-digital-transformatio.summary: Egypt's and Mali's ICT ministers agreed to begin technical talks on Mali drawing on Egypt's digital platforms and citizen services, with cooperation on fibre, government connectivity, AI and training.

2026-09-28-eth-ena-council-ministers-dat.summary: The state news agency's account of the same Council session names the bill the National Data Governance Draft Proclamation, referred to parliament with the Council's unanimous backing.

2026-09-28-eth-fanamc-council-ministers-.summary: Ethiopia's Council of Ministers unanimously sent a draft national data proclamation to parliament, framed around data security and sovereignty, data sharing and interoperability across government, and support for AI research.

2026-09-28-gab-agp-ouverture-strategie-i.summary: Gabon's digital ministry opened work on a national AI strategy with the UN Development Programme in Libreville, starting from a diagnosis of the country's AI landscape.

2026-09-28-gha-child-labour-monitoring-s.summary: Ghana is rolling out a digital child-labour monitoring system to identify, refer and follow up cases, interoperable with other child-protection systems and developed with ILO funding. District and regional officials were trained on it in mid-September.

2026-09-28-gnq-muni-dinero-tax-digitalis.summary: An Equatorial Guinean e-wallet provider presented itself to the transport ministry as a channel for collecting state revenue, citing a 2025 Presidency order that bans cash payment of any tax or fee in the administration. The company is seeking a favourable technical review.

2026-09-28-ifc-700m-digital-payments-ide.summary: The IFC launched a US$700m risk-sharing programme covering settlement risk so that more banks and fintechs in emerging markets can join international payment networks. It projects 360m cards and 90m new users, which the report says will put pressure on identity and fraud controls.

2026-09-28-ken-cisco-moran-ai-centre-of-.summary: Kenya's President and technology envoy discussed with Cisco the Moran AI Centre of Excellence, being developed with the defence forces as a regional hub for AI and cybersecurity, alongside AI skills for young people.

2026-09-28-ken-fintak-uber-exit-nga-uga-.summary: Kenya's fintech association argues that Uber's exits from Nigeria and Uganda on 2 September, after Tanzania in January, left drivers and riders with no notice or data on why. It calls for ride-hailing platforms, which depend on digital payments and identity, to be held to exit and disclosure rules.

2026-09-28-lbr-bet-on-liberia-payment-sw.summary: Liberia's finance minister told the diaspora conference near Washington that the national electronic payment switch is targeted for March 2027, alongside the central bank's inclusive instant payment system.

2026-09-28-lbr-gha-onehealthehr-goes-liv.summary: OneHealthEHR's offline-first health record and disease-surveillance platform went into clinical use in Liberia and Ghana on 1 September, growing from four to seven facilities in three weeks by the company's account. It targets 30-40 clinics by December, with Liberia's public health institute as its surveillance partner.

2026-09-28-lby-gaci-itu-emergency-teleco.summary: Libya's telecoms authority and the ITU held a first two-day workshop in Tripoli to review the national emergency telecommunications plan, develop early-warning systems and a unified protocol, and set agencies' roles. The plan was conceived after communications with Derna and other eastern cities failed during Storm Daniel in 2023.

2026-09-28-linkedin-frieden-rwanda-death.summary: A former head of the US disease-control agency describes Rwanda's phone-based death notification, in which village leaders report each community death with the deceased's national ID number, reaching the outbreak command centre within minutes. Rolled out nationwide in spring 2026, it logged about 10,000 community deaths in its first months, against a target of 70% of community deaths this year.

2026-09-28-mli-fasomali-cigem-migration-.summary: Mali's migration information centre ran a three-day workshop in Bamako on migration concepts and the governance of migration data.

2026-09-28-moz-biometricupdate-citizen-p.summary: Mozambique plans an integrated digital government by 2029, with its Citizen Portal, already offering about 26 services to more than 3,000 users, to launch at scale. The digital agency expects an interoperability platform in the fourth quarter of 2026 and has sent a shortlist for its mobile digital ID consultancy to the World Bank.

2026-09-28-mrt-elilam-digital-infrastruc.summary: Mauritania's digital ministry opened a week-long training for its officials and 120 new staff on applying unified state digital-infrastructure standards to every new digital service, following a March consultation of 34 ministerial sectors under the Digital-Y project. The ministry says the national government cloud now hosts state services and its design system is in use internally ahead of wider rollout.

2026-09-28-mus-defimedia-ai-progress-reg.summary: A Mauritian lawyer asks whether the country's regulatory and institutional frameworks can keep pace with AI adoption in finance and public services.

2026-09-28-mwi-iafrica-macra-ai-surveill.summary: Malawi's communications regulator recommended AI surveillance cameras for Blantyre under its Smart City Surveillance Initiative, a pilot combining number-plate recognition, traffic monitoring and a central command centre at four sites. No cost, supplier, timeline or rules on footage have been published, and the country has no AI policy yet.

2026-09-28-mwi-itwebafrica-macra-ai-crim.summary: Malawi's regulator backed AI-powered crime cameras for Blantyre after meeting city officials, with the police and road traffic directorate as partners. No budget, supplier or timetable is stated.

2026-09-28-mwi-linkedin-unicef-technolog.summary: A departing UNICEF official reflects on nearly four years of digital work in Malawi, arguing that what institutions can absorb, sustain and govern matters more than what technology can do.

2026-09-28-mwi-macra-blantyre-smart-city.summary: The regulator's engagement with Blantyre City Assembly on AI cameras able to detect objects and interpret incidents in real time was welcomed by the city's chief executive and mayor.

2026-09-28-nga-itwebafrica-fintech-regul.summary: Fintech and financial-crime specialists say Nigeria's rules leave stablecoin payments caught between the securities regulator, which treats digital assets as investments, and the central bank, which governs payments. They also point to compliance costs, identity fraud and weak coordination among regulators.

2026-09-28-nga-punch-data-centre-capacit.summary: An industry forum in Lagos set out a plan to raise Nigeria's data-centre capacity from about 50 MW of IT load to about 200 MW over five years, with a market assessment counting 21 operational facilities and 16 upcoming. A speaker said more than 80% of Nigeria's sovereign data is hosted abroad.

2026-09-28-nga-techcabal-overlapping-dat.summary: Nigeria's central bank rule requiring payment data to be stored locally by January 2027 and the national cloud policy come from two regulators with different mandates. Executives interviewed describe the result as an overlap to be managed rather than a clash, but warn of compliance costs.

2026-09-28-nga-wearetech-govtech-confere.summary: Nigeria's public service reform bureau will host the fourth GovTech conference in Abuja on 13-14 October, on digitising administration, digital identity, e-payments and service delivery.

2026-09-28-rwa-newtimes-jica-backed-digi.summary: Japan's development agency is backing ICT education, entrepreneurship and innovation projects in Rwanda with the polytechnic and the ICT ministry, centred on the QUEST project for industry-relevant digital skills.

2026-09-28-sen-wearetech-ecoles-connexio.summary: Senegal plans to connect 6,888 schools to broadband, with satellite for more than 2,000 others, against education-ministry figures showing 19.7% of public elementary schools online in 2023 and 15.4% in rural areas. The plan sits under the 2025-2029 digital education strategy.

2026-09-28-ssd-cajnewsafrica-ict-ministe.summary: South Sudan's ICT minister was kept on in a caretaker capacity when the President dissolved the transitional government ahead of December elections. An analyst expects a caretaker administration to hold the status quo rather than start long-term digital investment.

2026-09-28-ssd-radioyei-nsif-ecobank-dig.summary: South Sudan's social insurance fund opened talks with a commercial bank on linking its digital platform to the bank's systems through an API, ahead of contributor registration from 1 October. The fund reports more than 1,200 registered workers.

2026-09-28-swz-times-interpol-rstp-incid.summary: Eswatini's police have engaged INTERPOL over the incident at the National Data Centre and will investigate once a consultant hired by the science park and the ICT ministry reports. Unnamed sources suspect a third-party client gave attackers a way in; preliminary findings point to corrupted files and no data stolen.

2026-09-28-techmoonshot-airtel-starlink-.summary: Airtel Uganda switched on Starlink's satellite-to-phone messaging on 24 September, its second market after the DR Congo, nine months after the regulator said Starlink was unlicensed. The service covers SMS and light data on supported phones.

2026-09-28-tgo-e-id-togo-6-millions-enre.summary: Togo's identity agency closed biometric enrolment in the Centrale region with more than six million people registered and about 5.9 million cards produced, nearly 80% of them distributed. Kara, the last region, follows from October to December 2026.

2026-09-28-tgo-tvt-radio-lome-numerisent.summary: Togo put ten services of the state broadcasters TVT and Radio Lomé online, from death-notice broadcast requests to event coverage and advertising orders, under the programme to digitalise public services.

2026-09-28-truecaller-nigeria-privacy-ru.summary: Truecaller says it will not suspend or redesign its Nigerian service after the Lagos High Court dismissed a privacy suit on behalf of non-users, and points them to its unlisting portal. Judgment excerpts show the court held that a user's upload of contacts does not establish non-users' consent, and counsel for the applicants plans to appeal the refusal of relief.

2026-09-28-uga-mtn-ict-hub-palabek-refug.summary: MTN Uganda's foundation handed over an ICT hub with 12 computers and internet access at the Palabek refugee settlement, home to nearly 72,000 refugees and asylum seekers. The foundation says it has supported 94 ICT centres since 2007.

2026-09-28-uga-ncc2026-academia-industry.summary: The second day of Uganda's 10th National Conference on Communications at Makerere University focused on linking universities, industry and government to turn research into market-ready products.

2026-09-28-uga-uict-data-governance-fram.summary: A lecturer at Uganda's ICT institute presented research proposing a governance framework for turning institutional data into a shared knowledge resource, at a management conference in Entebbe. It argues for interoperability and data governance as conditions for inclusive digital transformation.

2026-09-28-vambo-ai-morena-african-langu.summary: Johannesburg-based Vambo AI built MORENA, a 1.5-billion-parameter model covering 12 African languages, on UNDP-backed supercomputing, but had to rely heavily on synthetic text because real African-language data was scarce.

2026-09-28-world-bank-cpv-2026-fpef-skil.summary: A World Bank blog describes Cabo Verde's employment and training fund, created in 2012, which finances training through competitive calls and tracks whether graduates find work.

2026-09-28-xaf-au-ministers-itu-pp26-com.summary: African ministers and the African Telecommunications Union coordinated the continent's common position for the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference at a closed session during the UN General Assembly.

2026-09-28-xaf-cioafrica-dfc-wiocc-300m-.summary: An analysis of WIOCC's funding notes that the US development finance agency joined a US$300m round three weeks after it was signed by a continental financier and a Saudi investor, with its own amount undisclosed and subject to congressional notification. It sets the round against data-centre costs of US$5-12m per megawatt, enough for tens rather than hundreds of megawatts.

2026-09-28-xaf-smart-africa-pan-african-.summary: At the Pan African AI Summit in Accra, Smart Africa set out its programmes for delivering the continent's AI ambitions within its single digital market of 42 member states, citing low intra-African trade and foundational digital skills held by 8% of people as the barriers.

2026-09-28-zaf-e-panic-button-data-breac.summary: South Africa's opposition DA in Gauteng will ask the Information Regulator to investigate the exposure of data from the provincial e-Panic Button app, including crime reporters' names, reports, photos and locations. It says the department did not inform the legislature's oversight committee.

2026-09-28-zaf-guardrisk-mip-cyber-breac.summary: Insurer Guardrisk says neither it nor its parent Momentum has any exposure to MIP Holdings, and that it has found no sign its own systems were breached, after a ransomware group claimed them.

2026-09-28-zaf-sita-rehabilitation-govte.summary: South Africa's communications department has formally begun a structural review of what the State IT Agency should be responsible for, the minister said at GovTech 2026. The agency's managing director set out a move from custom development to shared platforms and the retirement of legacy systems.

2026-09-28-zaf-woan-licensing-direction-.summary: South Africa withdrew the 2019 policy reserving high-demand spectrum for a wireless open access network that was never licensed, freeing it for the regulator to assign. Wholesale, universal-service and anti-concentration obligations on licensees stay, as does the 2024 set-aside for the state digital infrastructure company.

2026-09-28-zmb-digital-rights-media-deve.summary: MISA Zambia launched its 2026 Digital Rights and Media Development reports, and the information ministry restated its commitment to a rights-based digital environment.

2026-09-28-zwe-misa-information-integrit.summary: MISA Zimbabwe links access to information to information integrity and says the national AI strategy for 2026-2030 is a chance to build domestic AI capacity.

2026-09-29-actualite-cd-cod-banque-mondi.summary: A joint World Bank and French development agency mission is in Kinshasa until 2 October to review the Democratic Republic of Congo's digital transformation project. Its priority work covers connectivity of public institutions, state digital infrastructure, information-system security, civil registration and identification, and skills.

2026-09-29-ago-angop-ine-public-consulta.summary: Angola's statistics institute opened a public consultation, running to 2 October, on a revision of the national statistics law and a new national strategy for the development of statistics.

2026-09-29-ago-techreviewafrica-ggpen-an.summary: Traffic from Conecta Angola's satellite terminals is now routed from its hub onto the 2Africa cable through UNITEL's landing station at Cacuaco, to add capacity and a second international route. No capacity figure was given.

2026-09-29-airtel-malawi-revenue-rises-3.summary: Airtel Malawi's revenue rose 33.8% to K219.1bn in the half-year to June 2026, while exchange losses cut profit by more than half. Customers rose to 9.1 million, data customers to 2.9 million, and capital spending nearly tripled.

2026-09-29-au-innofest26-vibrant-youth-e.summary: The African Union held its Innovation Festival at its Addis Ababa headquarters on 29-30 September under the theme of youth ecosystems for AI and digital sovereignty.

2026-09-29-bfa-lefaso-yori-id-consular-p.summary: Burkina Faso's embassy in the United States launched YORI ID, a consular platform for cards, passports and administrative acts with online payment, as a one-year pilot. About 10,000 nationals are registered, most of them migrated from the previous system.

2026-09-29-cdpi-highlights-momentum-in-e.summary: The Centre for Digital Public Infrastructure visited Ethiopia's Fayda ID, EthSwitch, ArifPay, the agriculture ministry and the MESOB service centres, and said it would keep working with them.

2026-09-29-cpv-de-cix-cvtelecom-south-at.summary: DE-CIX and Cabo Verde Telecom signed a non-binding letter of intent to explore a Lisbon to Sao Paulo interconnection corridor, the operator supplying transport capacity in return for access to DE-CIX exchanges. Terms await a definitive agreement.

2026-09-29-gab-gabonreview-etat-civil-di.summary: A ten-day inter-ministerial workshop at Ntoum is preparing Gabon's national civil registry centre for operation and the reform of civil registration, under the World Bank-financed Gabon Digital programme. The programme coordinator said the rules for attributing identity must be settled before any platform is built.

2026-09-29-gab-gabonreview-video-verbali.summary: Gabon's road-safety directorate inspected the first cameras for automated enforcement of speeding, red-light and parking offences across Grand Libreville, ahead of going live. How notices will be served and fines collected has not been published.

2026-09-29-gab-lunion-e-commerce-revolut.summary: Online selling in Libreville runs on social media, mobile money and motorbike delivery, but sellers face poor connectivity and buyers little protection, as the sector still lacks rules.

2026-09-29-gha-myjoyonline-dvla-rfid-num.summary: Ghana's vehicle licensing authority began piloting RFID-enabled number plates ahead of issuance to newly registered vehicles from January 2027. How existing vehicles will be re-registered is still to be announced.

2026-09-29-ken-sle-techreviewafrica-ai-p.summary: Kenya's technology envoy and Sierra Leone's chief minister discussed working together on AI for public services and education with IDinsight and the OpenAI Foundation, after an UNGA dialogue on shared AI sovereignty. Nothing was agreed.

2026-09-29-ken-techcabal-mobile-money-ag.summary: Kenya lost about 34,000 mobile money agents between March and June 2026, down 5.6% to 568,463, while subscriptions rose 1.2% to 54.01 million, on regulator data. More people now transact directly from their phones.

2026-09-29-mar-techreviewafrica-mistral-.summary: Morocco's digital ministry and Mistral AI released their first open-source tools: a classifier that tells Arabic dialects including Darija apart, and a speech-recognition model for Darija that handles switching into French and English.

2026-09-29-mrt-ami-national-digital-addr.summary: Mauritania's digital and land ministers opened a four-day workshop presenting the national digital addressing system for consultation. It is meant as a single reference locating plots, buildings and facilities to Universal Postal Union standards, under the World Bank-financed regional digital integration programme.

2026-09-29-nga-itweb-africa-nigeria-digi.summary: Banking and fintech practitioners told ITWeb Africa that gaps in data sharing, affordability assessment and the use of alternative data limit how far Nigeria's digital lending can scale.

2026-09-29-nga-techcabal-cbn-data-locali.summary: A Central Bank of Nigeria supervision director said the payments-data localisation rule due on 1 January 2027 is about resilience and recoverability, not where servers sit. Further implementation guidance is being prepared, and institutions were told not to wait for it.

2026-09-29-nga-techreviewafrica-ncc-digi.summary: Nigeria's communications regulator opened the first Nigeria Digital Connectivity Investment Forum in Abuja, with Swedfund and Ookla as partners, to court investment in digital infrastructure.

2026-09-29-sajim-ai-enabled-e-services-j.summary: A case study of Namibia's justice ministry and a rural community, from 18 interviews, argues that AI could improve justice e-services for villages and rural areas.

2026-09-29-standard-bank-group-huawei-fo.summary: Standard Bank Group expanded its partnership with Huawei to move its core banking systems from legacy infrastructure to a hybrid cloud platform, in phases across the 21 African countries it operates in. No value, timetable or hosting location was given.

2026-09-29-tcd-lendjampost-adetic-moundo.summary: Chad's ICT development agency inaugurated a community multimedia centre in Moundou under the universal service programme, with a training room and a cybercafe on grid, solar and generator power.

2026-09-29-tcd-lendjampost-ndjamena-fact.summary: N'Djamena's city council told suppliers that their invoices must be standardised electronic invoices where they are liable, under a finance ministry circular of 10 September 2026, or risk not being paid.

2026-09-29-tgo-togofirst-online-public-s.summary: Togo's national public services portal added building-permit applications and the certification of the architect on a permit, along with services of the state broadcaster and public radio.

2026-09-29-tgo-togofirst-togo-ai-lab-voi.summary: Togo AI Lab put its Voix du Togo platform, built to give access to public services in local languages, to a public user test in Lome. It pilots Kabiye, Ewe and Moba, with the stated aim of covering about 50 languages.

2026-09-29-uga-nilepost-kamuntu-identity.summary: Figures at the opening of Uganda's first national identity expo put about 36.2 million people identified, roughly 78.8% of the population. The internal affairs minister called on the registration authority to reach everyone.

2026-09-29-xaf-techafricanews-au-questio.summary: The African Union Commission's AI coordinator said 17 countries have now formally adopted national AI policies, against eight when the continental strategy was written, at the consultation on continental AI governance guidelines. Draft guidelines and a model AI law are being prepared for ministerial review.

2026-09-29-xaf-techreviewafrica-auc-comm.summary: The African Union Commission's infrastructure and energy commissioner told a WEF roundtable at UNGA81 that AI sovereignty must be developmental, people-centred and inclusive, not focused on enterprises alone.

2026-09-29-xgl-africanenda-access-or-usa.summary: AfricaNenda's 2026 report on inclusive instant payment systems finds, on data from 54 economies, that a live instant payment system raises how often account holders use their accounts but not account ownership. The average transaction fell from US$58 in 2021 to US$25.

2026-09-29-zaf-citizen-gauteng-e-panic-b.summary: Gauteng's e-government department said the flaw in its e-Panic Button app is patched and no personal data was compromised, and put active users at 288,307. The student who reported the flaw disputes that account, saying ID numbers, addresses and crime details were exposed unencrypted.

2026-09-29-zaf-engineeringnews-vodacom-d.summary: Vodacom South Africa tested with Nokia a compact dual-band Massive MIMO unit across its 2,600 MHz and 3,500 MHz spectrum in a Western Cape pilot. It will deploy it at space-constrained sites to add 4G and 5G capacity.

2026-09-30-ago-forbes-lusofona-agt-integ.summary: Angola's tax and customs administration AGT is linking the commerce ministry's and other trade agencies' platforms to its own, and plans to let importers track customs processes by tax number, with service deadlines such as three days for the commerce ministry.

2026-09-30-cmr-cameroon-tribune-forum-cy.summary: Cameroon's ICT agency ANTIC reported 17,500 cybercrime complaints in 2025 with declared losses of 5.8 billion FCFA, at a cyberspace-security forum it co-hosts with the Russian embassy in Yaoundé. Since January it has counted 21,280 compromised machines and 39 attacks on government websites.

2026-09-30-cmr-linkedin-ojong-beyond-inf.summary: A LinkedIn policy brief argues that Cameroon has spent a decade building data centres, broadband and e-government platforms while ministries still cannot produce, share or use their own data, and that weak demand for evidence, not infrastructure, is the binding constraint.

2026-09-30-cod-agenceecofin-rdc-strategi.summary: The DRC's digital economy minister said the prime minister had signed decrees creating an online administrative-services portal and a national electronic certification agency, and that a national cybersecurity agency had been created by presidential ordinance. He said the RDC-PASS digital identity entered a first operational phase in September with 50 enrolment agents trained.

2026-09-30-douanes-et-fiscalit-la-tunisi.summary: Tunisia's customs and tax services plan to use machine learning to target high-risk declarations and audits; a customs risk-model test on 2025 data found about 96.9 million dinars in additional amounts. The finance ministry's IT centre said a one-year big-data tax-audit project on local infrastructure is at the bidding stage.

2026-09-30-egy-fintechgate-pdpc-children.summary: Egypt's Personal Data Protection Centre, part of the communications ministry, told a Meta-organised youth privacy event in Cairo on 24 September that children's privacy must be built into digital services at the design stage. Participants discussed age-appropriate design and effective age verification.

2026-09-30-ethiopia-establishes-financia.summary: Ethiopia set up a Financial Sector Cybersecurity Forum on 29 September, chaired jointly by the cyber agency INSA and the National Bank, for threat sharing and coordinated incident response across financial institutions.

2026-09-30-fsca-builds-ai-guardrails-as-.summary: South Africa's Financial Sector Conduct Authority told Parliament's finance committee that an AI framework for responsible use is being developed, the one outstanding element of its data and technology governance principle. It issued 140 scam warnings in 2025/26, up from 107, and tripled crypto-provider inspections to 30.

2026-09-30-ghana-ministry-receives-cyber.summary: Ghana's communications ministry received a cybersecurity white paper from Academic City University, drawn from academia, industry and the Cyber Security Authority, recommending local talent, local solutions and a move from policy to measurable implementation.

2026-09-30-gov-t-reviews-electronic-comm.summary: Zambia's technology ministry opened stakeholder consultations on amending the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act of 2021, approved in principle by Cabinet in September 2025. The changes would strengthen the national public key infrastructure under ZICTA and add appeal mechanisms.

2026-09-30-government-launches-integrati.summary: Uganda's internal affairs minister launched the integration of the national identification and tax identification systems at the country's first Identity Expo and Symposium in Kampala.

2026-09-30-information-regulator-to-enga.summary: South Africa's Information Regulator said it had received no breach notification from Gauteng's e-government department over the exposed e-Panic Button database and would engage the department, noting it can issue an information notice.

2026-09-30-ken-cbk-press-release-licensi.summary: The Central Bank of Kenya licensed 29 more digital credit providers, bringing the total to 281, from more than 900 applications since March 2022. Licensed lenders had made 9,596,509 loans worth Ksh165.1 billion by August 2026.

2026-09-30-ken-itweb-cbk-licenses-29-dig.summary: Trade-press report of the Central Bank of Kenya's licensing of 29 more digital lenders, summarised under the bank's own press release.

2026-09-30-kenya-data-commissioner-short.summary: Kenya's Public Service Commission shortlisted 13 of 152 applicants to succeed Immaculate Kassait as Data Protection Commissioner at the end of her single six-year term, with interviews on 5 October 2026.

2026-09-30-kenya-uk-deepen-cybersecurity.summary: The Communications Authority of Kenya hosted the UK National Cyber Security Centre's chief technology officer to discuss closer cooperation on the resilience of government systems and critical infrastructure. No agreement was announced.

2026-09-30-liberia-national-data-center-.summary: Liberia's posts and telecommunications ministry presented a planned national data centre to investors in New York, where reliable power was raised as the binding constraint. One investor has shown interest; the site and investment model await feasibility studies.

2026-09-30-lso-itweb-electronic-transact.summary: Lesotho's ICT ministry held a two-day validation workshop with UNDP on the Electronic Transactions and Communications Bill 2026, a revision of the 2022 bill, to fill the absence of any legal framework for electronic contracts, signatures and records. The bill now moves to the next legislative stages.

2026-09-30-mar-mistral-open-source-ai-br.summary: Morocco's digital transition ministry and Mistral released the first open-source tools from their AI partnership: a classifier that distinguishes Arabic dialects including Darija, and a Voxtral speech-recognition model for Darija that handles switching between Arabic, French and English. The ministry says further language and public-service models are in development.

2026-09-30-mastercard-partners-with-moja.summary: Mastercard announced it will explore pairing its A2A Protect fraud and dispute service with the Mojaloop Foundation's open-source instant-payment software, and will support AfricaNenda on instant-payment policy and governance. No country, sum or timetable was stated.

2026-09-30-mwi-itweb-macra-airtel-tnm-da.summary: Malawi's regulator MACRA is investigating complaints of rapid data-bundle depletion on Airtel and TNM, examining their charging and billing systems. It had earlier found both operators applied approved tariff rises of 22.2% and 26% before the required seven-day notice.

2026-09-30-nam-csirt-data-protection-adv.summary: Namibia's national computer incident response team, housed at the communications regulator, issued an advisory urging institutions to tighten information security and the public and media not to access or redistribute personal data leaked in cyber incidents. It said finalising a data protection law remains outstanding.

2026-09-30-ncc-hinges-1tr-economy-on-tel.summary: At the Nigerian Communications Commission's Digital Connectivity Investment Forum in Abuja, officials and operators argued that broadband underpins the government's US$1 trillion economy target for 2030, and the regulator sought investors to close coverage gaps. Power costs and fragmented regional regulation were named as the main obstacles.

2026-09-30-ndpc-chief-stronger-data-prot.summary: Nigeria's data protection commissioner opened a training programme in Abuja for data protection officers in federal ministries and agencies, and reminded them that breaching the 2023 Data Protection Act carries consequences.

2026-09-30-nibss-national-payment-stack-.summary: Nigeria's interbank settlement system NIBSS said its ISO 20022-compliant National Payment Stack had passed 100 million successful transactions, as a single rail for banks, microfinance banks, fintechs and mobile money operators.

2026-09-30-sen-kfw-prodap-progress-revie.summary: A KfW mission reviewed progress on PRODAP, the German-funded programme for more reliable digital technology in Senegal's administration, with Sénégal Numérique (formerly ADIE) and prepared its next steps. No figures on delivery were published.

2026-09-30-sen-vipeoples-passports-id-ca.summary: Senegal's National Assembly took in plenary on 29 September a bill amending the ECOWAS biometric identity card law. In committee the interior minister confirmed an attack on the directorate that runs identity files, announced a security audit and a national data centre for civil-status and identity data, and said card and passport production would pass to Senegalese firms as the Malaysian contract runs out.

2026-09-30-south-africa-s-competition-co.summary: Trade-press account of the Competition Commission's conditional recommendation on MTN's purchase of IHS, summarised under the Commission's own statement.

2026-09-30-tanzanie-infrastructure-numer.summary: Tanzania presented a digital-infrastructure investment envelope of TZS 7,000 billion (about US$2.6bn) to 2031 at an EU-Tanzania business forum in Helsinki, funds still to be raised. The portfolio includes fibre-to-the-home, the Kilimanjaro One submarine cable and a technology park; the national backbone stood at 13,820 of a planned 16,280 km.

2026-09-30-tchad-protection-des-donnees-.summary: Paradigm Initiative and ACSIS-Tchad opened a two-day Digital Policy Engagement Series in N'Djamena on 30 September on data protection, cybersecurity and digital rights, bringing together officials, magistrates, security forces and civil society.

2026-09-30-uganda-japan-discuss-expandin.summary: Uganda's ICT minister and Japan's ambassador discussed a second phase of the JICA-backed UJ Connect ICT industry project, adding AI, more mentorship and closer links between Ugandan ICT talent and Japanese firms. No budget or start date was given.

2026-09-30-xaf-techreviewafrica-auda-nep.summary: AUDA-NEPAD launched an Africa Semiconductor Technical Advisory Group in South Africa with the CSIR, the African Academy of Sciences and South Africa's science department, to coordinate chip design, packaging, critical minerals and skills across the continent. Its first twelve months cover six work areas including RISC-V adoption and standards.

2026-09-30-xaf-techreviewafrica-day-zero.summary: A pre-FIFAfrica dialogue convened by the Global Center on AI Governance, Digital Action and CIPESA called for African AI governance principles to be turned into concrete commitments on training data, worker participation and community interests.

2026-09-30-zaf-compcom-statement-decisio.summary: South Africa's Competition Commission recommended that the Tribunal approve MTN's acquisition of tower operator IHS, on conditions of fair and non-discriminatory access to IHS towers for rival operators, fair lease renewals, ring-fencing of customer information and an operationally independent IHS. Job protection and ownership conditions are attached.

2026-09-30-zaf-itweb-absa-digital-asset-.summary: Absa launched institutional digital-asset custody for South African clients on 21 September on Ripple's technology, the first such service by an African bank. It is for institutional and large corporate clients, not retail crypto.

2026-09-30-zambia-must-use-digital-platf.summary: President Hichilema told the UAE's cabinet affairs minister in Abu Dhabi that Zambia must use digital platforms to cut the bureaucracy slowing investment and services, treating digital infrastructure as part of service delivery itself. The UAE offered its own bureaucracy-reduction programme as a model.

2026-10-01-africa-cdc-calls-for-stronger.summary: Africa CDC called on member states to strengthen national health data stewardship and adopt interoperable digital standards, at a consultative session at the Africa HealthTech Summit in Kigali.

2026-10-01-afrinic-elections-2026-pdp-co.summary: AFRINIC opened candidate registration for one of its two policy development co-chair seats, closing on 29 October. The seat will be filled at the public policy meeting on 18 November.

2026-10-01-airtel-money-sets-ipo-price-a.summary: Airtel Money set the price of its London share offer at GBP1.96, valuing the company at about GBP5.3 billion. Trading is expected to begin on 14 October.

2026-10-01-anambra-launches-digital-gate.summary: Nigeria's Anambra State launched a redesigned website as a single entry point to state services, with grievance and freedom-of-information channels. An open-government section gives budgets, audit reports, procurement plans, contract awards and open data.

2026-10-01-auda-nepad-launches-atlas-umo.summary: The African Union's development agency launched and chairs an AI policy workstream, ATLAS Umoja, on AI governance and African-language AI. A mobile industry official said at the launch that fewer than 2% of African languages are meaningfully supported by today's AI models.

2026-10-01-businessday-meta-appeals-nige.summary: Meta filed a notice of appeal on 30 September against a Lagos High Court judgment of 25 September that held its processing of Nigerian users' data for behavioural advertising unlawful. The court ordered it to stop, comply with the data protection Act within eight weeks and pay the naira equivalent of US$100,000 in damages.

2026-10-01-digital-society-governing-ai-.summary: A systematic review of 30 peer-reviewed articles from 2020 to 2026 finds that evidence on AI for sustainability goals in the global south is concentrated in environmental uses such as climate-risk assessment and land-use monitoring. Reported benefits depend on AI tools being combined with data infrastructure, institutional capacity and accountability safeguards.

2026-10-01-e-panic-button-security-flaw-.summary: A Gauteng legislature committee said it will examine whether the provincial e-government department's earlier assurances about the e-Panic Button's security were accurate. The department says an attempted breach was identified and fixed and that no personal information was compromised.

2026-10-01-ethswitch-unveils-unified-gov.summary: Ethiopia's national payment switch presented a unified government payment platform at the Ethiopia Finance Forum. It would give government bill payments one interoperable route across mobile apps, ATMs, USSD, branches and agents.

2026-10-01-gabonreview-gabon-ai-strategy.summary: Preparatory work for Gabon's national AI strategy closed in Libreville on 30 September with 22 challenges and 36 recommendations from six working groups supported by UNDP. The ministry and UNDP will now draft the strategy, its action plan and financing for government validation.

2026-10-01-gabonreview-gabon-data-govern.summary: Gabon's data protection authority took part in a study visit on personal-data governance in Dakar on 7 to 10 September, run by the African Union's development agency with German cooperation. Participants cited the Gabonese authority's funding model as a reference.

2026-10-01-gha-myjoyonline-csa-no-digita.summary: Ghana's Cyber Security Authority opened the 2026 National Cyber Security Awareness Month on securing digital finance. Its director-general asked banks, telecoms operators, fintechs and regulators to share threat intelligence quickly enough to stop attacks before losses occur.

2026-10-01-independentnews-minister-sava.summary: Eswatini's ICT minister launched National Cybersecurity Awareness Month and said a review of the National Cybersecurity Strategy has begun. The Director of Public Prosecutions said her office has set up a Cybercrime Unit and trained prosecutors on the 2022 cybercrime Act.

2026-10-01-internet-society-fair-share-p.summary: An Internet Society paper argues that proposals to make large content providers pay telecoms operators for carrying traffic would raise costs, weaken local traffic exchange and increase market concentration in Africa.

2026-10-01-ken-techcabal-safaricom-pesap.summary: Safaricom and Pesapal put M-PESA tap-to-pay and QR payment on Pesapal's 30,000 point-of-sale terminals in Kenya, with no extra fee. Safaricom says scan-to-pay is live at more than 60,000 merchant outlets and targets 500,000 within a year.

2026-10-01-kenya-advances-digital-public.summary: Kenyan principal secretaries and private-sector leaders discussed the country's digital public infrastructure roadmap at a public sector forum, naming access, trust and interoperability as its three priorities. No document or timetable was published.

2026-10-01-lby-libyaherald-noc-officials.summary: Libya's Attorney General's Office ordered two National Oil Corporation officials, one of them its director of information and digital transformation, into pre-trial detention over leaked oil-sector data. Data on fields, production, reserves and exploration passed to a foreign company contracted in 2023 for a sector study.

2026-10-01-liberian-observer-liberia-ins.summary: Liberia's instant payment system has processed more than 5.3 million transactions between the two mobile money operators since its December 2025 launch, the central bank governor said. About 4.2 million were in Liberian dollars and 1.1 million in US dollars.

2026-10-01-ncc-launches-zero-rated-data-.summary: Nigeria's communications regulator and the operators' association launched zero-rated access to approved educational platforms, giving eligible learners up to 100MB of free data a day. The association put the industry's commitment at almost N200 billion for an initial pilot of 5,000 learners.

2026-10-01-ssd-radioyei-eaco-working-gro.summary: An East African Communications Organisation working group, meeting in Juba, finalised frameworks for rapid cyber-threat response among national response teams. It also produced guidelines for users of digital financial services, child online protection measures and mobile data quality standards.

2026-10-01-uga-nilepost-ucu-privacy-moot.summary: Uganda Christian University won a regional privacy moot court competition for law students from Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania and Rwanda. The ICT minister told the students that innovation must not undermine privacy and data protection.

2026-10-01-xaf-airtel-africa-airtel-mone.summary: Airtel Africa's regulatory announcement gives the terms of the Airtel Money offer: existing shareholders sell 270 million shares, with up to 27 million more under an over-allotment option, leaving about 16.5% of the company in public hands. Airtel Africa sells only through the over-allotment option.

2026-10-01-xaf-techcabal-kora-adds-stabl.summary: The Nigerian-founded payments company Kora launched One Rail, which lets merchants accept, convert and settle the dollar stablecoins USDT and USDC through its existing network. It is rolling out market by market.

2026-10-01-xaf-techcabal-space-data-cent.summary: Satlyt, a space-technology startup with its African headquarters in Nairobi, raised US$8 million in seed funding. Its software runs data processing and AI applications on the computers aboard other operators' satellites.

2026-10-01-xaf-techreviewafrica-atu-sg-s.summary: The African Telecommunications Union's secretary general told the 42nd meeting of the International Telecommunications Satellite Organization in Washington that satellite resources remain central to connectivity in Africa.

2026-10-01-zaf-citizen-gauteng-e-panic-b.summary: The Gauteng legislature's e-government committee rejected the provincial department's assurance that no personal information was compromised by the e-Panic Button exposure, and gave it seven days to report. It wants an incident timeline, proof of notification to the Information Regulator and residents, and the contract's data-protection clauses.

2026-10-01-zaf-citizen-green-id-book-end.summary: South Africa's home affairs minister said production of the green ID book will end on 31 March 2027. He showed the first working digital identity credential and put smart ID replacements at more than 515 bank branches and 822,000 users.

2026-10-01-zmb-itweb-zamportal-revenue-c.summary: Zambia's finance minister said the national services portal has collected about K9.8 billion across 572 services and 52 providers since 2019. The 2027-2029 budget call circular names the Government Service Bus and payment gateway as the state's centralised revenue-collection system.

2026-10-02-ago-nova-lei-da-ciberseguranc.summary: Angola's cybersecurity law has been published as Lei n.º 9/26 of 28 September and is in force, revoking the 2017 law. Operators of critical infrastructure, essential services, electronic communications, data centres and cloud services must register with the National Cybersecurity Centre within 180 days, set up incident response teams and notify significant incidents to CERT.ao.

2026-10-02-burundi-sim-registration-scam.summary: Burundi's mandatory SIM and eSIM registration, begun in mid-June, was about 70 per cent complete on the regulator's count. Users report long queues, few service points and slow systems, and scams continue; operators must keep customer data for at least five years.

2026-10-02-gabon-validation-digital-tran.summary: Gabon began a validation review of draft legal texts for digital transformation at Nkok on 1 October, to run about ten days. The texts cover digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, digital services and the institutional framework, under the World Bank-financed Gabon Digital programme.

2026-10-02-ghana-public-sector-ai-procur.summary: Ghana's communications minister announced that every AI system bought by a public institution will go through a centralised technical review. The national information technology agency will scope deployments against interoperability, data-protection, cybersecurity and local skills-transfer requirements, alongside procurement law.

2026-10-02-icasa-withdraws-affordability.summary: South Africa's communications regulator withdrew the notices for its telecommunications affordability inquiry and its inquiry into over-the-top services, citing administrative and procedural matters. The affordability notice is to be republished with a draft questionnaire and the other at a later date; those who have commented may resubmit.

2026-10-02-itweb-sa-eta-machine-learning.summary: South Africa's home affairs department said its Electronic Travel Authorisation uses machine learning to make automated, risk-based decisions on short-stay visa applications, with a human brought in where the system flags an anomaly. The system is live at four airports.

2026-10-02-lbr-liberia-advances-developm.summary: Liberia's education ministry closed a two-day consultation on 28 and 29 September on a policy for its education management information system, supported by the African Union. The policy covers how education data is collected, secured, shared and used.

2026-10-02-mdg-ecofin-4g-coverage-intern.summary: Madagascar's bill on electronic communications and digital infrastructure, submitted on 28 August, still waits for examination by the National Assembly. The article sets it against a market where 4G covers about 80 per cent of the population while mobile internet use stays low.

2026-10-02-moz-aim-uem-directrizes-ia.summary: Mozambique's Universidade Eduardo Mondlane has approved a directive on the responsible and transparent use of AI in teaching, research and administration. It was presented at a workshop on 30 September and 1 October that also shared a draft institutional AI roadmap.

2026-10-02-mus-defimedia-maupass-korek-a.summary: Mauritius Digital Promotion Agency staff will help citizens register on MauPass and reach their digital driving licence in the KOREK app from the coming week. The 883,700 licence holders have three months before the digital licence takes legal effect on 1 January 2027.

2026-10-02-nam-iafrica-national-ai-insti.summary: Namibia's research commission opened a National Artificial Intelligence Institute on 23 September with four centres, for datasets, research and development, software development and AI innovation. Each answers a gap named in the country's 2025 AI readiness assessment; that assessment's other findings, including no AI regulatory framework, are not addressed by the institute.

2026-10-02-nam-nampa-fnb-judiciary-court.summary: First National Bank of Namibia handed 42 card payment devices to the Office of the Judiciary on 30 September, so that court-related payments at Magistrates' Courts can be made electronically.

2026-10-02-ner-actuniger-soniloga-airtel.summary: The operator of Niger's vehicle one-stop shop began accepting Airtel Money for some of its services on 1 October, through an app or an offline USSD code. The transport ministry presented it as a way to trace public revenue.

2026-10-02-nigeria-digital-postcode-syst.summary: Nigeria's communications ministry asked businesses and developers to build services on the new national digital postcode system. An API is open to organisations that pass business verification, with testing alongside the postal service before production access.

2026-10-02-nigeria-tiktok-disruption-cso.summary: Twelve Nigerian civil-society groups asked for an investigation into disruptions to TikTok access in Kaduna, Kebbi, Kano and Sokoto, first reported around 14 September. They asked the communications regulator to facilitate independent network testing and said their findings do not establish a government-ordered block.

2026-10-02-rwa-ktpress-mastercard-founda.summary: Eight Rwandan education-technology companies are in the Mastercard Foundation EdTech Fellowship, an 18-month acceleration programme launched in June 2026 and run through the Rwanda ICT Chamber. Their products range from identifying learners at risk of dropping out to robotics for schools with few resources.

2026-10-02-sen-techafricanews-stellarix-.summary: STELLARIX Senegal, part of the AXIAN Group, said it has expanded its data-centre capacity in Senegal for cloud, AI and hosting demand. It named three contractors and gave no capacity or cost figure.

2026-10-02-tun-tunisienumerique-pacte-na.summary: Tunisia's health and communication technologies ministers signed a National Health Pact on 1 October to speed universal health coverage through digital transformation. Its six axes include sovereign governance of health data, modernised digital platforms and medicine supply-chain security; it is backed by the World Bank and WHO.

2026-10-02-tza-dailynews-who-protects-yo.summary: A Daily News feature sets out how personal data is collected across Tanzania's identity, health and financial services as the country implements its Dira 2050 development vision. It describes the role of the Personal Data Protection Commission in protecting that information.

2026-10-02-xaf-gsma-undp-partner-african.summary: UNDP and the GSMA announced a partnership to support African-led AI, including AI in African languages. Through UNDP's timbuktoo initiative they will work on access to compute for priority AI pilots and on connecting African talent to applied AI work.

2026-10-02-zaf-biometricupdate-digital-i.summary: South Africa's home affairs minister said a working prototype of the smartphone-based digital ID has been built and demonstrated his own credential. A pilot and wider rollout are being prepared, with no public release date.

2026-10-02-zmb-techreviewafrica-auc-zamb.summary: The African Union's infrastructure commissioner and Zambia's ambassador to the United Nations discussed implementing the Global Digital Compact in New York.
