They covered regional approaches to compute, including GPU capacity for each of Africa's five regions and a proposed SADC data centre.

2026-10-02-zwe-herald-cyber-strong-zimba.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT ministry said it is still advancing the National Cybersecurity Strategy 2026-2030, which would set up a National Cybersecurity Authority and a stronger national incident response team. The statement came at the launch of National Cybersecurity Awareness Month.

2026-10-03-africa-cdc-official-continent.summary: The head of digital health at the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention said most health AI models presented to her are hosted on a foreign cloud, because the continent lacks the infrastructure to run them. The agency is drafting a continental health data governance framework with more than 40 member states, setting who may access health data, for what purpose and for how long.

2026-10-03-cod-ap-ofac-bank-of-kigali-ci.summary: A Congolese civic platform has asked the United States Treasury's sanctions office to examine Bank of Kigali's direct participation in China's cross-border renminbi payment system, signed on 8 September. It argues the channel could be used to get round American sanctions on the Rwandan army and on networks trading Congolese minerals.

2026-10-03-cod-frpc-droit-acces-informat.summary: A federation of community radio stations held a press meeting in the Democratic Republic of Congo on the access-to-information bill, declared admissible by the National Assembly in March. The government spokesman said finishing the law is among the government's priorities; no date for a vote was given.

2026-10-03-eth-reporter-digital-transact.summary: An assessment of Ethiopia's second financial inclusion strategy found adult account ownership at 66 per cent in 2025 against a 70 per cent target, with some banks charging up to 11 per cent for transfers to mobile wallets. Only 29.56 per cent of 157.6 million mobile money accounts were active in June 2026; a third strategy, for 2026 to 2030, was launched alongside it.

2026-10-03-gha-myjoyonline-mtn-ghana-5g-.summary: MTN Ghana says it will roll out 5G once the regulator issues the spectrum licences it has been awarded in the 700 MHz and 3 GHz bands, at a cost of about US$202 million. The company told investors the payments are already in its cash-flow outlook.

2026-10-03-mdg-lexpress-inclusion-financ.summary: Madagascar's Mvola has made merchant payments free for customers, with the merchant bearing the fee. The mobile money operator reports close to 4 million users, more than 60,000 cashpoints and more than 50,000 merchants accepting payment.

2026-10-03-permis-de-conduire-numerique-.summary: Mauritius's digital driving licence takes legal effect on 1 January 2027, after a transition period that began on 29 September. A driver may show either the digital licence on the KOREK app or the original physical licence, and the ICT minister said 500,000 people have registered on MauPass, the account needed to reach it.

2026-10-03-xaf-techreviewafrica-auc-mata.summary: The African Union's infrastructure and energy commissioner called for artificial intelligence built around African languages and priorities rather than adopted from elsewhere. Figures cited by the African Union put the continent at 1 per cent of global AI compute capacity and about 3 per cent of AI talent.

2026-10-04-african-diplomats-in-cairo-ag.summary: Representatives of 11 African diplomatic missions in Cairo agreed to draft a joint Cairo Document for Trust and African Digital Integration. It is to set shared priorities on digital investment, digital trade, cybersecurity, data governance and emerging technologies.

2026-10-04-ben-beninwebtv-anip-50109-act.summary: Benin's identification agency said 50,109 children received a first birth certificate free of charge in September 2026. The campaign ran from 16 to 30 September for children under 14 who had never had one.

2026-10-04-cote-divoire-seeks-responsibl.summary: Cote d'Ivoire's digital transition minister told an international seminar that the government wants blockchain and digital assets developed inside a secure regulatory framework. He named agriculture, financial transactions, land administration and the creative sector as possible uses and announced no instrument.

2026-10-04-dza-dzwatch-akbou-i-cloud-sov.summary: Algeria inaugurated I-Cloud, described as its first wholly sovereign data centre, in the Akbou industrial zone in Bejaia. The knowledge economy minister presided, and agreements were signed with local industrialists and Algeria Venture on small firms' access to it; the inauguration date and capacity are not stated.

2026-10-04-dza-radioalgerie-tebboune-dig.summary: President Abdelmadjid Tebboune told his periodic media briefing that digitisation has sharply reduced corruption in Algeria by exposing manipulation across sectors, the foreign-currency allowance procedures among them. He gave no figures.

2026-10-04-egypt-electricity-ministry-on.summary: Egypt's electricity distribution companies lost sight of citizens' service requests after the holding company's systems sector replaced the unified e-services platform with an untested system and switched the old one off, a ministry source told Youm7. The minister ordered the fault fixed and those responsible held to account.

2026-10-04-gha-citinewsroom-attobrah-qua.summary: An opinion piece examines the Ghanaian cabinet's rejection of a proposed United States health compact worth about US$109 million over five years. President Mahama said it would have required Ghana to hand over pathogen data and medical records; the author argues that refusing is only the start of the work of data sovereignty.

2026-10-04-gha-gna-dpc-spot-checks-enfor.summary: Ghana's Data Protection Commission said it would begin spot checks and enforcement from 5 October against organisations that process personal data without registering or meeting the Data Protection Act, 2012. Its executive director said prosecution would follow where necessary.

2026-10-04-gha-gna-telecel-double-fibre-.summary: Two fibre cuts caused by road construction, on the Accra-Winneba and Winneba-Cape Coast routes, disrupted service to an estimated 72,754 Telecel Ghana subscribers on about 181 sites in the Central Region. The communications minister reported it on 3 October and said engineers were restoring service.

2026-10-04-liberia-studies-ghanas-paymen.summary: The governor of the Central Bank of Liberia led a delegation to the Bank of Ghana on 1 October to study how Ghana set up its interbank payment and settlement company. Liberia is working to connect its banks to the instant payment system it switched on in December 2025.

2026-10-04-mar-eyeofriyadh-cbuae-bank-al.summary: Bank Al-Maghrib and the Central Bank of the UAE signed two memoranda in Abu Dhabi. One covers supervisory information exchange and Islamic finance; the other is to explore linking the two countries' instant payment platforms, card switches and financial messaging systems, and to exchange expertise on central bank digital currencies.

2026-10-04-mobile-money-wallets-set-to-l.summary: Ethiopia's non-bank mobile-money operators and payment-service providers are preparing to connect to the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System. Each needs a letter of no objection from the National Bank of Ethiopia first, and operators are weighing a direct connection against routing through EthSwitch or partner banks.

2026-10-04-nam-marketwatch-namibia-stren.summary: Namibia's communications regulator launched DigiNam in Windhoek on 31 August as the public face of the national public key infrastructure, for which the regulator is root certification authority. It is meant to support electronic signatures, digital identity and authenticated online transactions under the Electronic Transactions Act of 2019.

2026-10-04-nga-businessday-split-cloud-b.summary: Nigerian banks and large fintechs face the central bank's 1 January 2027 deadline for storing payment transaction data in the country. Cloud providers say some may keep applications on foreign clouds and host the regulated data locally, an arrangement the central bank has not ruled on.

2026-10-04-nga-gentechnews-ncc-communiqu.summary: Nigeria's communications regulator issued the communique of its Digital Connectivity Investment Forum, held in Abuja on 29 and 30 September with Swedfund and Ookla. It sets actions on timelines of six to twenty-four months, among them open-access and wholesale regulation, a wholesale rate card, completed broadband mapping and a first national connectivity index report. It records broadband penetration at 57.4% against a 70% target.

2026-10-04-rwa-taarifa-digital-payments-.summary: Rwanda's prime minister said reported financial fraud complaints fell by about 30% in the second quarter of 2026 from 4,128 a year earlier. Digital transactions rose from about 256 million in 2017 to 3.1 billion in 2025, and he said phone-based fraud remains a problem.

2026-10-04-sdn-sudanews-un-desa-e-govern.summary: Sudan's foreign ministry undersecretary met the UN under-secretary-general for economic and social affairs in New York and briefed him on the economy, financial reform and reconstruction. The report names support for Sudan's digital transformation as a subject of cooperation and states no agreement or programme.

2026-10-04-sdn-sudanhorizon-mof-zain-eis.summary: Sudan's finance ministry signed an agreement with Zain in Khartoum on 4 October for text-message services on Eisali, the state electronic collection and payment system. Users are to be told the status of each transaction as it is registered, updated or completed.

2026-10-04-sha-to-hmis-how-kenyas-rushed.summary: A commentary argues that Kenya is moving health facilities from the health insurer's provider portal to facility-owned information systems before the arrangement has been tested. It questions the pace, the cost to hospitals and the handling of patient data during the switch.

2026-10-04-tgo-ipdcp-apdp-benin-seance-t.summary: Togo's data-protection authority hosted its Beninese counterpart in Lome on 2 and 3 October for a working session on sharing experience and building skills. It follows the Togolese authority's mission to Benin on 18 August and the two bodies' cooperation agreement.

2026-10-04-tun-businessnews-forum-chawki.summary: Tunisia's Forum Chawki Gaddes for digital rights condemned the spread on social media of personal and sensitive data, including leaked judicial documents and images of child victims. It says the national data-protection authority has stopped working although its law remains in force, and calls for it to be reactivated.

2026-10-04-xca-gep-beac-jornadas-banquer.summary: The governor of the Bank of Central African States, closing the CEMAC Bankers' Days in Bangui on 3 October, set a goal that by the end of 2027 every transfer under CFA 5 million settles in under ten seconds on the region's interoperable instant payment system. He also cited a regional switch project and a central bank sovereign cloud to keep payment data in the region, and a 35% financial inclusion target for 2028.

2026-10-04-zwe-herald-econet-infraco-mai.summary: Econet InfraCo, the tower, power and property company listed in Victoria Falls, reported revenue of US$70.1 million and EBITDA of US$29.0 million for the six months to 31 August 2026, its first half-year results since listing.

2026-10-05-camtel-minesec-sic-connectivi.summary: Cameroon's state operator CAMTEL says it will sign two framework agreements on 7 October: one with the secondary education ministry on connectivity for schools, the other with the state housing company on connectivity in housing estates.

2026-10-05-capitalfm-african-ict-regulat.summary: Opening the same Nairobi session, the head of Kenya's communications regulator urged African regulators to pool their efforts against fraud, cyber threats and cable disruptions that cross borders. He said Kenya has promulgated a new market structure for telecommunications and postal services and is reviewing its sector laws.

2026-10-05-cbl-electronic-transactions-8.summary: Libya's central bank said electronic transactions reached about 865 billion dinars by the end of September 2026. The figure came from a meeting between the governor, commercial bank heads and the state payments company on cash liquidity, wider electronic payment and cyber-risk readiness.

2026-10-05-csa-ghana-opens-ncsam-2026.summary: Ghana's Cyber Security Authority opened its 2026 awareness month with a call for banks, fintechs and telecoms operators to share threat information as routine. The national response team recorded 3,876 incidents between January and July 2026, about 47% of them online fraud.

2026-10-05-dcd-continent-8-johannesburg-.summary: Continent 8 Technologies, which hosts online gaming and betting operators, announced its first African data centre, in Johannesburg. It did not disclose the site or any colocation partner.

2026-10-05-gin-mediaguinee-orange-unicef.summary: Fondation Orange Guinée and UNICEF signed a protocol at Conakry on 5 October to equip 50 schools across six regions with digital learning hubs. It also provides for training 500 adolescents in science and digital skills and for 100 scholarships and prizes; no budget is stated.

2026-10-05-gmb-standard-udp-supplementar.summary: The Gambia's United Democratic Party asked the electoral commission to explain a gap of 28,932 between the 212,095 supplementary registrations it announced and the 183,163 in the dataset given to the party. It wants the figures before and after de-duplication, the records deleted and the method used, and says it is not alleging malpractice.

2026-10-05-gtco-payments-business-five-n.summary: An analysis of Guaranty Trust Holding Company's half-year results shows its payments subsidiary HabariPay earning ₦7.81 billion in profit, close to double a year earlier, on ₦74.72 trillion switched. Transfers through its Pay-with-Transfer service reached ₦1.11 trillion while USSD use fell.

2026-10-05-how-much-collected-digital-mi.summary: South Africa's communications minister told Parliament that about R1.29 billion was collected for the Universal Service and Access Fund over five years and about R652 million was unspent at the end of 2025/26. Spending that year included a R567 million write-off of set-top-box inventory, and there is still no analogue switch-off date.

2026-10-05-ipris-african-telecom-regulat.summary: A European-funded regulatory capacity programme is holding its eighth cohort in Nairobi from 5 to 9 October. Regulators from Liberia, Mauritius, Namibia, Sierra Leone, Tanzania and Zimbabwe are taking part with three regional regulators' associations.

2026-10-05-itweb-tlou-kala-data-centre-e.summary: Tlou Energy's annual report says Botswana's gas-powered Kala Data Centre ran well below its design of about 1MW in the year to June 2026, for lack of gas from the one connected well. The company has begun planning a pipeline from a second well, and any expansion depends on gas supply and funding.

2026-10-05-kenyas-health-system-has-a-gh.summary: A newspaper column asks what Kenya's Sh104.8 billion health digitisation contract of 2024 paid for, now that hospitals are being moved from one Social Health Authority system to another. It cites a 2025 patient-group survey in which six in ten respondents said they had been denied care at least once over system failures.

2026-10-05-minette-libom-li-likeng-patnu.summary: Cameroon's posts and telecommunications minister handed four platforms built under the World Bank-financed digital transformation project to the agriculture ministry on 1 October. They cover e-learning for training schools, a soil-fertility map and agro-pastoral statistics, and soil sampling was launched the same day.

2026-10-05-namibia-digital-trade-afcfta-.summary: Namibia's assessment of its laws and institutions against the African free-trade area's Protocol on Digital Trade went to a validation workshop in Windhoek. It will feed a National Digital Trade Action Plan; no findings are published.

2026-10-05-nga-vanguard-inec-voter-regis.summary: Nigeria's electoral commission chairman said the national register of voters stands at more than 103 million after the final biometric clean-up. Three phases of continuous registration added 10,772,421 voters, and card collection begins nationwide on 9 October.

2026-10-05-regional-afreximbank-eabc-afr.summary: Afreximbank made the East African Business Council a trade corridor partner of its Africa Trade Gateway, to bring the region's firms onto its matchmaking, trade finance and payment services. The bank puts the gateway in more than 45 countries with 110 banks and 25,000 verified companies.

2026-10-05-sa-land-availability-edge-dat.summary: A market study by DC Byte puts Africa at 3% of the 93GW of data-centre capacity built or planned across Europe, the Middle East and Africa. It names available land as South Africa's advantage and the time taken to deliver power as its constraint.

2026-10-05-sle-techreview-ai-roadmap-jus.summary: Sierra Leone's judiciary and the attorney-general's office are to draft a national artificial-intelligence roadmap for the justice sector with UNESCO, beginning with the security sector. Participants at the convening pointed to electronic filing and digital case management; no timetable is given.

2026-10-05-som-itweb-mobile-money-silos.summary: The chief executive of Somalia's SomLink Telecom says voice calls now interconnect across six operators while mobile-money wallets remain closed to one another. He calls for cost-based pricing and shared rails, and says the largest operators have little commercial reason to open up.

2026-10-05-swz-times-e182m-data-centre-l.summary: Eswatini's finance ministry says the E182 million India Exim Bank loan for a disaster recovery site at Siteki has not been cancelled. What the minister meant in Parliament was the commitment fee on the undrawn balance, which the lender has agreed to stop; 1% of the loan has been drawn.

2026-10-05-tariq-malik-export-dpi-mistak.summary: Tariq Malik, a World Bank identity adviser, argues that countries sharing digital public infrastructure should export their mistakes as well as their expertise. He proposes an exit test for partnerships and a published time-to-redress, and cites Malawi's enrolment of about nine million adults in roughly 180 days.

2026-10-05-tun-chourouk-ministere-tic-pr.summary: Tunisia's communications ministry announced child-protection measures resting on a telecommunications regulator's decision of 10 June 2026. Internet providers must offer parental controls covering site blacklists, device management and access-time limits, tell subscribers about them and write a child-protection clause into contracts.

2026-10-05-usaasa-usaf-manual-approved.summary: South Africa's universal service agency says the communications minister has approved the manual for the Universal Service and Access Fund, setting its objectives, governance, funding instruments and accountability. An earlier draft was withdrawn in November 2025 and a revised one went out for comment in February 2026.

2026-10-05-wearetech-burundi-e-justice-c.summary: Burundi is preparing an E-Justice platform to link the penal chain from the judicial police to the prisons, with online complaints and case tracking for citizens. An earlier programme digitised more than 15,000 case files, and the article sets the plan against an internet use rate of about 11%.

2026-10-05-xaf-techreviewafrica-au-eu-in.summary: The African Union's infrastructure and energy commissioner and the European Union's ambassador to the AU reviewed cooperation after their seventh summit. On digital infrastructure they covered the continental digital transformation and artificial-intelligence strategies and European support for regulation and data governance.

2026-10-05-xgl-rand-emerging-digital-bat.summary: A RAND study of the contest between the United States and China over third countries' digital networks finds that cost, bundled offers and presence on the ground give China structural advantages. The authors set out five priorities for the United States to close the gap.

2026-10-05-xwa-biometricupdate-ecowas-bi.summary: ECOWAS is running public campaigns in Ghana and Nigeria ahead of its December 2026 target for all member states to accept its biometric identity card at air, land and sea borders. Seven member states have issued the card so far.

2026-10-05-zamtel-myzamtel-super-app.summary: Zambia's Zamtel launched a self-care application with a build-your-own-bundle option, and Kongola Malaiti, a digital financial service reached by short code. No user figures are given.

2026-10-05-zarc-15m-za-domains.summary: South Africa's domain registry reports 1.5 million active registrations across its four commercial second-level namespaces. It says that makes .ZA the first African country-code domain to reach the mark.

2026-10-06-bfa-cfinance-222-procedures-d.summary: Burkina Faso's digital ministry reports 46.70% average physical execution of its minister's 20-action objectives contract at 30 June 2026. In the half year it described 222 administrative procedures for moving online, connected 10 more sites to the government network, counted 120 official platforms hosted abroad for repatriation and drafted nine implementing texts for the information-systems security law.

2026-10-06-cert-sc-takes-the-lead-in-thi.summary: Seychelles' national computer emergency response team designed and delivered the country's third national cyberdrill itself for the first time. The two-day exercise tests how organisations detect, respond to and recover from cyberattacks.

2026-10-06-cog-brazzavillois-ins-commerc.summary: Congo's statistics institute held a workshop in Brazzaville on 2 October to set up a permanent statistical system for informal cross-border trade. A mapping of border crossings is under way, a baseline survey is planned for 2027 and quarterly collection is to feed the balance of payments, with World Bank support.

2026-10-06-cs-duale-calls-for-timely-tra.summary: Kenya's health cabinet secretary urged providers to meet the timelines for moving from the insurer's provider portal to the health management information system and for completing the 2026-2029 contracting cycle. The ministry puts migration at 6,427 public facilities, 38 certified private facilities and 38 of 518 faith-based ones, and says correctly submitted claims will still be paid during the change.

2026-10-06-dza-algerieeco-aps-assamaka-e.summary: The Algerian account of the Assamaka ceremony, summarised above, says the link was built by Algerie Telecom and Niger Telecom, starts at 100 Gbps and can be expanded as traffic grows.

2026-10-06-foundation-sues-as-tiktok-res.summary: The Foundation for Digital Justice filed a fundamental-rights suit against TikTok at the Federal High Court in Abuja on 5 October. It alleges that users in Kaduna, Kano, Kebbi and Sokoto states have been restricted since mid-September while the rest of Nigeria keeps full access, and asks for an order restoring it.

2026-10-06-gab-gabonmailinfos-porte-paro.summary: Gabon's presidential spokesman said on radio that he uses a VPN, outside the law, to get round the social-media suspension the communications authority imposed in February 2026. The outlet reports the suspension still in force and the authority silent on any sanction.

2026-10-06-gauteng-transport-department-.summary: Gauteng's transport department launched a digital system to clear its backlog of public-transport operating licences, after six to eight months of testing with e-hailing, taxi and bus operators, municipalities and law enforcement. E-hailing operators are first in line to regularise.

2026-10-06-gmb-observer-gid-court-cannot.summary: A Gambia Immigration Department officer told a court on 6 October that the department can no longer reach data generated under the former Semlex biometric ID system, its access having ended with the contract. That leaves open who holds the historical identity records, although Semlex says it handed the system to the government in March 2024.

2026-10-06-gnq-gqpress-boletin-oficial-d.summary: Equatorial Guinea's government announced a digital edition of its official gazette at boe.gob.gq, giving free online access to laws, decrees, ministerial orders and circulars with search of past publications.

2026-10-06-government-institutions-urged.summary: Opening Kenya's National Customer Service Week, the public service principal secretary told government institutions that good service is a standard citizens are entitled to and that the week's exhibitions should be used to listen to them.

2026-10-06-ict-minister-mavetera-directs.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT minister asked the telecommunications regulator to consider a dedicated unit to oversee operators' commercial arrangements, mediate disputes and enforce active infrastructure sharing. She also wants the Universal Service Fund to reach every marginalised ward and the regulator's sharing and tower-relocation directives evaluated in 2027.

2026-10-06-itweb-bofinet-launches-digita.summary: Botswana's state fibre operator BoFiNet announced the launch of the Digital Delta Internet Exchange Point, where service providers, mobile operators and content and cloud providers can exchange local traffic inside the country. It builds on the operator's Tier III-certified data centre.

2026-10-06-ken-kenyans-e-notification-bi.summary: Kenya will extend electronic birth notification to every hospital contracted by the Social Health Authority within three months, by December 2026, the immigration principal secretary said. Newborns notified this way receive a Unique Personal Identifier, and talks with the health ministry on linking civil registration to hospital systems are complete.

2026-10-06-ken-techafricanews-kcb-stima-.summary: KCB Bank Kenya and Stima Sacco launched a link that lets the Sacco's members deposit straight into their accounts through the bank's mobile application. KCB says its digital Sacco products have grown from 345 to 407, without dating either count.

2026-10-06-ken-techcabal-equity-finserve.summary: Equity Bank's fintech arm, Finserve Africa, has launched a wallet called EMMA, reached by Android application, short code or the Equitel SIM toolkit and opened with an identity document and a facial check. Users can send money to M-PESA merchants, Airtel Money and bank accounts; the analysis reads it as the bank's bid to keep everyday payments, and the data behind them, on its own platform.

2026-10-06-kzn-launches-the-public-works.summary: KwaZulu-Natal is launching a portal listing its public works properties, after an audit of all 10,067 assets and the release of a first batch of 81 unused buildings and land parcels. Organisations and developers can identify assets to lease or reuse, and residents can log complaints about them.

2026-10-06-lbr-fpa-lisgis-ecowas-statist.summary: A week-long ECOWAS training for managers of member states' national statistical systems opened in Monrovia on 5 October. The head of Liberia's statistics office said statisticians need training to use AI in data collection properly, and warned that it can harm the data as well as help.

2026-10-06-moz-clubofmozambique-atdi-des.summary: Mozambique's digital transformation agency held the country's first Digital Service Delivery Design Lab, bringing public bodies and partners together to pick priority services, map how citizens use them now and redesign them. The process runs in five stages, ending in assigned responsibilities and action plans.

2026-10-06-ner-anp-assamaka-dorsale-tran.summary: Niger and Algeria launched operation of the fibre link between In Guezzam and the Arlit-Agadez region at a ceremony at Assamaka, on the border, on 6 October, chaired by the two communications ministers. Algeria's account gives a starting capacity of 100 Gbps.

2026-10-06-ner-anp-caravane-wuri-niamey.summary: The Niamey stage of Niger's national awareness caravan on civil registration and identification opened on 6 October under the World Bank-supported WURI project. The two-day session is to take stock of the caravan's regional stages; the project has been restructured to speed up civil registration and biometric identification.

2026-10-06-ner-mcnti-niger-algerie-inter.summary: Niger's communications ministry reported its minister's arrival at Agadez on 5 October with an Algerian delegation, describing the mission as the launch of fibre interconnection works between the two countries; the ceremony itself is summarised above.

2026-10-06-nigerias-ncc-to-leverage-itu-.summary: Nigeria's Digital Bridge Institute has been designated an ITU Digital Transformation Centre, and the communications regulator says it will use the status to widen digital skills training for underserved groups. The work is tied to the national target of 95% digital literacy by 2030.

2026-10-06-nigerias-ndpc-noa-sign-mou-to.summary: Nigeria's data protection commission and the National Orientation Agency signed a memorandum on joint public awareness work. It covers training for the agency's staff, coordinated campaigns across traditional and digital media, and guidance on applying the 2023 data-protection Act to the agency's own mandate.

2026-10-06-paperless-courts-spread-to-mi.summary: Zimbabwe's Judicial Service Commission took its electronic case management system live in Midlands and Mashonaland West provinces on 1 October, after installing recording and transcription machines and issuing computers to court staff. Litigants and lawyers can file and follow cases online.

2026-10-06-problem-with-plan-for-digital.summary: South Africa's Home Affairs missed its first-quarter target to sign a work order starting procurement of digital ID hosting infrastructure, its quarterly report to Parliament's committee says. It also missed revising the National Identification Registration Bill for public comment, and now aims to finalise the procurement in the second quarter.

2026-10-06-sdn-sudanese-banks-and-the-po.summary: An opinion piece argues that Sudan's banks are investing too slowly in electronic services at a moment when war and high inflation have made cash costly and risky and disrupted branch networks. The author presents the post-war period as a chance to build an economy less dependent on cash.

2026-10-06-sen-apanews-ai-judicial-archi.summary: A high court in the Dakar suburbs has begun piloting a locally deployed AI application to digitise, manage and analyse judicial archives, with UNDP and Korean funding. Computing and digitisation equipment was handed to the justice ministry's dematerialisation directorate, and a phased national rollout is planned with no cost or timetable stated.

2026-10-06-sen-aps-senegal-digital-facto.summary: Senegal's telecommunications ministry signed a US$150 million partnership convention, nearly CFA 88 billion, with an Africa investment council and the Indian firm Blue Cloud Softech Solutions under the Senegal Digital Factory project. It covers local assembly of electronic devices, quality control, certification and intellectual property; the ministry puts computer hardware imports at CFA 419 billion a year.

2026-10-06-sen-aps-senum-smtd-backbone-i.summary: Senegal's and Mali's state fibre operators inaugurated the interconnection of their national backbones at the Kidira-Diboli border crossing on 5 October, to secure and diversify routes between the two countries. No capacity or cost is given.

2026-10-06-sle-sierraloaded-nra-asycuda-.summary: Sierra Leone's revenue authority has begun consultations with security agencies and local stakeholders at the Jendema border crossing as it prepares to launch the ASYCUDA World customs system there. The system will automate import, export and transit procedures; no launch date is given.

2026-10-06-som-somalia-moves-to-link-nat.summary: Somalia's identity authority is moving to link its registration services to HALMEEL, the national unified public service delivery centre, where an area has been set aside for it. The aim is one national identity across several government services; the integration is planned and not yet in place.

2026-10-06-swz-who-was-held-accountable-.summary: Eswatini senators asked on 5 October whether anyone had been held to account for the pension crisis at the state posts and telecommunications corporation, after Parliament approved the government guarantee for its US$26 million World Bank loan under the Digital Eswatini Project. The ICT minister said E26 million of the loan goes to the post office pension fund, affecting about 500 employees, and that the bank will manage and audit the loan.

2026-10-06-tanesco-modernizes-its-custom.summary: Tanzania's energy minister launched new customer service systems for the state power utility on 6 October: an AI-powered assistant available round the clock, a portal and a dedicated unit for large customers, and a 185 hotline, with a revised service charter.

2026-10-06-techcabal-airtel-money-ipo-ni.summary: Airtel Money's London listing leaves out its Nigerian business. Its prospectus, as reported, says a Central Bank of Nigeria directive required it to transfer its 25% stake in SmartCash back to Airtel's Nigerian network company, for US$3 million; Nigeria made up 1.24% of the unit's quarterly revenue and 6.02% of its customers at June 2026.

2026-10-06-techcabal-south-africans-bypa.summary: Half of 903 South Africans surveyed had got round their employer's restrictions on AI tools in the past year, an Oliver Wyman partner told a cybersecurity roundtable in Johannesburg, citing a report due in November. He said 35% had seen AI-generated work passed off as human, and that consumer trust in AI rose from 11% in 2023 to 44% in 2026.

2026-10-06-tgo-republicoftogo-voix-du-to.summary: Togo's Voix du Togo pilot, backed by UNDP, is collecting voice and text in Kabiye, Ewe and Moba to train AI models for public services in local languages. Contributors are paid through a dedicated platform, linguists and communities validate the data, and field agents collect it where phones and internet are scarce.

2026-10-06-tiktok-sued-over-nigeria-blac.summary: A second report of the suit over TikTok access in four northern Nigerian states, summarised above, frames it as a test of platform accountability and digital rights.

2026-10-06-tun-techafricanews-orange-foc.summary: Orange Tunisie and Focus Tunisie announced a partnership to offer companies cloud and infrastructure resources hosted and operated in Tunisia, pitched on control over where data sits. No value, capacity or start date is given.

2026-10-06-tun-tuniscope-interieur-casie.summary: Tunisia's interior ministry, answering a deputy's written question, said its plan for the criminal-record extract rests on digitising the record through interconnection with the justice ministry, to update judgments, and the finance ministry, to enter fines automatically. The aim is faster issue of the extract.

2026-10-06-uga-monitor-ag-2021-digital-n.summary: Uganda's Attorney General told a parliamentary committee that the supplier of the digital number plate system has consistently failed the core obligations of its 2021 contract, which the newspaper reports him declaring null and illegal. Defaults cited include no training of Ugandan staff and no transfer of the system's technology to the state enterprise.

2026-10-06-uga-nilepost-fitspa-fintech-c.summary: Fintech firms, regulators and development partners at Uganda's eighth annual fintech conference called for interoperable systems, shared digital infrastructure and stronger data standards, to move from separate products towards connected services.

2026-10-06-vodacom-western-cape-invests-.summary: Vodacom says it is investing more than R500 million in its Western Cape network this financial year. About R380 million goes to modernising the radio network at more than 50 sites, with 4G capacity upgrades, new 5G sites and backup power in townships including Khayelitsha, Delft and Mitchells Plain.

2026-10-06-woan-is-dead-but-measurable-i.summary: South Africa's withdrawal of the requirement to reserve high-demand spectrum for a wireless open access network ends a seven-year impasse and frees that spectrum for licensing by the regulator. Commentators in this analysis ask how the competition and transformation aims the network was meant to serve will now be delivered, and press for measurable obligations in its place.

2026-10-06-xaf-connectingafrica-saudi-ai.summary: An analysis asks whether Saudi Arabia's spending on data centres, AI and cloud can reach Africa while the kingdom is under attack from the Houthis. It cites the US$300 million committed to the infrastructure company WIOCC by a Saudi investor with the Africa Finance Corporation, and an investor's view that the conflict does not reduce Saudi capacity to do business.

2026-10-06-xaf-ictworks-fcdo-78-question.summary: A commentary notes that across 78 questions at the UK development minister's first parliamentary scrutiny session on 15 September, nobody raised digital development, connectivity or digital public infrastructure. The author reads that as the sector being moved out of the development brief rather than merely short of budget.

2026-10-06-xaf-techcabal-amr-data-gap.summary: A contributed analysis argues that Africa's response to antimicrobial resistance is held back by missing laboratory data. It cites a WHO estimate that one in five laboratory-confirmed bacterial infections in its African Region in 2023 was resistant to antibiotics, a figure that cannot count infections never tested.

2026-10-06-xss-reuters-world-bank-africa.summary: The World Bank's October Africa Economic Update urges Sub-Saharan governments to invest in AI for productivity and jobs, pointing to low-cost applications on affordable devices, shared data centres and stronger data-protection laws. It puts the region's 2026 growth at 4.3%, 0.3 of a point above its April forecast.

2026-10-06-zambia-ready-to-sign-us-healt.summary: Zambia's health minister said the five-year health memorandum with the United States is finalised and due for signature this week, after negotiators removed a clause requiring Zambia to share specimens from its disease-surveillance system. The revised text also addresses health data, intellectual property and benefit sharing; this account puts US funding at US$1.5 billion over five years, tapering annually, and an opposition party wants the final text published before signing.

2026-10-06-zambia-us-finalise-3-6-billio.summary: A second account of the Zambian health minister's briefing puts the money to be mobilised for the sector at US$3.6 billion and gives Thursday as the signing day. The minister said the contested clauses on data protection, intellectual property, benefit sharing and specimens have all been reviewed, and that the specimen-sharing obligation is gone entirely.

2026-10-06-zimbabwe-eyes-indias-upi-tech.summary: Zimbabwe's central bank is negotiating with NPCI International to build a real-time payments system on India's UPI technology, linking banks, mobile-money operators and fintechs. The governor told Bloomberg an agreement is possible by 31 October 2026; cross-border payments and remittances are not part of the first deployment.

2026-10-07-10th-afrigeo-symposium-opens-.summary: The tenth symposium of Africa's earth observation community opened at Nigeria's space centre in Abuja. The head of the Nigerian space agency urged participants to turn data into intelligence that feeds decisions.

2026-10-07-africanenda-trains-journalist.summary: AfricaNenda says its payments regulation initiative with the African Union Commission has moved to implementation after a feasibility study found a harmonised framework workable. The study names eight priority areas, licence passporting and interoperability standards among them, and a phased roadmap.

2026-10-07-ai-takes-the-bench-before-the.summary: South Africa's judiciary has not finalised its draft policy on artificial intelligence, which a judges' conference in July sent to a steering committee to complete. Judges have meanwhile used a chatbot in rulings, in one case to reconcile payments and in another to test fabricated citations.

2026-10-07-c-te-d-ivoire-terrakora-ai-si.summary: Cote d'Ivoire's environment ministry signed a framework memorandum with an Ivorian company to map land use, monitor environmental change and estimate carbon stocks from satellite data, field observation and AI. The 2021 forest inventory put forest cover at 2.97 million hectares, 9.2% of the territory.

2026-10-07-cemac-la-beac-annonce-la-crat.summary: Closing a bankers' meeting at Bangui on 3 October, the governor of the Central African regional central bank announced a secondary market for debt, with other work to modernise payments and deepen the regional financial market.

2026-10-07-dpgs-for-dpi-collection-launc.summary: The Digital Public Goods Alliance launched a collection of 18 digital public goods for digital public infrastructure on 7 October at a regional forum in Santo Domingo. Each was assessed against technical criteria across identity, payments, data exchange, registries and trust systems.

2026-10-07-egypt-personal-data-protectio.summary: Egypt's Personal Data Protection Center opened its electronic portal for accreditation, licence and permit applications in early October, weeks before the data-protection law's compliance grace period ends on 31 October 2026, on a law firm's account. Applying needs a Digital Egypt login tied to an Egyptian national ID, so foreign controllers and processors must act through an authorised local representative.

2026-10-07-finguard-swz-smart-africa-gen.summary: A magazine account of the same Eswatini pilot of Smart Africa's gender impact assessment framework, which is meant to test whether digital programmes narrow the divide facing women. It names the tools differently from the ministry's account.

2026-10-07-gab-gabonreview-huawei-souver.summary: Huawei's Gabon subsidiary was received by the vice-president of the government on 6 October and restated its offer to support the state's digital transformation, in infrastructure, energy, cybersecurity and skills transfer. No agreement is reported.

2026-10-07-gab-union-magt-etat-conventio.summary: Gabon's incumbent operator and the digital-economy ministry signed a convention at Mouila on 6 October ceding to the State the 196 km Fougamou-Mouila fibre section the operator pre-financed and built, with two technical centres. It is the first segment of the first phase of the national backbone extension.

2026-10-07-gender-checks-proposed-for-di.summary: Eswatini's ICT minister, opening the gender impact assessment workshop in Mbabane, said the government wants such assessments built into digital policies and programmes before they are implemented.

2026-10-07-govt-steps-up-safety-against-.summary: Kenya's ICT minister told the Senate that the national incident response centre's digital forensics laboratory has received more than 200 investigation requests, most involving online abuse. A working group on online safety, a national referral directory and a review of gaps in the law have been agreed.

2026-10-07-moz-timesdetodos-metical-sadc.summary: Mozambique's central bank governor said the metical could be used for payments between Southern African countries from January 2027 through the regional real-time settlement system, which is hosted at South Africa's central bank.

2026-10-07-mus-lexpress-mauritius-teleco.summary: Mauritius Telecom and Amazon Web Services brought more than 125 delegates from state-owned enterprises to an executive workshop on cloud, data and AI at Ebene on 6 October, to identify uses in public services.

2026-10-07-nigerian-company-milsat-techn.summary: Nigeria's communications minister named a Nigerian company as the builder of the technology behind the new national digital postcode, saying it moved from a 2023 pilot to the national system.

2026-10-07-obidients-want-inec-to-abando.summary: A Nigerian opposition movement called on the electoral commission to abandon its planned use of AI to verify the 2027 election results until the governance framework is published. It demands independent verification, traceability from polling unit to final collation and publication of the result forms.

2026-10-07-only-15-of-mozambicans-can-af.summary: A proposed Internet for All strategy for Mozambique, to be implemented by the communications regulator with targets to 2030, was presented in Maputo. A partner organisation said only 15% of the population can afford to keep a mobile data package, against about 5.6 million mobile internet subscribers in some 36 million people.

2026-10-07-regional-digitnomics-african-.summary: African payment companies are pressing for licence passporting, under which a firm licensed in one country could operate in others without starting again. It is part of the African Union Commission's work with AfricaNenda on cross-border payment rules.

2026-10-07-senegal-signs-deal-to-launch-.summary: Senegal's digital minister signed a memorandum on 6 October with an African investment council and an Indian technology company under the Senegal Digital Factory phase of the national digital strategy. A digital equipment assembly complex at Diamniadio is its centrepiece.

2026-10-07-sim-deactivation-now-backed-b.summary: Kenya's communications regulator told a National Assembly committee that SIM deactivation and number recycling now run under its 2026 procedures: notice to the subscriber's contact after three months' inactivity, a public notice and status check before recycling after six, and whitelisting for subscribers who are sick, imprisoned or deceased. It was answering a petition against the largest operator's recycling.

2026-10-07-south-africas-usaasa-publishe.summary: South Africa's universal service agency published the manual for its fund, a framework for how subsidies and project grants under the Electronic Communications Act are to be run. Procedures for applying and for payment are to follow separately.

2026-10-07-swz-independentnews-mict-smar.summary: Eswatini's ICT ministry and Smart Africa opened a workshop on 7 October to develop and pilot gender impact assessment tools for digital policy, with Eswatini and The Gambia as pilot countries. Three instruments are to be tested on selected digital policies before validation.

2026-10-07-techcabal-m-kopa-kilpitek.summary: M-KOPA's financial statements show it completed the US$8m acquisition of a Finnish device-locking software company on 26 March 2026, US$2.67m of it in cash. The purchase brings in-house the technology that restricts financed smartphones when customers fall behind.

2026-10-07-tiktoker-charged-over-alleged.summary: A TikTok user was charged in Kampala on 6 October with unlawfully obtaining and disclosing personal data under Uganda's data protection act, and with publishing false news, over a photograph and video of a State House employee. He denied the charges; the case returns on 19 October.

2026-10-07-uganda-launches-child-online-.summary: Uganda's communications regulator launched a child online protection campaign at a Kampala secondary school, to teach children to recognise and manage online risks. The ICT permanent secretary called on parents, schools, technology companies and government to share the work.

2026-10-07-wearetech-djibouti-oif-cybers.summary: The Francophonie organisation and Djibouti's education and vocational training ministry signed an agreement to train 200 young people in web and mobile development and in network infrastructure and cybersecurity. It extends a programme that the organisation says has trained 200 since 2022.

2026-10-07-wearetech-leatherback-foren.summary: The cross-border payments company Leatherback has renamed itself Foren, after its acquisition by a Nigerian financial group in July 2026.

2026-10-07-wearetech-rwanda-slovakia-ai-.summary: Rwanda's ICT minister received Slovakia's ambassador on 6 October to discuss widening the two countries' cybersecurity cooperation to artificial intelligence, space and digital skills. Nothing was signed.

2026-10-08-ago-pti-lourenco-regime-assin.summary: Angola's Law 12/26 of 2 October authorises the President to legislate the regime for electronic signatures and digital certification and the rules of the national public key infrastructure, within 90 days.

2026-10-08-ben-beninwebtv-quatre-etablis.summary: Four companies held a payment institution licence in Benin at 31 August 2026, on the BCEAO's list: Julaya, Open SI, FedaPay and QOS, of 34 across the monetary union. Two of the four were licensed in 2026.

2026-10-08-ben-lanation-semo-plus-missio.summary: Benin launched Semo+, which lets an official prove a mission took place from a mobile application using geolocation and biometric identification tied to the personal identification number. It replaces the visa obtained at a police station.

2026-10-08-bi-gasape-chat-presidency.summary: Burundi's presidency adopted Gasape Chat, a locally built messaging application, as a channel for citizens' grievances. The terms were not disclosed, and analysts noted that nothing says who controls the servers or protects users' data.

2026-10-08-caf-corbeaunews-cellule-veill.summary: An opposition-leaning outlet attacks the communication-monitoring cell created by decree under the Central African Republic's government spokesperson, calling it an instrument against critics on social media.

2026-10-08-camtel-and-minesec-sign-deal-.summary: CAMTEL and Cameroon's secondary education ministry signed a framework agreement to interconnect 130 schools in the Adamawa, North and Far North regions. No amount was stated.

2026-10-08-camtel-partners-with-sic-to-e.summary: CAMTEL signed a framework agreement with Cameroon's state housing company to bring fibre to its existing estates and build it into new ones. Residents are offered a connection at FCFA 25,000 and FCFA 15,000 a month.

2026-10-08-cm-civil-registration-funding.summary: Cameroon needs more than FCFA 50 billion, about US$85 million, to digitise civil registration fully by 2029-2030, the head of the civil status office said. A public-private partnership is planned, and several decrees under the 2024 law are still to be made.

2026-10-08-cod-acp-digitalisation-secteu.summary: The DRC's land affairs minister said implementation of the December 2025 land law has begun: digitisation directorates created and more than 350 officials trained in archiving. Three of Kinshasa's nine land districts are in the first phase, toward a geolocated digital cadastre.

2026-10-08-cod-actu7-kibassa-skolkovo-te.summary: The DRC's digital economy minister visited the Skolkovo innovation centre near Moscow as a model for a technology park and sovereign data centre planned for Kinshasa's extension zone. No site, cost or timetable is given.

2026-10-08-egy-sis-communications-labor-.summary: Egypt's communications and labour ministries signed a memorandum to digitise the labour ministry's work and run digital-skills programmes for its staff, graduates and job seekers.

2026-10-08-ethiopia-appoints-ethio-telec.summary: Ethiopia's parliament approved Ethio Telecom chief executive Frehiwot Tamru as Minister of Innovation and Technology in the new cabinet. She had led the state operator since 2018.

2026-10-08-gab-agp-banque-mondiale-refon.summary: The World Bank's 2026 public finance review of Gabon recommends connecting the Digitax tax platform to the economy ministry's other systems; the new property-tax software runs in isolation. It also urges cross-checking tax data with banks and the utility.

2026-10-08-gab-agp-indra-ministre-sante-.summary: Spanish technology group Indra presented Gabon's health minister with a patient platform covering electronic medical records, vaccination records and teleconsultation, and a virtual health map. No agreement was announced.

2026-10-08-gha-ghanaiantimes-kokma-ai-lo.summary: Accra's Korle Klottey Municipal Assembly is seeking international partners to use AI in local government, its chief executive said after a city forum in Seoul. He cited the assembly's digital mapping of properties and businesses for revenue.

2026-10-08-gha-ghanaweb-attafuah-id-ecos.summary: A former head of Ghana's identification authority said the Ghana Card's value lies in trusted identity services, not the card. He put enrolment at 20.1 million and cards issued at 19.2 million as of 17 August 2026.

2026-10-08-gha-techafricanews-csa-ot-cri.summary: Ghana's communications minister said compliance with cybersecurity requirements is mandatory for the 13 designated critical information infrastructure sectors and about 200 owner institutions. He was opening a workshop on securing industrial control systems.

2026-10-08-gin-armp-dgcmp-banque-mondial.summary: Guinea's procurement regulator, the control directorate and the World Bank reviewed the Télémo e-procurement platform, in a new phase of use since September. The price reference list and public-private partnerships are not yet integrated, and a new procurement law is being drafted.

2026-10-08-ken-gpsdd-idc-action-plan-202.summary: Kenya drafted its second Inclusive Data Charter action plan, for 2026 to 2030, at a workshop on 5 to 7 October. It widens the first plan's focus on disability to gender, children and older persons.

2026-10-08-ken-the-star-spacex-fcc-15000.summary: US regulatory approval for up to 15,000 SpaceX direct-to-device satellites could expose Kenyan mobile operators to competition from space, this analysis argues. Safaricom's mobile data revenue passed voice for the first time in the year to March 2026.

2026-10-08-latimes-u-s-zambia-sign-2-49-.summary: Zambia and the United States signed their five-year health financing memorandum in Lusaka after clauses on specimen sharing and patient data were removed. The State Department put it at US$2.49 billion, US$1.52 billion from the United States and US$975 million from Zambia, and Zambia said minerals were not part of it.

2026-10-08-lbr-police-online-clearance-u.summary: Liberia's online police clearance system has generated more than US$200,000 since May 2026, the deputy information minister said. No figure for the manual system it replaced was given.

2026-10-08-lby-lana-us-strategic-coopera.summary: Libya's communications authority and the US State Department signed a cooperation framework in Washington covering digital infrastructure, AI, data centres, cybersecurity and satellite communications. No programme or amount was published.

2026-10-08-m-kopa-reaches-10-million-cus.summary: M-KOPA reported revenue of US$600 million for its 2025 financial year, up 45%, and ten million customers since 2011 across Kenya, Nigeria, Ghana, Uganda and South Africa.

2026-10-08-mar-maroc24-ausim-ia-2030-sou.summary: Morocco's digital transition minister set out five priorities for the 'Maroc IA 2030' roadmap, among them bringing sovereign compute into service and completing the legal framework for AI. The roadmap aims to add MAD 100 billion to GDP by 2030.

2026-10-08-mdg-allafrica-tana-digitalisa.summary: Antananarivo's urban commune began digitalising its markets: traders are registered on tablet and issued chip and QR cards debited by collectors' payment terminals in place of paper tickets. Markets bring the commune MGA 7 to 9 billion a year.

2026-10-08-mdg-sputnik-ministre-souverai.summary: Madagascar's digital development minister said sovereignty means controlling infrastructure and data while staying open to foreign expertise. AI is at an early stage but already used by customs for risk analysis.

2026-10-08-moz-bcl-estrategia-internet-p.summary: Mozambique's regulator is validating a proposed national 'Internet para Todos' strategy with operators, academia and civil society, with targets to 2030. Figures presented put internet access at about 20% of the population.

2026-10-08-moz-mznews-certificacao-digit.summary: A Mozambican government team is training in Brasília until 16 October on public key infrastructure and digital certification, ahead of a national certification system. A digital signature pilot at home involves about 40 entities.

2026-10-08-moz-pav-pawapay-licensed-psp.summary: The Bank of Mozambique licensed payments aggregator PawaPay as a payment service provider through its local subsidiary, among the first such licences. It can now onboard merchants directly across the country's three mobile money operators.

2026-10-08-mus-mitci-meta-online-abuse.summary: Mauritius's ICT ministry met Meta on faster removal of fake accounts, impersonation and illegal content, moderation in Kreol and a local presence for the company. Amendments to the 2021 cybercrime law and age assurance for children were also discussed.

2026-10-08-nam-biometricupdate-mps-digit.summary: Namibian MPs questioned the planned digital ID on rural reach, cost, data ownership and cybersecurity at a briefing by two ministries. The rollout planned for September was delayed because the legal framework had not been finalised.

2026-10-08-nam-nampa-cabinet-mict-online.summary: Namibia's Cabinet directed the ICT ministry to develop a standard template for reporting which government services are available online.

2026-10-08-nam-techafricanews-paratus-eu.summary: Paratus Namibia launched Eutelsat's OneWeb low earth orbit satellite service across Namibia, with capped and uncapped packages for homes and businesses.

2026-10-08-nga-cbn-insists-on-january-1-.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria said its 1 January 2027 deadline for storing payment transaction data in Nigeria has not changed. Industry executives warned that a rushed migration carries operational and security risk.

2026-10-08-nga-nan-orodata-csos-frontier.summary: Nigerian research group Orodata published a brief urging civil society to take part in governing frontier AI. It warns that voluntary commitments by technology companies are no substitute for enforceable rules.

2026-10-08-openzambia-zambia-and-us-sign.summary: Zambia and the United States signed a five-year health memorandum and a data sharing agreement. On this account the agreement exchanges only aggregated, de-identified programme data, with Zambia keeping ownership under its own laws; the health minister said the money will fund 40,000 health workers.

2026-10-08-opt-out-registry-arrives-as-m.summary: South Africa's opt-out registry is to be enforced from April 2027, sixteen years after it was first proposed. The direct marketing industry is meanwhile moving from contact databases to targeted digital advertising.

2026-10-08-pesalink-s-new-id-makes-bank-.summary: Kenya's bank-owned instant payment switch says a portable identifier is ready, so a sender need not know the recipient's bank, and institutions must now map customers to it. A fintech association asks who will own the rail as the alias takes hold.

2026-10-08-rwa-ktpress-bnr-digital-agri-.summary: Rwanda's central bank is piloting a digital agricultural lending platform meant to cut farmers' wait for a loan from five to seven weeks to under 48 hours. The six-month pilot began in September 2026 with two microfinance institutions and two banks; a national rollout is planned for 2027.

2026-10-08-rwa-nida-temporarily-suspends.summary: Rwanda's identification agency suspended the photography exercise for the digital identity card and gave no date for resuming it. Pre-enrolment through Irembo continues, and residents are asked to correct civil-registration details first.

2026-10-08-sle-blacknews-iprp-dismisses-.summary: Sierra Leone's procurement review panel dismissed a bidder's complaint over the evaluation of the World Bank-funded government network contract. It directed the ministry to open financial proposals and proceed to award.

2026-10-08-ssd-caretaker-finance-ministe.summary: South Sudan's caretaker finance minister called for digital payment systems that reach rural areas, to ease the demand for physical cash, at a workshop on the liquidity crisis.

2026-10-08-starlink-rival-maps-out-sa-st.summary: Amazon Leo said it has applied for licences to bring a direct-to-device satellite service to South Africa with mobile operators, probably from around 2028. Its fixed satellite broadband is to be distributed by Herotel from 2027.

2026-10-08-swz-escom-national-cyber-dril.summary: Eswatini held its first national cyber drill on 5 October: a multi-sector ransomware simulation for energy, telecoms, government, aviation, health and finance, facilitated by Lesotho's regulator. The communications commission showed a prototype incident-sharing platform.

2026-10-08-tgo-atop-kozah-dialogue-gouve.summary: Community groups in Togo's Kara region were briefed on the risks and uses of AI at a regional dialogue run by two associations with outside funding, part of a citizen dialogue project on AI governance.

2026-10-08-tza-mwigulunchemba-pm-meets-s.summary: Tanzania's prime minister met SpaceX and Starlink representatives in London on 7 October about investment in the communications sector, with three ministers present. No outcome was stated.

2026-10-08-uga-itweb-child-online-protec.summary: Uganda launched a nationwide child online protection campaign at a Kampala secondary school. A regulator survey of students there found 88.5% had met digital harm and 74.2% of those exposed had told no one.

2026-10-08-uga-techtrendske-mam-telecom-.summary: Ugandan startup MAM Telecom received a US$250,000 grant from an unnamed South African businessman to license and build a settlement platform that lets mobile-money agents obtain digital float. It has not launched.

2026-10-08-uga-ucc-child-online-protecti.summary: A second account of the Uganda Communications Commission's child online protection campaign, launched during cybersecurity awareness month and aimed at children, parents and teachers.

2026-10-08-xaf-techafricanews-single-who.summary: Ghana, Rwanda and South Africa have each moved away from the single wholesale network model for mobile broadband. Commercial sharing of towers, fibre and spectrum between operators is replacing it.

2026-10-08-za-icasa-regulate-when-not-to.summary: ICASA's chairperson said the regulator has developed a draft satellite licensing framework and will use sandboxes and lighter-touch approaches beside licensing. He named data centres and cloud computing as infrastructure it must now address.

2026-10-08-za-spam-calls-opt-out-registr.summary: South Africa's consumer commission launched a national opt-out registry against a count of 17.5 billion spam calls in the first half of 2026. Marketers must register and clean their lists monthly before any campaign.

2026-10-08-zwe-herald-papss-5-8-million-.summary: Afreximbank said Zimbabwe is processing US$5.8 million a month through the pan-African payment and settlement system. Yuan clearing is being brought onto the platform through its link to China's interbank system.

2026-10-08-zwe-herald-zrp-hit-crime-mana.summary: Zimbabwe's home affairs minister told the National Assembly that a crime management system built by the Harare Institute of Technology is running as a proof of concept at Warren Park and a few other police stations. Reporting crime by mobile phone is to follow, and wider deployment depends on the test.

2026-10-09-assabah-bank-al-maghrib-cbdc-.summary: Morocco's central bank published two research working papers on a central bank digital currency, one on the stakes and lessons for Morocco and one a modelling exercise. It presents them as its researchers' work, shared for debate.

2026-10-09-au-stc-cict-6th-ordinary-sess.summary: The African Union will hold the sixth ordinary session of its technical committee on communication and ICT in Libreville from 26 to 29 October 2026. The committee, which meets every two years, feeds the Executive Council on the Commission's ICT programmes.

2026-10-09-bfa-lefaso-zama-tche-maisons-.summary: Burkina Faso's digital-transition minister said 80 citizen service houses have been launched on a FCFA 10 billion envelope, against a target of one in each of 351 communes by 2030. She put the two modular data centres at FCFA 15 billion and a national data centre at an estimated FCFA 20 billion, and said digital identity enrolment was due to start in October.

2026-10-09-biometricupdate-nigeria-abis-.summary: Nigeria's electoral commission put the register at 103,428,715 voters after a biometric clean-up, with 10,772,421 new registrations since August 2025. Voter card collection began on 9 October, ahead of elections in January and February 2027.

2026-10-09-bnr-moves-to-tackle-delayed-e.summary: Rwanda's central bank said it is working with financial institutions on delayed and failed transfers on the national payment switch, with rejections below 2% by September. Active accounts rose from 2.03 million to 10.3 million in a year.

2026-10-09-cod-rdc-monde-dgi-facture-nor.summary: The DRC's tax directorate began nationwide checks of the standardised invoice on 5 October, after the moratorium ended. Consumers are asked to verify invoices by QR code in the official application, with rewards for verified reports of non-compliance.

2026-10-09-cybersecurity-rwandans-urged-.summary: Rwanda launched its 2026 cyber security and data protection awareness campaign in Kigali, the ICT minister citing online fraud, phishing and identity theft. The government technology agency counts about 2,000 digital ambassadors to carry it to communities.

2026-10-09-dza-prixalgerie-digital-ident.summary: Algeria's digitalisation commission set out how the national digital identity is obtained: registration and an appointment at the commune, activation, then verification against biometric data. It also said a national data-governance system that classifies data sources against one reference is under way.

2026-10-09-ecomatin-cemac-mobile-money-4.summary: Central Africa's seven licensed payment institutions processed 4.6 billion operations worth FCFA 44,037 billion in 2025, against 3.4 billion operations in 2024, on the banking commission's annual report. Two Cameroonian operators' services held 65.4% of the sector's income.

2026-10-09-eth-biometricupdate-fayda-dev.summary: Ethiopia opened a public sandbox where developers and startups can test the Fayda digital identity's authentication interfaces before going live. Fayda counted more than 52 million registrations, 150 integrated partners and 208 million electronic verifications.

2026-10-09-financialafrik-bceao-plafond-.summary: The West African central bank doubled the ceiling on electronic money one client may hold at one issuer to FCFA 4 million and raised monthly reloads from FCFA 10 million to FCFA 15 million. Issuers may go beyond them only with its prior authorisation.

2026-10-09-gab-gabonreview-etat-civil-at.summary: The workshop preparing Gabon's national civil-registration conferences closed with a diagnosis of badly kept archives, irregular data entry and a Civil Code dating from 1972. Its final report goes to the Interior minister, who sets the calendar.

2026-10-09-gab-gabonreview-poste-sa-akib.summary: Gabon's postal company presented Akiba, an application built and hosted in Gabon that combines payments, public services such as birth-certificate requests, postal services and insurance. A USSD version was announced; the app-store launch is still to come.

2026-10-09-gha-techafricanews-csa-reject.summary: A second account of the Ghana Cyber Security Authority's statement on Operation Blackout: it names the Ghanaian, British, American and Nigerian agencies that took part and says the operation ran under Ghanaian authority.

2026-10-09-ghana-csa-operation-blackout-.summary: Ghana's Cyber Security Authority said Ghana, not the FBI, led Operation Blackout, which arrested eight suspects and rescued 120 suspected trafficking victims at cybercrime centres in Greater Accra. It asked the FBI to correct its public account, saying foreign agencies have no police powers in Ghana.

2026-10-09-ghana-cybersecurity-essential.summary: Ghana's communications minister said the security of power, water, transport, health and financial services now depends on the control systems behind them, at a Cyber Security Authority workshop. He repeated that 13 critical sectors and about 200 institutions are designated.

2026-10-09-ghana-ghima-unlicensed-health.summary: Ghana's health information managers' association warned against unlicensed staff handling health records in facilities. It said the law requires a licence from the allied health professions council and that data quality and patient safety are at stake.

2026-10-09-ghana-miif-cyber-resilience-m.summary: The head of Ghana's minerals income fund called for stronger protection of the control systems that run mines, at a Cyber Security Authority workshop. She said an attack on them bears on safety, production and national revenue, not only on IT.

2026-10-09-ken-techafricanews-ict-state-.summary: Kenya's ICT principal secretary met Equity Group's chief executive on 6 October to explore working together on digital infrastructure, financial inclusion and regional trade. Nothing was signed.

2026-10-09-ken-techafricanews-kica-revie.summary: Kenya's ICT department told a National Assembly committee that the Kenya Information and Communications Act is under review and accession to the Budapest Convention on Cybercrime is advancing. Billing transparency for internet service was also discussed.

2026-10-09-lequotidien-taazour-sanad-dig.summary: Mauritania's national solidarity agency launched Sanad, a single digital platform for social assistance. It opens with transport costs for 11,656 pupils and students from households in the social registry, who are verified by facial recognition.

2026-10-09-linfodrome-artci-meta-monetis.summary: The head of Côte d'Ivoire's telecoms regulator received a Meta delegation to discuss paying Ivorian content creators on its platforms and the regulation of digital services. No decision or date was announced.

2026-10-09-malawi24-undp-printers-decent.summary: UNDP handed Malawi 152 printers to bring birth, marriage and death registration closer to people: 100 for registration offices at Traditional Authority level and 52 for health facilities. The minister said 180 health facilities are already digitalised.

2026-10-09-mar-nexus-core-systems-infras.summary: The developer of Morocco's planned AI compute platform states 500 MW of total planned capacity, a 40 MW initial deployment and a 12-hectare first site, on renewable power. The page gives no dates.

2026-10-09-midi-madagasikara-gouvernemen.summary: Madagascar scores 9 of 16 points against the 12 it needs to rejoin the Open Government Partnership, which it first joined in 2016. A colloquium is drafting commitments for a national action plan for 2026 to 2030.

2026-10-09-moz-mznews-atdi-x-road-traini.summary: Mozambique's digital transformation agency trained 25 technicians from nine public bodies on the X-Road data-exchange layer, among them civil identification, migration and tax. Estonian experts led the four days, under a World Bank project.

2026-10-09-mozambique-95-broadband-2030.summary: Mozambique's regulator validated its Internet for All strategy, which targets 95% broadband coverage by 2030, 12 million mobile internet subscribers and at least 60% of schools connected. It cited a programme to subsidise about 280,000 internet-enabled devices.

2026-10-09-nam-marketwatch-fibre-copper-.summary: Telecom Namibia signed a partnership with Demshi Investment Holdings to replace copper with fibre in areas hit repeatedly by theft and vandalism. Demshi builds and maintains the open-access network and Telecom Namibia sells service over it.

2026-10-09-nga-securing-digital-trust-nd.summary: Nigeria's data protection commissioner visited the salaries and wages commission to press compliance with the 2023 Act and pay structures that keep data protection staff in the public service. He put the commission's revenue at more than ₦12 billion in 2026, against ₦7 billion in 2025.

2026-10-09-rwanda-ida-19m-digitalization.summary: Rwanda's parliament ratified EUR 17 million of World Bank financing for digital identity, public data management and cybersecurity, restoring part of US$20 million cut from the project in 2024. Delays to the government data hub have pushed the project's deadline to June 2028.

2026-10-09-sen-techreviewafrica-artp-new.summary: Senegal's new telecoms regulator chief said at his handover that he will move the authority toward data-led regulation, with real-time measurement of service quality. He named 5G, cloud, satellite broadband and digital finance as what it must anticipate.

2026-10-09-southwood-africas-digital-lan.summary: An analyst updates his 2019 study of African online content: digital advertising's share of spend rose from 5 to 10% in 2019 to 45% in 2024. He finds video creators can be paid in only a handful of sub-Saharan countries, and payout services work in hard currency only.

2026-10-09-swz-independentnews-ecot-miss.summary: An analysis of professional profiles presented at a skills workshop found 265 ICT professionals in Eswatini trained at Limkokwing and 152 at the University of Eswatini, and none visible from the Eswatini College of Technology. The presenter read it as a visibility problem for the college.

2026-10-09-swz-independentnews-eptc-post.summary: Eswatini's postal corporation said 34 of its branches now take payments for public services, in partnership with the revenue service. It is turning to government services to keep the network open as mail falls.

2026-10-09-tcd-lendjampost-e-visa-demand.summary: Applications on Chad's electronic visa platform have risen from under 10 a day to more than 100, the police official in charge said. The platform, launched in December 2024, has been the required route since 11 May 2026, though some embassies still issue visas.

2026-10-09-tcd-lendjampost-stpe-poste-ba.summary: Chad's telecoms minister set out a transformation of the state postal operator: a postal bank in the medium term, an integrated payment platform and post offices as one-stop counters. Its virtual-operator and internet-provider licences are to be put to use; no budget or date was given.

2026-10-09-thisdaysl-sierra-leone-cybera.summary: Sierra Leone's communications ministry confirmed that 44 website addresses, one a government institution's, were hit on 25 September through the system that administers the national internet domain. Service was restored the same day; how the attackers got in has not been made public.

2026-10-09-za-ict-industry-redesign-ngca.summary: The president of Digital Council Africa told a Johannesburg conference that South Africa's ICT industry needs a full redesign of its regulation and physical infrastructure for AI. He said the country has very few specialists investigating and prosecuting cybercrime.

2026-10-09-zaf-itweb-woan-open-access-ma.summary: An industry opinion piece argues that South Africa's withdrawal of the wireless open access network direction leaves its principles in place: leasing of networks, wholesale capacity for other licensees and rural access. The author's case is for better use of infrastructure already built.

2026-10-09-zaf-techafricanews-kredete-ca.summary: Kredete acquired an entity holding a South African crypto asset service provider licence, to offer stablecoin remittances and payments. The regulator had approved about 310 of 533 licence applications by early 2026.

2026-10-10-bdi-burunditimes-eapss-paieme.summary: The East African Legislative Assembly's accounts committee reported that Burundi left parts of the regional payment-systems integration project unfinished when its grant closed in June. It recommends an audit and a costed completion plan; the central bank says it still intends to join the East African Payment System by December.

2026-10-10-cod-7sur7-copil-ptn-ptba-2026.summary: The steering committee of the DRC's digital transformation project met for the first time on 8 October and approved the 2026 work plan and budget. Members went through delays component by component and set priorities to 2027.

2026-10-10-cod-gachette-continuite-donne.summary: An economist's opinion piece starts from Google One refusing subscription renewals in the DRC and argues for data portability, trust standards for cloud services and enforcement of the 2023 digital code.

2026-10-10-gha-b2bgh-shaibu-fintech-open.summary: The head of Ghana's largest mobile-money fintech names AI, open finance, embedded finance, digital assets and instant payments as the themes that will shape the sector over the next two years.

2026-10-10-gha-ghanaguardian-agyeman-raw.summary: Visiting the Ghana Atomic Energy Commission on 9 October, the science and technology minister said the AI data centre it proposes must run under human oversight to protect sensitive nuclear information. She asked for governance arrangements to be written into the plan.

2026-10-10-gin-mediaguinee-moussotech-10.summary: An NGO in Guinea launched MoussoTech on 9 October, an app in four national languages giving women information on health, rights and violence. A mobile operator is giving the first 100 participants a smartphone and a year of data.

2026-10-10-lby-lana-al-baour-fcc-meeting.summary: The head of Libya's communications authority met officials at the US Federal Communications Commission in Washington, on licensing, spectrum, satellite licensing and the protection of subsea cables.

2026-10-10-mar-customs-ai-audits.summary: Moroccan customs are reported to have used AI and risk-analysis tools to audit imports worth about MAD 650 million and recover close to MAD 50 million for undervaluation. The account rests on unnamed sources, with no official statement.

2026-10-10-mdg-torohy-tax-corruption-pla.summary: Madagascar's tax directorate launched Torohy on 9 October, a platform for the public to report corruption in the tax administration. The head of state asked for the same at customs and the treasury.

2026-10-10-moz-techreviewafrica-sofala-c.summary: Mozambique's ICT institute held a consultation in Beira on 6 October to collect provincial input on the proposed national cybersecurity strategy for 2026 to 2030.

2026-10-10-mwi-undp-printers-nrb.summary: UNDP's own account of the 152 printers handed to Malawi's registration bureau: 100 for registration at Traditional Authority offices and 52 for health facilities. It puts the Nzika registration application in pilot at 87 locations in five districts, with 250 planned by 2028.

2026-10-10-nam-bank-windhoek-face-id.summary: Bank Windhoek says it has recorded no fraud among customers using facial recognition. A quarter of its individual customers are now enrolled, up from 15% a year earlier.

2026-10-10-nga-theafricanchronicle-stand.summary: Standard Bank Group has agreed to invest in the payments company OPay, which has filed for a New York listing. The amount is not disclosed, and closing depends on the listing and on regulatory approval.

2026-10-10-nga-theliberalist-nigeria-nee.summary: An opinion piece argues that Nigeria's data protection act and its implementing directive already regulate automated decisions, and points to the data protection commission's fines as evidence that a separate AI law is not needed.
