2026-10-10-nga-timeexpressnigeria-gov-ra.summary: Katsina State and Nigeria's identity commission agreed a working group to link the state's identity management system to the national one, with a framework and memorandum due within eight weeks.

2026-10-10-nga-undp-cisco-networking-aca.summary: UNDP and Cisco signed a memorandum in Abuja on 9 October giving fellows of the Nigeria Jubilee Fellows Programme free access to the Cisco Networking Academy, with a target of up to 50,000 young people.

2026-10-10-sdn-alroya-bankak-ussd-1913-l.summary: Bank of Khartoum has opened a USSD transfer service on MTN lines, so customers can move money without a smartphone or a data connection. It comes as complaints about outages of the bank's app continue; the bank says more services will follow on the same channel.

2026-10-10-sdn-sudanhorizon-will-higher-.summary: A former banker argues that the Central Bank of Sudan's capital circular of February 2026 sets the same floor for digital banks as for commercial banks, and that the mergers it will force need scrutiny.

2026-10-10-sen-ledakarois-intrants-agric.summary: Senegal's agriculture ministry launched an app on 9 October for distributing subsidised seed and fertiliser nationwide. Producers get a text message before collecting, and the minister says the state now holds a digital register of who is entitled to what.

2026-10-10-sen-leral-pikine-guediawaye-a.summary: Senegal's justice ministry judged the first results of the pilot digitising judicial archives at the Pikine-Guédiawaye court satisfactory. Recruiting qualified staff and keeping the court platform fed are the open problems; other courts may follow.

2026-10-10-tgo-ancy-formation-cybersecur.summary: Togo's cybersecurity agency has been running the second phase of its national training programme since 7 September, for 350 public-administration staff. Training is free; trainees pay their own exam fees.

2026-10-10-tgo-atop-etat-civil-relecture.summary: A territorial administration ministry delegation consulted local officials in Avé 1 commune on 8 October as part of the review of Togo's 2009 civil status law. Participants raised the difficulty of deciding where a birth should be declared.

2026-10-10-tun-lapresse-plateforme-numer.summary: Tunisia's religious affairs ministry has launched a platform to manage mosque staff: it follows personnel files, shows vacant posts and links central and regional services.

2026-10-10-tza-eanso-cybercrime-fraud-le.summary: A second legal study judges Tanzania's Cybercrimes Act sound on paper and weakly enforced against mobile-money fraud. It calls for judicial warrants before communications are intercepted.

2026-10-10-tza-eanso-lga-cybersecurity-u.summary: A legal study finds that the security duties in Tanzania's e-Government Act are not tied to accountability in local government authorities, and that audits keep finding unauthorised access to council systems.

2026-10-10-tza-moh-data-use-partnership-.summary: Tanzania's health ministry describes its Data Use Partnership, a programme run with an international partner that has set up a digital health centre, a health enterprise architecture and an administrative-area registry covering more than 12,000 villages.

2026-10-10-uga-eprc-ai-opportunities-fea.summary: A Ugandan think-tank blog weighs the risk that AI chatbots weaken learning against the risk of unequal access, and asks for an education chapter in the national AI strategy.

2026-10-10-xwa-seneplus-ia-afrique-franc.summary: A long read on the AI guidelines six francophone West African countries published together: seven principles and five ways of putting them into effect, with formal national adoption still to come. It notes that the size of the proposed AI fund is stated inconsistently.

2026-10-10-zaf-sundaytimes-2026-10-10-pu.summary: South Africa's universal service agency is consulting on whether to update the 2010 determination that defines universal access and universal service. Its discussion document sets out three options and leans towards a targeted revision; it creates no new funding or licence obligations.

2026-10-10-zwe-heraldonline-government-m.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT minister said the government is working to end fragmented digital systems across public bodies, and called for common standards so that citizens are not asked for the same information twice.

2026-10-11-ago-deliberacao-sobre-process.summary: Angola's data protection agency publishes its register of fines: 15 sanctions between 2022 and 2026, from US$75,000 to US$525,000, with banks, telecoms operators, the national airline and the Luanda water utility among those penalised. The largest 2026 fine was for storing personal data in a cloud abroad without authorisation.

2026-10-11-alchourouk-khadamat-app-app-s.summary: Tunisia's communication technologies ministry released its Khadamat public-services app on a second mobile platform, after an Android release at the end of August. It is reached through the e-Houwiya digital identity and covers civil-status records, driving licence and vehicle data, traffic fines, inspection bookings, health-insurance and social-security services and e-payments.

2026-10-11-bj-lanation-ia-images-retouch.summary: A learner prosecuted for circulating altered photographs of his teacher appeared before Benin's economic crimes and terrorism court on 8 October. The newspaper sets out the digital code's penalty for publishing a doctored image of a person without consent: five years in prison and a fine of FCFA 25 million.

2026-10-11-btw-afrinic-policy-petition-b.summary: An analysis of the second draft of AFRINIC's policy-process guidelines finds that its petition route, which lets the working group seek ratification of a policy, opens only when no operative Board exists. It needs 15 supporters from three subregions and still depends on a change to the Bylaws.

2026-10-11-caf-acdd-agence-presentation.summary: The Central African Republic's digital development agency sets out its own footing: a public industrial and commercial establishment created by a law of June 2023, with a mandate to implement the national digital strategy. The page gives no budget, staffing or activity figures.

2026-10-11-citizen-za-novazi-pay-or-cons.summary: A Stellenbosch law lecturer argues that South Africa's data-protection, consumer and competition laws are too fragmented to police platforms that make users choose between paying a subscription and surrendering personal data. The study, in a law review, calls for reform.

2026-10-11-cod-7sur7-gouvernement-annonc.summary: DR Congo's posts and telecommunications minister presented the commercial launch of 5G to the Council of Ministers on 9 October, as a new source of state revenue and a way to improve service quality. Deployment is to begin in urban areas; no operator, spectrum assignment or launch date was given.

2026-10-11-gha-myjoyonline-bog-develops-.summary: The Bank of Ghana is drafting a directive on the use of artificial intelligence by financial institutions, its governor told the banks' annual meeting. The Bank will also run thematic reviews of how banks have implemented its revised cyber and information security directive.

2026-10-11-guardian-nga-postcode-next-di.summary: A commentary on Nigeria's new eleven-character postcode, switched on by the postal service on 1 October, reports early users finding it accurate for some buildings and missing for others. It argues the code could serve commerce, banking and lending as a proof of address if coverage is completed.

2026-10-11-mdg-2424-e-pasipaoro-online-p.summary: Madagascar's digital ministry said its online passport application portal is being tested. Applicants will be able to file, pay and track a first application, renewal or replacement online, while biometric capture and signature remain in person; no launch date was given.

2026-10-11-nga-thisday-galaxy-backbone-d.summary: Nigeria's state network operator said more than 30 federal ministries, departments and agencies have moved onto one platform for paperless approval of documents and memos, and promised wider adoption. It gave no list of agencies and no target; customers at the same event pressed for faster complaint handling.

2026-10-11-osiris-sen-marches-publics-ia.summary: An opinion article argues that Senegal should allow generative artificial intelligence in public procurement but require its use to be declared. The author says no Senegalese text now governs the use of artificial intelligence in public purchasing, and that the 2008 data protection law predates the technology.

2026-10-11-uga-how-scammers-are-stealing.summary: Uganda's financial services providers reported 6,533 fraud cases to regulators between January and August 2026, with about Ush23.5 billion lost of Ush67 billion targeted, on an industry consortium's figures. About 95% of reported cases involve mobile transactions, and few court cases end in conviction.

2026-10-11-world-bank-nga-2026-private-c.summary: The World Bank Group says it is helping mobilise up to US$5.79 billion of private financing in Nigeria in its 2026 financial year, through policy reform, investment platforms, guarantees and commercial lending. The national open-access fibre project is among the investments it names.

2026-10-11-zaf-applesandoranges-agsa-sit.summary: South Africa's Auditor-General found that 2,076 of about 7,800 sites on the state IT agency's network ran below 10Mbps and that 294 government facilities were still on copper, in its audit of the communications department for 2025/26. The state broadband programme also fell short of its target of 14,742 sites for the year.

2026-10-11-zaf-dailymaverick-local-ai-po.summary: A commentary argues that South Africa's revised artificial intelligence policy must settle who controls data, computing capacity and models, and proposes pooling them regionally. It is opinion, written as AI systems become more autonomous.

2026-10-11-zaf-enca-creecy-trn-dormant-b.summary: South Africa's transport minister said 300,000 dormant traffic register numbers have been blocked, about half of those found to be fraudulent. Holders of the rest have been asked to verify their details with Home Affairs, and about 8,000 have come forward.

2026-10-11-zaf-sanews-asylum-court-guida.summary: South Africa's government will ask the courts for a supervisory order on implementing the Constitutional Court's July 2026 asylum judgment. Home Affairs is to introduce an online intention-registration and appointment system by 10 November 2026, with assisted registration at Refugee Reception Offices.

2026-10-11-zaf-sanews-home-affairs-biome.summary: South Africa's home affairs minister said a biometric online platform for asylum applications is to be operating by 10 November 2026, checking applicants' biometrics against earlier rejected claims and verifying their travel documents. He put the backlog of asylum appeals at about 120,000, a figure he said would be confirmed.

2026-10-11-zaf-sanews-transport-amend-re.summary: South Africa's transport department plans to amend the road traffic regulations so that traffic register number certificates, learner's licences and driving licences no longer count as identification. A traffic register number would be valid only as long as the passport and permit it was issued on, and the draft is to be gazetted for 30 days of comment.

2026-10-11-zwe-why-zim-needs-real-time-t.summary: An opinion article argues that Zimbabwe's telecommunications regulator should move from periodic audits of service quality, based on operators' submitted data and scheduled drive tests, to continuous automated monitoring. It says the regulator's quarterly reports show high compliance while users experience dropped calls and outages.

2026-10-12-agenceecofin-centrafrique-rdc.summary: The digital-economy ministers of the Central African Republic and DR Congo agreed in Moscow on 8 October on the need to carry out a fibre interconnection between the two countries, which would give the Central African Republic a third international route, toward the submarine cable landing at Moanda. No timetable or financing was announced.

2026-10-12-bwa-sundaystandard-hikvision-.summary: A newspaper investigation reports that two Chinese surveillance-camera makers have a substantial footprint in Botswana, from the police surveillance network to a nationwide banking CCTV system and public facilities. Only the opening of the article is held; the detail is behind a paywall.

2026-10-12-civ-senat-vote-electronique.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's Senate opened its second ordinary session of 2026 with attendance recorded in real time instead of a roll call, amendments filed online and proceedings archived automatically. Electronic voting was trialled the same day, with training for senators on 13 to 16 October.

2026-10-12-dza-agence-ecofin-fibre-optiq.summary: Algeria's fibre-to-the-home subscriptions passed 4 million in early October, from 53,000 in June 2020, on the posts minister's figures. The monthly price of an offer of 100 Mbit/s or more has fallen 76%, and the target is more than 4.4 million by the end of the year.

2026-10-12-eyeradio-ssd-moscow-digital-f.summary: The head of South Sudan's Media Authority, leading the country's delegation at a digital forum in Moscow, said the government needs to put in place measures bringing digital technology into public administration and to understand the risks and benefits of artificial intelligence. No instrument or timetable was announced.

2026-10-12-financialexpress-airtel-money.summary: Airtel Money began conditional trading on the London Stock Exchange on 9 October after an oversubscribed offer in which existing shareholders sold 270 million shares, raising about US$703 million. The shares ended just below the offer price on the first day, and unconditional dealings were due on 14 October.

2026-10-12-gab-biometricupdate-gabon-dig.summary: An account of Gabon's bill ratifying its digital payments ordinance ties it to the regional central bank's interoperability rules. It puts the national merchant QR scheme at more than 3,273 merchants and 1,382 GIMAC QR codes as of July.

2026-10-12-gha-myjoyonline-nyaho-medical.summary: Ghana's Data Protection Commission directed an Accra hospital to report to the police criminal investigations department over an expired data protection registration certificate, after an enforcement operation on 12 October. How long the registration had lapsed was not stated.

2026-10-12-gha-myjoyonline-sam-george-kn.summary: Ghana's communications minister said national AI language models will be built locally, tasking a Kumasi university to lead a Twi model and other universities to lead other Ghanaian languages. Voice interfaces for farmers and telemedicine are planned; no budget or timetable was given.

2026-10-12-gha-who-afro-health-records-g.summary: The Ghana Health Service, supported by WHO, convened a national workshop to revise its Medical Records Strategy and Operational Guidelines, written nearly a decade ago. The revision is to cover electronic medical records, data governance, interoperability, cybersecurity and the use of artificial intelligence in healthcare.

2026-10-12-itweb-africa-botswana-invests.summary: Botswana's universal service fund, working with one mobile operator, has deployed 12 mobile broadband and voice sites along the 1,900km Trans-Kalahari Highway at a cost of P34.5 million, the communications minister said. Infrastructure sharing with the other two operators is to extend coverage by the end of the next financial year.

2026-10-12-itweb-africa-zambia-unlocks-d.summary: Zambia's technology and youth ministries are developing a framework for local content creators to earn from digital platforms, and are talking to Meta, TikTok and Google about the legal and technical arrangements. The President named it a priority when opening the 14th National Assembly, and a national database of creators is being compiled.

2026-10-12-ken-absa-employee-data-leak-c.summary: A former senior manager at a Kenyan bank testified, in a Sh1.5 billion data breach suit against it, that a credit manager disclosed a borrower's loan distress to a third party. He said the bank's legal department recommended no action because it saw no material risk of abuse.

2026-10-12-ken-ca-central-database-recyc.summary: Kenya's communications regulator said it will set up a central database of recycled phone numbers, which operators must update every three months. Banks, fintechs and bulk message senders would check it before sending account messages to a number.

2026-10-12-lbr-lta-public-consultation-d.summary: Liberia's telecommunications authority consulted internet service providers, mobile operators and licensees on draft regulations for deploying, sharing, managing and decommissioning telecoms infrastructure. The draft text is not held.

2026-10-12-lso-govls-smart-africa-allian.summary: Lesotho's communications minister took part in the 21st Smart Africa Alliance meeting, and government said efforts are under way to establish the alliance's digital academy in the country. Lesotho joined the alliance in 2025.

2026-10-12-lso-govls-world-bank-digital-.summary: A World Bank urban and land team told Lesotho's communications ministry it is interested in supporting a nationwide digital address system, in talks that also covered geospatial data for planning and digital public works for young people. No commitment or amount was stated.

2026-10-12-mar-maroc-ma-morocco-cybersec.summary: Morocco's information systems security directorate is hosting a three-day cybersecurity event in Rabat from 12 to 14 October, with an ITU exercise drawing representatives of about thirty countries. The African Network of Cybersecurity Authorities meets on its sidelines.

2026-10-12-moz-clubofmozambique-cybersec.summary: Mozambique's communications minister said the national cybersecurity strategy for 2026 to 2030 is being updated and will be the main instrument for implementing the Cybersecurity Act. He put cyber incidents recorded in 2025 at about 39,600 and urged operators of critical infrastructure to set up their incident response teams.

2026-10-12-moz-tan-incm-postal-operators.summary: Mozambique's communications regulator held its first postal operators forum on 9 October and called for the sector to be formalised and modernised as e-commerce grows. The country has 38 licensed postal operators, and the regulator named unlicensed delivery through digital platforms as a problem for oversight and consumer protection.

2026-10-12-mus-lexpress-water-tank-grant.summary: Mauritius's ICT ministry says it is building an online application platform with the Central Water Authority for a household water tank and pump grant announced on 9 October. Access terms are to follow.

2026-10-12-mwi-mra-ataf-tax-administrati.summary: The Malawi Revenue Authority said it is building a second integrated tax administration system in-house and is still seeking funding for it. It credited its electronic invoicing system, enforced from 1 May, with part of a rise in average monthly VAT collections from MK66.73 billion to MK81.24 billion.

2026-10-12-scenenow-egy-ration-card-digi.summary: Egypt has put key ration card services on the Digital Egypt platform: heads of household can update card data, replace or activate cards, transfer a file between governorates and add family members. The data-update service is being introduced in Port Said for an initial three months before other governorates.

2026-10-12-sudantimes-sdn-tasis-governan.summary: The prime minister of Sudan's TASIS-backed administration announced plans for a national smart identity card for banking, judicial and administrative transactions in the territory it runs, alongside new vehicle registration, licensing and customs procedures. He put that territory at about 90 localities and 24 million people, figures that are not independently verified.

2026-10-12-tan-zambia-ai-career-guidance.summary: Zambia's technology ministry is piloting Njila.ai, an artificial-intelligence career-guidance platform, in the technical and vocational training system under a World Bank-backed skills project. The pilot is expected to reach more than 17,000 young people, and feedback is to decide any wider rollout.

2026-10-12-tcd-chad-moves-towards-adopti.summary: Chad held a pre-validation workshop on its draft national artificial-intelligence strategy, drafted with the UN Economic Commission for Africa. The draft covers 2027 to 2035 and names agriculture, public administration, security and defence, education and health as priority sectors.

2026-10-12-tza-6-308-nida-cards-remain-u.summary: Tanzania's home affairs minister said 6,308 national identity cards printed for Zanzibar residents had not been collected. He said government is considering fines for late collection and may require the physical card for services that now accept the identity number alone.

2026-10-12-uga-nilepost-ucc-reviews-crac.summary: Uganda's communications regulator said it is reviewing its enforcement against unauthorised Wi-Fi and hotspot resellers after complaints from operators. A public notice was promised within the week.

2026-10-12-undp-tza-zanzibar-care-georef.summary: UNDP says a tool it piloted in Unguja to map disability care and support services has been integrated into Zanzibar's Jumuishi management information system. The mapping found 32 providers, 30 of them in one region.

2026-10-12-wearetech-africa-rdc-5g-en-pr.summary: DR Congo's government is preparing a commercial 5G launch, which the telecommunications minister said in late September it was working to make available before the end of 2026. The article sets that against internet use of about 30.5% of the population at the end of 2025 and mobile internet coverage of 45%.

2026-10-12-xwa-togofirst-bceao-doubles-m.summary: The West African central bank's new instruction doubles the cap on electronic money one client may hold at one issuer to FCFA 4 million, from a limit set in 2015. Issuers must now keep at least 65% of their float in demand deposits, down from 75%.

2026-10-12-yonhap-koica-digital-oda-chin.summary: A South Korean MP said Korea's aid agency had supplied Chinese-made equipment to e-government projects it funded abroad, among them Senegal's National Assembly system, Egypt's public e-procurement system, Cameroon's e-procurement system and Rwanda's e-receipt and tax portal. The agency told him it has no criteria for judging whether equipment comes from a high-risk supply chain.

2026-10-12-zaf-businessday-regulate-plat.summary: Two authors summarise their report for a free-expression campaign, arguing that South Africa should regulate the platforms cybercriminals use by borrowing from the European Digital Services Act: notice-and-action, trusted flaggers, systemic-risk duties and transparency reports. It is opinion; the report itself is not held.

2026-10-12-zaf-dailymaverick-foxglove-ca.summary: One of the organisations appealing against land-use rights for a planned hyperscale data centre in Cape Town argues that the mayor should uphold the appeal because the application did not state the site's water use, emissions or jobs. It writes that the appeal went before the city's advisory panel on 12 October and that the mayor then has 90 days to decide.

2026-10-12-zwe-government-gives-postal-s.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT minister gave her ministry, the regulator and the postal operator 90 days to produce a costed plan for the postal and courier sector to 2030, with quarterly reporting. She also directed operators to comply with the Cyber and Data Protection Act and required pilots of artificial intelligence and drones to carry a named lead, a timetable and measurable benefits.

2026-10-13-acet-gender-inclusive-ai-gove.summary: A think-tank paper sets out policy options for African governments to build gender inclusion into artificial intelligence governance, arguing that the first national strategies arrive while governments still hold bargaining power over how the technology enters their economies.

2026-10-13-bwa-china-botswana-joint-stat.summary: China and Botswana raised relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership in a joint statement issued during President Duma Boko's state visit. It affirms digital sovereignty and each state's right to choose its own path on artificial intelligence; Botswana joins China's digital economy trade-cooperation initiative and will consider joining the World AI Cooperation Organization.

2026-10-13-cassava-pemhiwa-keep-africa-d.summary: The chief executive of Cassava Technologies said Africa risks repeating its history of exporting raw commodities unless it builds its own computing capacity for artificial intelligence and keeps its data on the continent.

2026-10-13-civ-cybersecurite-la-cote-div.summary: Côte d'Ivoire's information-systems security agency will run a first national cyber-crisis simulation in Abidjan on 28 and 29 October 2026.

2026-10-13-cod-agenceecofin-microsites-a.summary: DR Congo's posts and telecommunications ministry is promoting solar-powered microsites to extend mobile coverage to rural and peri-urban areas, presented to the universal service fund and four operators. Fifty pilot sites are planned, each said to cost a quarter of a conventional mast.

2026-10-13-cod-congorassure-fizi-baraka-.summary: Civil society in Fizi territory and Baraka, South Kivu, published a memorandum to the President demanding the reopening of telecommunications networks it says have been cut since 3 July 2026. It alleges that soldiers seized satellite kits and phones and that local authorities resold satellite Wi-Fi, and announces a sit-in from 19 October.

2026-10-13-egy-shura-pdpl-compliance-dea.summary: A law firm's checklist notes that the one-year transition under the executive regulations of Egypt's Personal Data Protection Law ends on 31 October 2026, and that the Personal Data Protection Centre opened its portal for licence and permit applications in early October.

2026-10-13-gab-fonction-publique-sigrh-p.summary: Gabon's civil-service ministry reviewed technical preparations for an integrated human resources management system and named the procurement tender as the next step. The platform, under a World Bank-supported project, is to hold one register of state employees linked to payroll, budget and national identification.

2026-10-13-gab-infosgabon-frontiere-ere-.summary: Gabon's transport minister visited a United States operator's installations at Libreville airport to speed the commissioning of a passenger-data screening system, insisting that trained national staff run it. No go-live date or cost was given.

2026-10-13-gha-gna-dpc-2575-data-control.summary: Ghana's Data Protection Commission said it had registered 2,575 data controllers in 2026, more than in any previous year, and was adding spot checks, inspections and complaint investigations.

2026-10-13-gha-gna-sam-george-knust-2000.summary: Ghana's communications minister presented 2,000 more laptops to a university for the One Million Coders Programme, where 195 of 1,447 enrolled students had completed the course. He said the ministry was working to open regional offices of the Cyber Security Authority.

2026-10-13-gha-techafricanews-one-millio.summary: Ghana's communications ministry is addressing training and infrastructure problems in the One Million Coders Programme after beneficiaries raised them in a monitoring exercise.

2026-10-13-gmb-gambiana-gid-denies-losin.summary: The Gambia Immigration Department denied losing access to national identity card data, saying the servers used under the former contract remain in the country. It attributed the reports to a misunderstanding of an officer's court testimony.

2026-10-13-ken-dawan-access-to-informati.summary: An explainer on Kenya's newly gazetted Access to Information Policy asks whether it will change practice: citizens already hold a right to request records, it notes, but often do not get them.

2026-10-13-ken-kenyans-icta-kdeap-digita.summary: Kenya's ICT Authority invited consulting firms to express interest in integrating digital literacy into the competency-based school curriculum through gender-inclusive strategies, under a World Bank-funded digital economy project. Firms must show experience in developing artificial intelligence curricula.

2026-10-13-ken-kenyans-microsoft-nairobi.summary: Microsoft plans to close the engineering department of its Africa Development Centre in Nairobi after more than seven years, a Kenyan outlet reports. Between 400 and 500 employees could be affected.

2026-10-13-ken-peopledaily-kabogo-gazett.summary: Kenya's ICT Cabinet Secretary gazetted the Access to Information Policy, 2026 on 9 October. It requires public offices to disclose key records proactively, answer requests within set timelines and give written reasons for refusals.

2026-10-13-ken-techafricanews-jitume-hub.summary: Kenya commissioned a Jitume ICT hub at a technical training campus in Uasin Gishu, taking the national network to 391 equipped sites and 23,387 devices. Of 253 technical and vocational institutions, 186 have the equipment and 67 still wait.

2026-10-13-ken-techafricanews-ksg-eliti-.summary: The Kenya School of Government launched an eLearning and Information Technology Institute as 1,239 public officers graduated from a UNESCO-Oxford programme on artificial intelligence and digital transformation in government.

2026-10-13-ken-techafricanews-ksh13bn-fi.summary: Kenya will put KSh 13 billion into extending its national fibre backbone and cross-border links by at least 27,000 km, the ICT principal secretary told a pre-bid session. Gaps are to be allocated by reverse auction to draw matching private capital.

2026-10-13-ken-techcabal-microsoft-shut-.summary: Microsoft is winding down its Africa Development Centre in Nairobi, staff were told on 12 October, putting nearly 400 jobs at risk with fewer than 10 expected to remain. The company confirmed only proposed changes to its engineering operations; Kenya's ICT Cabinet Secretary, briefed the same day, agreed a joint action plan with it.

2026-10-13-moz-mznews-atdi-digital-id-mi.summary: Mozambique's digital agency is leading a 14-member technical mission to Ethiopia to prepare a national digital identity, with staff from the justice ministry, civil identification, the migration service and the road-transport institute.

2026-10-13-mtn-sa-5g-u6ghz-trial.summary: MTN South Africa said it had completed a 5G-Advanced trial in the upper 6GHz band at its headquarters, under a temporary licence, reaching peak downloads of 10.35 gigabits a second. The regulator's 2026 frequency plan allocates the band to mobile, but it is not yet licensed commercially.

2026-10-13-nam-economist-ai-policy-civil.summary: Namibia's Cabinet has directed the Office of the Prime Minister and the ICT ministry to develop an internal policy on civil servants' use of artificial intelligence, the ICT minister announced at the National ICT Summit. No timeline or draft was given.

2026-10-13-nga-digitisation-raises-c-riv.summary: The head of a technology firm said digitising government services had raised Cross River State's internally generated revenue by N46 billion in under a year. The figure is the firm's own.

2026-10-13-nga-hamzat-tasks-govt-busines.summary: Lagos State's deputy governor said more than 6.4 million residents have enrolled in the state's resident identity system. He put state fibre at about 3,000 km, with a further US$22 million invested towards a 6,000 km network.

2026-10-13-nigeria-internet-data-consump.summary: Nigerians used 11.94 million terabytes of internet data in January to August 2026, about 90% of the whole of 2025, on the regulator's statistics. August alone took 1.76 million terabytes, with about 800,000 new internet subscriptions.

2026-10-13-rwa-yonhap-koica-rwanda-codin.summary: A South Korean news agency reports from the Rwanda Coding Academy, a secondary school modelled on Korean vocational schools and supported by Korea's aid agency with about 10.9 billion won.

2026-10-13-sdn-sudanhorizon-banks-foreig.summary: A Sudanese report examines foreign shareholdings in the country's 38 banks, a question raised when the government cut relations with the United Arab Emirates in May 2025 while Emirati investors held more than 40% of the bank behind the most used banking app. It weighs the need for outside capital against influence over the post-war banking sector.

2026-10-13-sdn-sudanhorizon-bede-bban-se.summary: Bede Sudan, a mobile operator's fintech arm, launched a bank account number service that links its digital wallet to the banking system, with a commercial bank and central bank approval. Wallet users can send and receive funds across all Sudanese banks.

2026-10-13-sen-aps-ansd-acces-distance-d.summary: Senegal's statistics agency is working towards remote access for authorised researchers to the anonymised detailed data now consulted on site in its data-access centres. Its director-general named personal-data protection, access security and conditions of use as the questions to settle.

2026-10-13-sen-rts-assemblee-pastef-enqu.summary: Majority deputies in Senegal's National Assembly filed a proposal for a commission of inquiry into the health cooperation agreement with the United States, in particular what it means for Senegalese personal data. The Assembly's Bureau will rule on whether it is admissible.

2026-10-13-sen-seneweb-digisen-couvertur.summary: A four-year research project in Saint-Louis and Ziguinchor, Senegal, collected more than 100,000 connectivity measurements and concluded that network coverage is not the same as connectivity: cost, place, time of day and gender shape the service people actually get.

2026-10-13-sle-emerging-technologies-can.summary: In an interview, a senior engineer at Sierra Leone's telecommunications regulator says gaps in connectivity, technical skills and cross-border integration stand between African countries and artificial intelligence and cloud services, and argues for sustained investment in infrastructure, skills and regulation.

2026-10-13-sle-sierra-leone-counts-down-.summary: Sierra Leone opened the 50-day countdown to its 2026 Population and Housing Census, its first fully digital enumeration. Census Night is 1 December and nationwide enumeration starts the next day.

2026-10-13-tcd-tchadinfos-central-africa.summary: Chad's digital ministry and its partners opened the Central Africa Internet Governance Forum in N'Djamena on 13 October 2026.

2026-10-13-tza-thecitizen-222-health-fac.summary: Tanzania's health ministry said 222 public health facilities are connected to an integrated electronic medical records system introduced in October 2025. It named unreliable connectivity, power, equipment shortages and incomplete interoperability as obstacles to covering the country.

2026-10-13-uga-monitor-digital-plates-pr.summary: A former works minister told a Ugandan parliamentary committee that the digital number plate rollout went ahead without a preliminary feasibility study, and a former internal affairs minister said early warnings were ignored. The contractor defended plate fees paid to it rather than into the Consolidated Fund.

2026-10-13-zaf-itweb-icasa-regulatory-re.summary: South Africa's communications regulator is widening its approach to take in satellite services, data centres, cloud computing and artificial intelligence, its chairperson said. It is weighing conventional licensing against lighter oversight and regulatory sandboxes.

2026-10-13-zwe-263chat-national-msme-dat.summary: Zimbabwe's small-enterprise development corporation said a national database of micro, small and medium enterprises has reached minimum-viable-product stage, with an online registration portal in development. Talks are under way to link it to the revenue authority and the procurement regulator.

2026-10-13-zwe-zimbabwesituation-electro.summary: Zimbabwe's police said logistics for an Electronic Traffic Management System were being finalised. The system is linked to the vehicle and civil registries to identify offenders and issue penalties electronically.

2026-10-14-afdb-undp-advance-ai-10-billi.summary: The African Development Bank and UNDP said the AI 10 Billion Initiative has moved to delivery after a UNDP mission to the Bank in Abidjan. It is to start in five countries and reach 20 by the end of 2027, arranging US$1 billion a year for ten years; no country, contributor or committed sum is named.

2026-10-14-ago-cajnews-q-kon-sistec-twoo.summary: Q-KON and SISTEC opened a point of presence in Luanda for the Twoobii OneWeb low-Earth-orbit satellite service, hosted at SISTEC's premises. It gives in-country data breakout with local IP addresses alongside Eutelsat OneWeb's Angolan gateway, and is sold to banks, government, defence and enterprises.

2026-10-14-airtel-money-virtual-card-ken.summary: Airtel Money plans to launch a Mastercard prepaid virtual card linked to its wallets in Kenya, competing with Safaricom's M-PESA GlobalPay. Communications Authority figures put M-PESA's mobile money share at 88.8% and Airtel Money's at 11.1% in June 2026; Airtel has issued more than 875,000 virtual cards in Uganda, Zambia and Tanzania since 2025.

2026-10-14-ben-wearetech-prix-simplifica.summary: Benin's government launched a national administrative simplification prize on 12 October, open to civil servants, citizens and businesses, for proposals to improve public services. Submissions run from 29 October to 12 November; selected ideas go to feasibility studies and possible trials, towards the target of all procedures online by 2030.

2026-10-14-bfa-sidwaya-passeports-biomet.summary: Burkina Faso's Security Ministry opened biometric passport enrolment at the regional police directorate in Ziniaré on 13 October, part of extending mobile enrolment kits to every region. Applicants no longer need to travel to Ouagadougou or Bobo-Dioulasso; the AES passport costs 50,000 FCFA and takes two weeks.

2026-10-14-bog-governor-asiama-africa-ai.summary: At the IMF African Caucus in Bangkok on 14 October, Bank of Ghana Governor Johnson Asiama asked the Fund to expand capacity support for African AI governance, supervisory technology and cybersecurity. He also asked it to include AI in its surveillance and Financial Sector Assessment Programs, and to help finance digital public infrastructure.

2026-10-14-cmr-businessincameroon-camtel.summary: CAMTEL and the state housing developer SIC signed a framework agreement in Yaoundé to connect SIC estates to fibre, starting with about 40 households out of more than 30,000 SIC clients. Subscriptions start at CFAF 15,000 a month with CFAF 25,000 installation, and new SIC buildings are to be prewired.

2026-10-14-dailytrust-inec-econec-ai-gui.summary: The ECOWAS Network of Electoral Commissions (ECONEC) has adopted guidelines on the use of AI in elections, validated at meetings on 12 and 13 October, its permanent secretary Serigne Mamadou Ka said during a visit to INEC in Abuja. The visit concerned implementing them across West African election bodies; the text has not been published.

2026-10-14-dci-rolls-out-biometric-clear.summary: Kenya's Directorate of Criminal Investigations extended its biometric police clearance certificate service to diplomats. The MBIS system behind it, launched on 23 July, linked 26 of 63 application centres by September; the DCI says processing has fallen from 14 days to same-day.

2026-10-14-egy-etdatacenters-telecom-egy.summary: Telecom Egypt chief executive Tamer El Mahdi set out the company's investment in subsea and terrestrial routes, including the 200km Sharm El Sheikh-Taba cable agreed in September and due in service late next year. He said the company has set up a separate entity for its data-centre business and that its transit capacity exceeds 330Tbps.

2026-10-14-egy-itweb-idsc-workshop-digit.summary: A workshop at the Cabinet's Information and Decision Support Centre recommended putting commercial registers and investor licensing on the Digital Egypt platform, wider use of national digital IDs and e-signatures, and backup connectivity for public networks running essential services. The recommendations were published by the State Information Service; no decision was announced.

2026-10-14-gab-ecofin-airtel-zte-massive.summary: Airtel Gabon and ZTE announced on 13 October the commercial deployment of FDD+TDD Massive MIMO on Airtel's 4G network in Gabon, presented as preparation for 5G. The regulator ARCEP discussed the conditions for 5G with Airtel Gabon and Moov Africa Gabon Télécom in December 2025.

2026-10-14-gab-wearetech-api-pnr-securip.summary: Gabon's transport minister Ulrich Manfoumbi Manfoumbi visited Securiport LLC's installation at Libreville's Léon-Mba airport on 12 October to speed up the start of an API-PNR passenger data system. The US firm holds a concession signed in May 2026 for Libreville, Port-Gentil and Mvengué airports, funded by a USD 30 levy per international passenger set in June.

2026-10-14-gha-myjoyonline-audit-2016-co.summary: Ghana's communications minister Samuel Nartey George said the government will commission an independent audit of 2,016 community network sites inherited under an existing contract, to establish which are complete and working. He made the statement after inspecting four solar-powered rural telephony sites in Sekyere Afram Plains District on 13 October, which he said should be upgraded from 3G to 4G.

2026-10-14-ghana-rwanda-nigeria-cross-bo.summary: Bank of Ghana Governor Johnson Asiama said on 13 October that the bank is testing cross-border payment interoperability with Rwanda and Nigeria across CBDCs, stablecoins, bank accounts and mobile wallets, with the aim of moving to live services on rails such as PAPSS. He said Ghana's mobile money transactions passed one billion in a month for the first time in August 2026, worth GH¢519 billion, and reported fraud cases rose 48% in 2025.

2026-10-14-govt-probes-mass-whatsapp-tak.summary: Zimbabwe's ICT minister Tatenda Mavetera said her ministry has opened a multi-agency investigation, including the police Cyber Crime Division, into a wave of WhatsApp Business account takeovers. It will examine whether personal or financial data was compromised and the role of SMS termination aggregators, and is engaging Meta and the affected mobile operator.

2026-10-14-ipris-african-telecom-regulat.summary: The iPRIS programme, run by SPIDER and Sweden's PTS, held its eighth cohort's African phase in Nairobi from 5 to 9 October with regulators from Liberia, Namibia, Mauritius, Sierra Leone, Tanzania and Zimbabwe. Each presented a planned regulatory change; Liberia's authority switched its project from 5G spectrum guidelines to licensing private networks.

2026-10-14-itweb-free-cyber-crime-victim.summary: MiDO Academy and the UK charity The Cyber Helpline, funded by Amazon Web Services, began a 12-month pilot of a free, 24-hour cyber crime victim helpline in South Africa for anyone aged 13 or over. Supervised MiDO students answer calls and refer victims to banks, the police and mental health services.

2026-10-14-lbr-liberianobserver-upgraded.summary: Liberia's Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection launched an upgraded Gender-Based Violence Information Management System with UNFPA support under the EU-backed Spotlight Initiative 2.0. It covers incident reporting, survivor case management and referrals; UNFPA handed over 40 tablets, a server and four laptops.

2026-10-14-mdg-techafricanews-metfp-oran.summary: Madagascar's Ministry of Technical Education and Vocational Training signed a partnership with Orange Madagascar on 8 October on digital-skills training and matching vocational courses to labour-market demand. No budget or targets were given.

2026-10-14-moz-jornalnoticias-centro-pro.summary: President Daniel Chapo opened Centro Pronto in Maputo on 14 October, a centre that issues identity cards, passports, DIRE residence documents, driving licences and residence permits in one place. It was launched at the Citizen Connect Africa conference.

2026-10-14-nga-guardian-afcfta-digital-t.summary: Nigeria is conducting a regulatory gap analysis with the World Bank Group to bring its pending digital economy bill and planned e-commerce policy into line with the AfCFTA Digital Trade Protocol. With Egypt and Kenya, it is one of three pilot countries for ADAPT, a digital-trade infrastructure initiative of the AfCFTA Secretariat and the Tony Blair Institute.

2026-10-14-nga-guardian-data-centre-capa.summary: The chairman of Nigeria's ruling party said industry and government aim to raise data-centre capacity from about 50 MW to 200 MW of IT load within five years. He said power and water supply will decide which facilities last, and that cloud sovereignty should not turn into protectionism.

2026-10-14-nga-techcabal-cascador-sterli.summary: Cascador and Sterling Bank announced the SME Credit Backstop, a planned USD 200 million first-loss fund to support up to USD 1 billion of bank loans to Nigerian start-ups and SMEs nominated by their investors. Underwriting is to use AI; the fund's capital has not yet been raised.

2026-10-14-nga-techcabal-nimc-identity-d.summary: Nigeria's identity agency NIMC said the national identity database is hosted wholly in Nigeria, not in the cloud, and run by its own staff. It said about 63 government agencies have integrated with the database and 142 million people held a NIN in September 2026.

2026-10-14-tan-ghana-gifec-rural-telepho.summary: After inspecting rural telephony sites on 13 October, Ghana's communications minister directed GIFEC to extend service to three more communities in Sekyere Afram Plains. The government is also working with MTN Ghana on 800 new sites at locations proposed by MPs.

2026-10-14-tan-tanzania-tcra-30-days-fix.summary: Tanzania's TCRA gave telecoms providers 30 days to correct faults found in inspections, among them unsafe cabling, damaged poles and unmarked infrastructure. Some providers must file full GIS maps of their networks, and new fibre installations now need the Authority's prior approval.

2026-10-14-tra-ghana-sam-george-2000-lap.summary: Ghana's communications minister gave 2,000 more laptops to KNUST, adding to 500 given earlier, and said the One Million Coders Programme will now target third- and final-year students instead of first-years. He visited the university's Responsible AI Lab, which drafted the National AI Strategy launched in April 2026.

2026-10-14-tra-kenya-odpc-hosts-sri-lank.summary: Kenya's Office of the Data Protection Commissioner is hosting Sri Lanka's Data Protection Authority for a three-day study visit led by Data Commissioner Immaculate Kassait. Sessions cover compliance, complaints, investigations and enforcement, and automation of the office's work.

2026-10-14-tra-senum-hosts-central-afric.summary: Sénégal Numérique (SENUM SA) hosted a delegation from the Central African Agency for Digital Development, accompanied by the World Bank, on a study mission. Topics included information-system governance, cybersecurity operations centres, the national backbone, digital identity and interoperability, with a visit to the Diamniadio data centre.

2026-10-14-tun-alchourouk-interoperabili.summary: Tunisia's Presidency of the Government said in a written answer to MP Fatma Mseddi that a platform for real-time, secured data exchange between public bodies is still being completed. It said the same of the national administrative-procedures platform, intended as a single point of access for procedures.

2026-10-14-tun-assabah-employment-minist.summary: Tunisia's Ministry of Employment and Vocational Training signed a five-year renewable framework agreement with Tunisie Telecom on 14 October. The operator is to connect employment offices and training centres to fibre, install AI labs in vocational-training centres and host a distance-training system in its national data centre.

2026-10-14-tza-mwananchi-eaco-posta-napa.summary: Deputy ICT minister Switbert Mkama opened the East African Communications Organisation's fifth annual postal and logistics meeting in Arusha on 14 October. He named Tanzania's national address system, NAPA, as a tool for parcel delivery and access to digital services, and called for regional cooperation on payments, logistics and technical standards.

2026-10-14-uga-nilepost-itms-auditors-de.summary: Uganda's parliamentary Physical Infrastructure Committee ordered two directors of the Office of the Auditor General detained after they said the digital number plate project (ITMS) has not been audited since it began in 2021. The Auditor General said the project was classed as security-related and is financed by the Russian firm Joint Stock Company Global Security; motorists pay over Shs750,000 a plate.

2026-10-14-undp-ghana-home-grown-ai-digi.summary: UNDP deputy resident representative Shaima Hussein urged Ghana to favour locally built AI solutions at the opening of a three-day Digital and AI Champions training for civil servants in Accra. The programme, run with the communications ministry and funded by Japan, aims to certify 50 officers and train 40 chief directors and 120 directors.

2026-10-14-vanguard-inec-chairman-ai-dem.summary: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan told a Yiaga Africa forum on AI and democracy in Abuja that the 2027 election will involve more than 103 million registered voters at 176,846 polling units. He said INEC has received additional BVAS devices, its nomination portal has processed more than 15,000 nominations from 22 parties, and voter registration is now online.

2026-10-14-vanguard-meta-removes-3-7m-ac.summary: Meta removed more than 3.7 million Facebook and Instagram accounts, Pages and Groups linked to West African scam networks, in an operation led by the UK National Crime Agency with the US DOJ and FBI. Nigerian police arrested nine people and seized 53 devices; Ghanaian police arrested 19 near Accra and identified 117 trafficking victims made to work in scam operations.

2026-10-15-african-startups-raise-2-49b-.summary: African startups raised $2.49 billion across 315 disclosed deals in the first nine months of 2026, up 7.8% on the same period of 2025 on fewer deals. The third quarter alone brought in $1.025 billion.

2026-10-15-africantechjournal-thompson-p.summary: A backend engineer argues that Africa's cross-border payment links are being built before the connected systems agree on how to establish whether a transaction has completed, leaving customers unable to learn where a payment is.

2026-10-15-ago-techreviewafrica-ggpen-ge.summary: Angola's national space programme office and the Portuguese company GEOSAT signed a letter of intent on 13 October to cooperate on Earth observation and satellite-data services under the ANGEO-1 programme, for uses ranging from land planning and agriculture to mining and water.

2026-10-15-ampath-downplays-data-breach-.summary: South African pathology group Ampath confirmed a cyber attack detected on 2 October that may have exposed patient ID numbers and medical-aid details. It disputes a threat actor's claim of 80 million stolen records, saying the figure counts database entries rather than people, and has notified the Information Regulator.

2026-10-15-caf-africabusinessinsight-dig.summary: The Central African Republic launched a national portal for online government services on 14 October, covering driving licences, criminal-record extracts, nationality and school certificates, and medical appointments. About 12% of the population used the internet at the end of 2025, which limits who can use it.

2026-10-15-can-africas-new-crvs-decade-c.summary: About one death in ten is registered in Africa, and the 2026-2036 Africa CRVS Decade agreed by civil registrars aims to close that gap by linking civil registration with health and identity systems, widening local registration and digitising records.

2026-10-15-cipesa-comments-uganda-digita.summary: CIPESA made a submission to the Ugandan Parliament's committee examining the digital number plate project, raising concerns about privacy, surveillance and data protection in the vehicle-tracking system behind it.

2026-10-15-com-alwatwan-etat-civil-amecc.summary: The second phase of Comoros's civil-registration modernisation project was reported 84% complete and given three more months at its steering committee, chaired by the interior minister with UNICEF and the French ambassador. Civil-registration centres have been mapped nationwide, the pre-digitisation study finished and new forms designed; France's support is put at EUR 1 million.

2026-10-15-dalberg-compute-costing-toolk.summary: Dalberg Data Insights released a beta toolkit, built with the Rwanda AI Scaling Hub and Gates Foundation support, that estimates what an AI deployment will cost to run as a range across shared, rented and owned inference. The authors argue that costing should start before a pilot ends.

2026-10-15-ethiopia-launches-seventh-nat.summary: Ethiopia's Information Network Security Administration opened the seventh National Cybersecurity Month, tying national cyber capacity to the Digital Ethiopia 2030 strategy. Its director general warned that attacks on critical infrastructure could trigger social, economic and political crises.

2026-10-15-ethiopia-s-new-technology-min.summary: Ethiopia's new Minister of Innovation and Technology, appointed on 8 October, told the six institutions under her ministry, among them the technology, communications and intellectual property authorities, to prepare assessments of their operational status, and announced visits to each.

2026-10-15-gha-myjoyonline-sam-george-ai.summary: Ghana's communications minister said the government has committed US$270 million to its AI plans, US$250 million of it for the first phase of a national AI compute centre and US$20 million for an AI fund, and targets about US$5 billion a year in economic gains. He said the ministry is building a data exchange hub to connect 48 government registries.

2026-10-15-ken-citizen-moh-denies-tamper.summary: Kenya's Ministry of Health denied switching off Murang'a County's AfyaKE electronic medical records system. The health cabinet secretary called the system a private arrangement between the county and its developers and said neither had sought certification from the Digital Health Agency; the county says it has run in 165 facilities since 2023.

2026-10-15-ken-mit-news-trust-government.summary: Research by the MIT Governance Lab and Busara on a Kenyan county services portal built with a telecoms company found that stressing the company's role made people more willing to use the portal but lowered their trust in government. The study appears in the September issue of Government Information Quarterly.

2026-10-15-ken-standard-kangata-afyake-s.summary: Murang'a's governor accused Kenya's national government of switching off the county's AfyaKE digital health system to force it onto another platform, leaving patient records from 2023 inaccessible and services scaled down. Claims the county had uploaded to the Social Health Authority are reported missing. See the health ministry's denial under the same heading.

2026-10-15-ken-techtrendske-dama-kenya-d.summary: A Kenya chapter of the Data Management Association launched in Nairobi, planning to train more than 10,000 data professionals over three years with a training partner. It reports more than 900 members and was welcomed by the data protection commissioner's office.

2026-10-15-local-insurers-go-solo-amid-a.summary: South African insurers are writing their own AI frameworks as they adopt the technology, because the country still has no national AI policy after the draft was withdrawn. The communications department still aims to finalise the policy in the 2026/27 financial year.

2026-10-15-nga-ebrd-power-distribution-d.summary: The EBRD agreed financing for Beacon Power Services to extend smart metering and grid-management technology across Nigeria's electricity distribution companies, aimed at cutting losses and improving revenue collection. The sum was not disclosed.

2026-10-15-nga-eu-ebrd-14m-fibre-backbon.summary: Nigeria, the European Union and the EBRD signed a EUR 14 million grant for the planned 90,000 km national fibre backbone, funded by the EU and managed by the bank. It pays for scoping, detailed network design, project preparation and capacity-building in the agencies implementing it.

2026-10-15-nga-inec-ai-safeguards-2027-e.summary: Nigeria's electoral commission has set up an artificial intelligence unit in its ICT directorate to watch for deepfakes and manipulated electoral information before the 2027 general elections. Its chairman said result collation, voter accreditation and candidate qualification will not be fully automated, and that 10 of 14 major milestones under the Electoral Act 2026 are complete.

2026-10-15-sen-us-health-agreement-perso.summary: Senegal's National Assembly is to examine the health memorandum signed with the United States on 13 March 2026, over the protection of personal data, under one of five parliamentary inquiries the prime minister announced. The US embassy says Senegal committed to co-invest US$27.3 million in health over five years under the agreement.

2026-10-15-shore-africa-ifc-proposes-35m.summary: The IFC disclosed a proposed sustainability-linked loan of up to $35 million to the wholesale operator WIOCC, for more subsea cable capacity, terrestrial fibre in Southern and West Africa and data-centre capacity. Board consideration is projected for 13 November 2026.

2026-10-15-south-africa-ai-policy-halluc.summary: One of the two South African officials suspended over the draft national AI policy that cited invented sources has resigned, and disciplinary proceedings continue against the other. The communications minister said cabinet will finalise a replacement before the end of March 2027, with public consultation expected from April.

2026-10-15-ssd-salc-oral-statement-cyber.summary: The Southern Africa Litigation Centre told the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights that the region's decade of striking down sedition, criminal defamation and false-news offences is being reversed, through routine surveillance, new cybercrime laws and prosecutions under them.

2026-10-15-ssd-ssra-zambian-delegation-d.summary: A Zambian finance ministry delegation visited the South Sudan Revenue Authority to study its e-Tax, e-Customs and SSCAFFA revenue platforms, which the commissioner general credits with raising monthly collections. The platforms' technical contractor says it does not collect, hold or control government funds.

2026-10-15-tcd-aspa-internet-cher-fractu.summary: A Chadian commentary written during the Central Africa Internet Governance Forum in N'Djamena argues that the cost of getting online, not the official talk of digital sovereignty and AI, decides who takes part in the digital economy.

2026-10-15-tza-guardian-vp-govt-digital-.summary: Tanzania's Vice President directed the youth and labour ministries to merge the YES youth-enrolment system, the Ajira Portal and the Kazi Portal into one interoperable network, after hearing that YES had registered over 22,000 young people but listed only seven opportunities. He asked for an integration report within a week.

2026-10-15-uga-ict-ministry-koica-digita.summary: Uganda's ICT ministry and the Korea International Cooperation Agency discussed widening their digital-transformation partnership to ICT skills, local innovation and technology in public services. No new agreement or sum was announced.

2026-10-15-uga-mediacentre-statement-afr.summary: Uganda's trade minister issued a statement ahead of a Kampala symposium on building Africa's digital single market, arguing that the country must help shape the rules for cross-border digital trade, payments and delivery. The symposium is set for 22-23 October 2026.

2026-10-15-zaf-lifestyleandtech-telkom-i.summary: Telkom announced a R20 million partnership with South Africa's Electoral Commission to provide connectivity and technical support for the 4 November 2026 local government elections, carried on Openserve's national fibre network.

2026-10-15-zwe-hanyani-data-protection-a.summary: Panellists at a media policy dialogue in Zimbabwe said the Cyber and Data Protection Act, passed to curb cybercrime and protect women and children online, is being used against journalists.

2026-10-15-zwe-herald-potraz-critical-in.summary: Zimbabwe's telecoms regulator is developing a Cybersecurity Framework for Critical Infrastructure Protection, its draft regulation cited as a governance example at a regulators' follow-up meeting in Nairobi. The regulator also restated that data controllers must be licensed under the Cyber and Data Protection Act.
